1.s:
vimalakalāśrayābhinavasṛṣṭimahā jananī bharitatanuśca pañcamukhaguptarucirjanakaḥ /
tadubhayayāmalasphuritabhāvavisargamayaṃ hṛdayamanuttarāmṛtakulaṃ mama sasphuratāt // 1
1.d:
विमलकलाश्रयाभिनवसृष्टिमहा जननी भरिततनुश्च पञ्चमुखगुप्तरुचिर्जनकः ।
तदुभययामलस्फुरितभावविसर्गमयं हृदयमनुत्तरामृतकुलं मम सस्फुरतात् ॥ 1
1.m: May my heart vibrate, [identical with] the unexcelled nectar-clan of the Kula, consisting in the creative emission of states of being vibrating from the dyad of those two: the mother, whose glory is the new creation resting upon pure arts, and the father, whose body is full and whose luster is guarded by five faces! // 1

1.s:
naumi citpratibhāṃ devīṃ parāṃ bhairavayoginīm /
mātṛmānaprameyāṃśaśūlāmbujakṛtāspadām // 2
1.d:
नौमि चित्प्रतिभां देवीं परां भैरवयोगिनीम् ।
मातृमानप्रमेयांशशूलाम्बुजकृतास्पदाम् ॥ 2
1.m: I praise the supreme goddess, the intuitive flash of consciousness, the Bhairava-yoginī, / who has taken Her abode on the lotus-trident formed of the portions of knower, means of knowledge, and object of knowledge. // 2

1.s:
naumi devīṃ śarīrasthāṃ nṛtyato bhairavākṛte /
prāvṛṇmeghaghanavyomavidyullekhāvilāsinīm // 3
1.d:
नौमि देवीं शरीरस्थां नृत्यतो भैरवाकृते ।
प्रावृण्मेघघनव्योमविद्युल्लेखाविलासिनीम् ॥ 3
1.m: I praise the goddess residing in the body of the dancing form of Bhairava, / sporting like a streak of lightning in a sky dense with monsoon clouds. // 3

1.s:
dīptajyotiśchaṭāpluṣṭabhedabandhatrayaṃ sphurat /
stājjñānaśūlaṃ satpakṣavipakṣotkartanakṣamam // 4
1.d:
दीप्तज्योतिश्छटाप्लुष्टभेदबन्धत्रयं स्फुरत् ।
स्ताज्ज्ञानशूलं सत्पक्षविपक्षोत्कर्तनक्षमम् ॥ 4
1.m: May the vibrating trident of knowledge appear, scorching the threefold bond of duality with a burst of blazing radiance, / capable of cutting down true arguments and counter-arguments! // 4

1.s:
svātantryaśaktiḥ kramasaṃsisṛkṣā kramātmatā ceti vibhorvibhūtiḥ /
tadeva devītrayamantarāstāmanuttaraṃ me prathayatsvarūpam // 5
1.d:
स्वातन्त्र्यशक्तिः क्रमसंसिसृक्षा क्रमात्मता चेति विभोर्विभूतिः ।
तदेव देवीत्रयमन्तरास्तामनुत्तरं मे प्रथयत्स्वरूपम् ॥ 5
1.m: The power of absolute autonomy, the desire to project succession, and the nature of succession itself: such is the omnipresent Lord's sovereignty. / May that very triad of goddesses manifest internally within me my unexcelled true nature! // 5

1.s:
taddevatāvibhavabhāvimahāmarīcicakreśvarāyitanijasthitireka eva /
devīsuto gaṇapatiḥ sphuradindukāntiḥ samyaksamucchalayatānmama saṃvidabdhim // 6
1.d:
तद्देवताविभवभाविमहामरीचिचक्रेश्वरायितनिजस्थितिरेक एव ।
देवीसुतो गणपतिः स्फुरदिन्दुकान्तिः सम्यक्समुच्छलयतान्मम संविदब्धिम् ॥ 6
1.m: May that son of the goddess, Gaṇapati alone, whose own presence acts as the Lord of the great wheel of rays originating from the glory of that deity, / gleaming with the luster of the moon, make my ocean of consciousness surge completely! // 6

1.s:
rāgāruṇāṃ granthibilāvakīrṇa yo jālamātānavitānavṛtti /
kalombhitaṃ bāhyapathe cakāra stānme sa macchandavibhuḥ prasannaḥ // 7
1.d:
रागारुणां ग्रन्थिबिलावकीर्ण यो जालमातानवितानवृत्ति ।
कलोम्भितं बाह्यपथे चकार स्तान्मे स मच्छन्दविभुः प्रसन्नः ॥ 7
1.m: May that Lord Macchanda be gracious to me, he who unfolded along the external path the net [of doctrine] / that is reddened with passion, scattered with apertures of knots, extending wide in function, and strung with arts! // 7

1.s:
traiyambakābhihitasantatitāmraparṇīsanmauktikaprakarakāntiviśeṣabhājaḥ /
pūrve jayanti guravo guruśāstrasindhukallolakelikalanāmalakarṇadhārāḥ // 8
1.d:
त्रैयम्बकाभिहितसन्ततिताम्रपर्णीसन्मौक्तिकप्रकरकान्तिविशेषभाजः ।
पूर्वे जयन्ति गुरवो गुरुशास्त्रसिन्धुकल्लोलकेलिकलनामलकर्णधाराः ॥ 8
1.m: Victorious are the ancient gurus belonging to the lineage revealed by Traiyambaka, who partake of the special luster of a heap of excellent pearls from the Tāmraparṇī river, / spotless helmsmen in steering the sport of the billowing waves of the ocean of weighty scriptures! // 8

1.s:
jayati gurureka eva śrīśrīkaṇṭho bhuvi prathitaḥ /
tadaparamūrtirbhagavān maheśvaro bhūtirājaśca // 9
1.d:
जयति गुरुरेक एव श्रीश्रीकण्ठो भुवि प्रथितः ।
तदपरमूर्तिर्भगवान् महेश्वरो भूतिराजश्च ॥ 9
1.m: Victorious is the guru alone, venerable Śrīkaṇṭha, famed on earth, / and his other manifestation, the blessed Maheśvara, Bhūtirāja. // 9

1.s:
śrīsomānandabodhaśrīmadutpalaviniḥsṛtāḥ /
jayanti saṃvidāmodasandarbhā dikprasarpiṇaḥ // 10
1.d:
श्रीसोमानन्दबोधश्रीमदुत्पलविनिःसृताः ।
जयन्ति संविदामोदसन्दर्भा दिक्प्रसर्पिणः ॥ 10
1.m: Victorious are the compositions fragrant with consciousness, spreading in all directions, / that flowed forth from the glorious Utpaladeva through the awakening of the venerable Somānanda! // 10

1.s:
tadāsvādabharāveśabṛṃhitāṃ matiṣaṭpadīm /
gurorlakṣmaṇaguptasya nādasaṃmohinīṃ numaḥ // 11
1.d:
तदास्वादभरावेशबृंहितां मतिषट्पदीम् ।
गुरोर्लक्ष्मणगुप्तस्य नादसंमोहिनीं नुमः ॥ 11
1.m: We praise the bee of the intellect of the guru Lakṣmaṇagupta, invigorated by the full absorption of tasting that [nectar], / captivating through sound. // 11

1.s:
yaḥ pūrṇānandaviśrāntasarvaśāstrārthapāragaḥ /
sa śrīcukhulako diśyādiṣṭaṃ me gururuttamaḥ // 12
1.d:
यः पूर्णानन्दविश्रान्तसर्वशास्त्रार्थपारगः ।
स श्रीचुखुलको दिश्यादिष्टं मे गुरुरुत्तमः ॥ 12
1.m: May that venerable Cukhulaka, the supreme guru, grant my desire, / he who has crossed to the further shore of all scriptural teachings, resting in full bliss! // 12

1.s:
jayatājjagaduddhṛtikṣamo'sau bhagavatyā saha śaṃbhunātha ekaḥ /
yadudīritaśāsanāṃśubhirme prakaṭo'yaṃ gahano'pi śāstramārgaḥ // 13
1.d:
जयताज्जगदुद्धृतिक्षमोऽसौ भगवत्या सह शंभुनाथ एकः ।
यदुदीरितशासनांशुभिर्मे प्रकटोऽयं गहनोऽपि शास्त्रमार्गः ॥ 13
1.m: Victorious be that unique Śambhunātha together with the Goddess, who is capable of uplifting the world, / through the rays of whose uttered instruction this path of scripture, deep though it is, has become clear to me! // 13

1.s:
santi paddhatayaścitrāḥ srotobhedeṣu bhūyasā /
anuttaraṣaḍardhārthakrame tvekāpi nekṣyate // 14
1.d:
सन्ति पद्धतयश्चित्राः स्रोतोभेदेषु भूयसा ।
अनुत्तरषडर्धार्थक्रमे त्वेकापि नेक्ष्यते ॥ 14
1.m: There are many diverse manuals for the different streams [of revelation], / but not even one is seen for the process of the meaning of the unexcelled Trika. // 14

1.s:
ityahaṃ bahuśaḥ sadbhiḥ śiṣyasabrahmacāribhiḥ /
arthito racaye spaṣṭāṃ pūrṇārthā prakriyāmimām // 15
1.d:
इत्यहं बहुशः सद्भिः शिष्यसब्रह्मचारिभिः ।
अर्थितो रचये स्पष्टां पूर्णार्था प्रक्रियामिमाम् ॥ 15
1.m: Thus repeatedly requested by good disciples and fellow students, / I compose this clear system, complete in meaning. // 15

1.s:
śrībhaṭṭanāthacaraṇābjayugāttathā śrībhaṭṭārikāṃghriyugalādgurusantatiryā /
bodhānyapāśaviṣanuttadupāsanotthabodhojjvalo'bhinavagupta idaṃ karoti // 16
1.d:
श्रीभट्टनाथचरणाब्जयुगात्तथा श्रीभट्टारिकांघ्रियुगलाद्गुरुसन्ततिर्या ।
बोधान्यपाशविषनुत्तदुपासनोत्थबोधोज्ज्वलोऽभिनवगुप्त इदं करोति ॥ 16
1.m: Abhinavagupta, illuminated by the awakening arising from worshiping the lineage of gurus that stems from the lotus feet of the venerable Bhaṭṭanātha and the feet of the venerable Bhaṭṭārikā, / dispelling the poison of bonds other than awakening, composes this [work]. // 16

1.s:
na tadastīha yanna śrī-mālinīvijayottare /
devadevena nirdiṣṭaṃ svaśabdenātha liṅgataḥ // 17
1.d:
न तदस्तीह यन्न श्री-मालिनीविजयोत्तरे ।
देवदेवेन निर्दिष्टं स्वशब्देनाथ लिङ्गतः ॥ 17
1.m: There is nothing here that was not taught in the venerable Mālinīvijayottara / by the God of gods, either in His own words or by implication. // 17

1.s:
daśāṣṭādaśavasvaṣṭabhinnaṃ yacchāsanaṃ vibhoḥ /
tatsāraṃ trikaśāstraṃ hi tatsāraṃ mālinīmatam // 18
1.d:
दशाष्टादशवस्वष्टभिन्नं यच्छासनं विभोः ।
तत्सारं त्रिकशास्त्रं हि तत्सारं मालिनीमतम् ॥ 18
1.m: The teaching of the Lord, divided into ten, eighteen, and sixty-four [tantras], / has the Trika scripture as its essence; and the essence of that is the doctrine of the Mālinī. // 18

1.s:
ato'trāntargataṃ sarva saṃpradāyojjhitairbudhaiḥ /
adṛṣṭa prakaṭīkurmo gurunāthājñayā vayam // 19
1.d:
अतोऽत्रान्तर्गतं सर्व संप्रदायोज्झितैर्बुधैः ।
अदृष्ट प्रकटीकुर्मो गुरुनाथाज्ञया वयम् ॥ 19
1.m: Therefore, by the command of the lord of gurus, we make manifest everything contained herein / that was unseen by scholars devoid of lineage tradition. // 19

1.s:
abhinavaguptasya kṛtiḥ seyaṃ yasyoditā gurubhirākhyā /
trinayanacaraṇasaroruhacintanalabdhaprasiddhiriti // 20
1.d:
अभिनवगुप्तस्य कृतिः सेयं यस्योदिता गुरुभिराख्या ।
त्रिनयनचरणसरोरुहचिन्तनलब्धप्रसिद्धिरिति ॥ 20
1.m: This is the work of Abhinavagupta, whose name was uttered by the gurus / as 'the one who has attained renown through meditating on the lotus feet of the Three-Eyed Lord.' // 20

1.s:
śrīśambhunāthabhāskaracaraṇanipātaprabhāpagatasaṃkocam /
abhinavaguptahṛdambujametadvicinuta maheśapūjanahetoḥ // 21
ādivākyaṃ
1.d:
श्रीशम्भुनाथभास्करचरणनिपातप्रभापगतसंकोचम् ।
अभिनवगुप्तहृदम्बुजमेतद्विचिनुत महेशपूजनहेतोः ॥ 21
आदिवाक्यं
1.m:
Examine this lotus-heart of Abhinavagupta, whose contraction has vanished through the radiance of the falling rays of the sun that is the venerable Śambhunātha, / for the purpose of worshiping Maheśvara! // 21
Initial Statement

1.s:
iha tāvatsamasteṣu śāstreṣu parigīyate /
ajñānaṃ saṃsṛterheturjñānaṃ mokṣaikakāraṇam // 22
1.d:
इह तावत्समस्तेषु शास्त्रेषु परिगीयते ।
अज्ञानं संसृतेर्हेतुर्ज्ञानं मोक्षैककारणम् ॥ 22
1.m: Here, indeed, in all scriptures it is proclaimed / that ignorance is the cause of cyclic existence, and knowledge is the sole cause of liberation. // 22

1.s:
malamajñānamicchanti saṃsārāṅkurakāraṇam /
iti proktaṃ tathā ca śrīmālinīvijayottare // 23
1.d:
मलमज्ञानमिच्छन्ति संसाराङ्कुरकारणम् ।
इति प्रोक्तं तथा च श्रीमालिनीविजयोत्तरे ॥ 23
1.m: They maintain that impurity is ignorance, the cause of the sprout of transmigratory existence; / so it has also been stated in the venerable Mālinīvijayottara. // 23

1.s:
viśeṣaṇena buddhisthe saṃsārottarakālike /
saṃbhāvanāṃ nirasyaitadabhāve mokṣamabravīt // 24
1.d:
विशेषणेन बुद्धिस्थे संसारोत्तरकालिके ।
संभावनां निरस्यैतदभावे मोक्षमब्रवीत् ॥ 24
1.m: By qualifying [ignorance], [the scripture] refuted the assumption that it resides in the intellect at a time subsequent to cyclic existence, / and declared liberation to consist in its absence. // 24

1.s:
ajñānamiti na jñānābhāvaścātiprasaṅgataḥ /
sa hi loṣṭādike'pyasti na ca tasyāsti saṃsṛtiḥ // 25
1.d:
अज्ञानमिति न ज्ञानाभावश्चातिप्रसङ्गतः ।
स हि लोष्टादिकेऽप्यस्ति न च तस्यास्ति संसृतिः ॥ 25
1.m: Ignorance is not the mere absence of knowledge, for that leads to unwarranted extension; / indeed, that [absence] exists even in a clod of earth and the like, yet it has no cyclic existence. // 25

1.s:
ato jñeyasya tattvasya sāmastyenāprathātmakam /
jñānameva tadajñānaṃ śivasūtreṣu bhāṣitam // 26
1.d:
अतो ज्ञेयस्य तत्त्वस्य सामस्त्येनाप्रथात्मकम् ।
ज्ञानमेव तदज्ञानं शिवसूत्रेषु भाषितम् ॥ 26
1.m: Therefore, that ignorance has been declared in the Śivasūtras to be knowledge itself / whose nature is the non-manifestation of the knowable reality in its entirety. // 26

1.s:
caitanyamātmā jñānaṃ ca bandha ityatra sūtrayoḥ /
saṃśleṣetarayogāśyāmayamarthaḥ pradarśitaḥ // 27
1.d:
चैतन्यमात्मा ज्ञानं च बन्ध इत्यत्र सूत्रयोः ।
संश्लेषेतरयोगाश्यामयमर्थः प्रदर्शितः ॥ 27
1.m: In the two sūtras, 'Consciousness is the self' and 'Knowledge is bondage,' / this meaning has been shown by the union and disjunction [of the terms]. // 27

1.s:
caitanyamiti bhāvāntaḥ śabdaḥ svātantryamātrakam /
anākṣipraviśeṣaṃ sadāha sūtre purātane // 28
1.d:
चैतन्यमिति भावान्तः शब्दः स्वातन्त्र्यमात्रकम् ।
अनाक्षिप्रविशेषं सदाह सूत्रे पुरातने ॥ 28
1.m: The word 'consciousness' ending in an abstract suffix denotes mere absolute autonomy; / not implying any particularity, it was spoken in the first sūtra. // 28

1.s:
dvitīyena tu sūtreṇa kriyāṃ vā karaṇaṃ ca vā /
bruvatā tasya cinmātrarūpasya dvaitamucyate // 29
1.d:
द्वितीयेन तु सूत्रेण क्रियां वा करणं च वा ।
ब्रुवता तस्य चिन्मात्ररूपस्य द्वैतमुच्यते ॥ 29
1.m: By the second sūtra, however, expressing an action or an instrument, / duality is predicated of that which is of the nature of pure consciousness alone. // 29

1.s:
dvaitaprathā tadajñānaṃ tucchatvādbandha ucyate /
tata eva samucchedyamityāvṛttyānirūpitam // 30
1.d:
द्वैतप्रथा तदज्ञानं तुच्छत्वाद्बन्ध उच्यते ।
तत एव समुच्छेद्यमित्यावृत्त्यानिरूपितम् ॥ 30
1.m: The manifestation of duality is that ignorance; because of its unsubstantiality, it is called bondage. / For that very reason, it must be eradicated; this is determined through repetition. // 30

1.s:
svatantrātmātiriktastu tuccho' tuccho'pi kaścana /
na mokṣo nāma tannāsya pṛthaṅnāmāpi gṛhyate // 31
1.d:
स्वतन्त्रात्मातिरिक्तस्तु तुच्छो' तुच्छोऽपि कश्चन ।
न मोक्षो नाम तन्नास्य पृथङ्नामापि गृह्यते ॥ 31
1.m: Other than the autonomous self, there is nothing substantial or insubstantial / named liberation; therefore, it does not even receive a separate name. // 31

1.s:
yattu jñeyasatattvasya pūrṇapūrṇaprathātmakam /
taduttarottaraṃ jñānaṃ tattatsaṃsāraśāntidam // 32
1.d:
यत्तु ज्ञेयसतत्त्वस्य पूर्णपूर्णप्रथात्मकम् ।
तदुत्तरोत्तरं ज्ञानं तत्तत्संसारशान्तिदम् ॥ 32
1.m: That knowledge, however, which consists in the increasingly complete manifestation of the reality to be known, / progressively brings about the pacification of that particular transmigratory existence. // 32

1.s:
rāgādyakaluṣo'smyantaḥśūnyo'haṃ kartṛtojjhitaḥ /
itthaṃ samāsavyāsābhyāṃ jñānaṃ muñcati tāvataḥ // 33
1.d:
रागाद्यकलुषोऽस्म्यन्तःशून्योऽहं कर्तृतोज्झितः ।
इत्थं समासव्यासाभ्यां ज्ञानं मुञ्चति तावतः ॥ 33
1.m: 'I am unstained by attachment and the like; I am internally void; I am devoid of agency': / in this way, knowledge releases to that extent, through summary and detail. // 33

1.s:
tasmānmukto'pyavacchedādavacchedāntarasthiteḥ /
amukta eva muktastu sarvāvacchedavarjitaḥ // 34
1.d:
तस्मान्मुक्तोऽप्यवच्छेदादवच्छेदान्तरस्थितेः ।
अमुक्त एव मुक्तस्तु सर्वावच्छेदवर्जितः ॥ 34
1.m: Therefore, one who is released from one limitation still remains within another limitation / and is indeed unliberated; but the liberated one is free from all limitations. // 34

1.s:
yattu jñeyasatattvasya jñānaṃ sarvātmanojjhitam /
avacchedairna tatkutrāpyajñānaṃ satyamuktidam // 35
1.d:
यत्तु ज्ञेयसतत्त्वस्य ज्ञानं सर्वात्मनोज्झितम् ।
अवच्छेदैर्न तत्कुत्राप्यज्ञानं सत्यमुक्तिदम् ॥ 35
1.m: That knowledge of the reality to be known, however, which is entirely free / from limitations, is nowhere ignorance; it bestows true liberation. // 35

1.s:
jñānājñānasvarūpaṃ yaduktaṃ pratyekamapyadaḥ /
dvidhā pauruṣabauddhatvabhidoktaṃ śivaśāsane // 36
1.d:
ज्ञानाज्ञानस्वरूपं यदुक्तं प्रत्येकमप्यदः ।
द्विधा पौरुषबौद्धत्वभिदोक्तं शिवशासने ॥ 36
1.m: The nature of knowledge and ignorance that has been described is each / declared to be twofold in the teaching of Śiva, divided into existential and intellectual. // 36

1.s:
tatra puṃso yadajñānaṃ malākhyaṃ tajjamapyaya /
svapūrṇacitkriyārūpaśivatāvaraṇātmakam // 37
1.d:
तत्र पुंसो यदज्ञानं मलाख्यं तज्जमप्यय ।
स्वपूर्णचित्क्रियारूपशिवतावरणात्मकम् ॥ 37
1.m: Therein, the ignorance of the person called impurity, and what is born from it, / consists in the covering of one's own Śivahood, whose form is full consciousness and action. // 37

1.s:
saṃkocidṛkkriyārūpaṃ tatpaśoravikalpitam /
tadajñānaṃ na budghyaṃśo'dhyavasāyādyabhāvataḥ // 38
1.d:
संकोचिदृक्क्रियारूपं तत्पशोरविकल्पितम् ।
तदज्ञानं न बुद्घ्यंशोऽध्यवसायाद्यभावतः ॥ 38
1.m: It takes the form of contracted vision and action; it is non-conceptual in the bound soul. / That ignorance is not part of the intellect, because of the absence of determination and the like. // 38

1.s:
ahamitthamidaṃ vedmītyevamadhyavasāyinī /
ṣaṭkañcukābilāṇūtthapratibimbanato yadā // 39
1.d:
अहमित्थमिदं वेद्मीत्येवमध्यवसायिनी ।
षट्कञ्चुकाबिलाणूत्थप्रतिबिम्बनतो यदा ॥ 39
1.m: When, through the reflection arising from the subtle soul within the cavity of the six cuirasses, / an intellect is produced that determines thus: 'I know this in such a manner,' // 39

1.s:
dhīrjāyate tadā tādṛgjñānamajñānaśabditam /
bauddhaṃ tasya ca tatpauṃsnaṃ poṣaṇīyaṃ ca poṣṭṛca // 40
1.d:
धीर्जायते तदा तादृग्ज्ञानमज्ञानशब्दितम् ।
बौद्धं तस्य च तत्पौंस्नं पोषणीयं च पोष्टृच ॥ 40
1.m: then such knowledge is termed intellectual ignorance; / and that existential [ignorance] of his is both to be nourished and the nourisher. // 40

1.s:
kṣīṇe tu paśusaṃskāre puṃsaḥ prāptaparasthiteḥ /
vikasvaraṃ tadvijñānaṃ pauruṣaṃ nirvikalpakam // 41
1.d:
क्षीणे तु पशुसंस्कारे पुंसः प्राप्तपरस्थितेः ।
विकस्वरं तद्विज्ञानं पौरुषं निर्विकल्पकम् ॥ 41
1.m: When, however, the latent impression of the bound soul is attenuated in a person who has attained the supreme state, / that expanding existential knowledge is non-conceptual. // 41

1.s:
vikasvarāvikalpātmajñānaucityena yāvasā /
tadbauddhaṃ yasya tatpauṃsnaṃ prāgvatpoṣyaṃ ca poṣṭṛ ca // 42
1.d:
विकस्वराविकल्पात्मज्ञानौचित्येन यावसा ।
तद्बौद्धं यस्य तत्पौंस्नं प्राग्वत्पोष्यं च पोष्टृ च ॥ 42
1.m: Whatever determination corresponds to the expanding, non-conceptual knowledge / is intellectual [knowledge]; for him, that existential [knowledge] is, as before, both what is to be nourished and the nourisher. // 42

1.s:
tatra dīkṣādinā pauṃsnamajñānaṃ dhvaṃsi yadyapi /
tathāpi taccharīrānte tajjñānaṃ vyajyate sphuṭam // 43
1.d:
तत्र दीक्षादिना पौंस्नमज्ञानं ध्वंसि यद्यपि ।
तथापि तच्छरीरान्ते तज्ज्ञानं व्यज्यते स्फुटम् ॥ 43
1.m: In that context, although existential ignorance is destroyed through initiation and the like, / nevertheless, that knowledge is manifested clearly only at the end of the body.

1.s:
bauddhajñānena tu yadā bauddhamajñānajṛmbhitam /
vilīyate tadā jīvanmuktiḥ karatale sthitā // 44
1.d:
बौद्धज्ञानेन तु यदा बौद्धमज्ञानजृम्भितम् ।
विलीयते तदा जीवन्मुक्तिः करतले स्थिता ॥ 44
1.m: However, when the expansion of intellectual ignorance dissolves through intellectual knowledge, / then liberation in life is held in the palm of one's hand.

1.s:
dīkṣāpi bauddhavijñānapūrvā satyaṃ vimocikā /
tena tatrāpi bauddhasya jñānasyāsti pradhānatā // 45
1.d:
दीक्षापि बौद्धविज्ञानपूर्वा सत्यं विमोचिका ।
तेन तत्रापि बौद्धस्य ज्ञानस्यास्ति प्रधानता ॥ 45
1.m: Initiation, too, truly liberates when preceded by intellectual knowledge; / therefore, there as well, intellectual knowledge is preeminent.

1.s:
jñānājñānāgataṃ caitaddvitvaṃ svāyambhuve rurau /
mataṅgādau kṛtaṃ śrīmatkheṭapālādidaiśikaiḥ // 46
1.d:
ज्ञानाज्ञानागतं चैतद्द्वित्वं स्वायम्भुवे रुरौ ।
मतङ्गादौ कृतं श्रीमत्खेटपालादिदैशिकैः ॥ 46
1.m: And this duality pertaining to knowledge and ignorance in the Svāyambhuva, Ruru, / Mataṅga, and other [tantras] has been elucidated by venerable teachers such as Kheṭapāla.

1.s:
tathāvidhāvasāyātmabauddhavijñānasampade /
śāstrameva pradhānaṃ yajjñeyatattvapradarśakam // 47
1.d:
तथाविधावसायात्मबौद्धविज्ञानसम्पदे ।
शास्त्रमेव प्रधानं यज्ज्ञेयतत्त्वप्रदर्शकम् ॥ 47
1.m: For the attainment of intellectual knowledge consisting of that kind of certitude, / the scripture alone is preeminent, which reveals the reality to be known.

1.s:
dīkṣayā galite'pyantarajñāne pauruṣātmani /
dhīgatasyānivṛttatvādvikalpo'pi hi saṃbhaveta // 48
1.d:
दीक्षया गलितेऽप्यन्तरज्ञाने पौरुषात्मनि ।
धीगतस्यानिवृत्तत्वाद्विकल्पोऽपि हि संभवेत ॥ 48
1.m: Even when inner ignorance in the form of existential [ignorance] has melted away through initiation, / conceptual constructs can still occur, because that which resides in the intellect has not ceased.

1.s:
dehasadbhāvaparyantamātmabhāvo yato dhiyi /
dehānte'pi na mokṣaḥ syātpauruṣājñānahānitaḥ // 49
1.d:
देहसद्भावपर्यन्तमात्मभावो यतो धियि ।
देहान्तेऽपि न मोक्षः स्यात्पौरुषाज्ञानहानितः ॥ 49
1.m: Since the identification with the self remains in the intellect as long as the body exists, / liberation would not occur through the destruction of existential ignorance alone, even at the end of the body.

1.s:
bauddhājñānanivṛttau tu vikalponmūlanāddhruvam /
tadaiva mokṣa ityuktaṃ dhātrā śrīmanniśāṭane // 50
1.d:
बौद्धाज्ञाननिवृत्तौ तु विकल्पोन्मूलनाद्ध्रुवम् ।
तदैव मोक्ष इत्युक्तं धात्रा श्रीमन्निशाटने ॥ 50
1.m: On the cessation of intellectual ignorance, however, because conceptual constructs are uprooted, / liberation occurs at that very moment, as stated by the Creator in the illustrious Niśāṭana:

1.s:
vikalpayuktacitastu piṇḍapātācchivaṃ brajet /
itarastu tadaiveti śāstrasyātra pradhānataḥ // 51
1.d:
विकल्पयुक्तचितस्तु पिण्डपाताच्छिवं ब्रजेत् ।
इतरस्तु तदैवेति शास्त्रस्यात्र प्रधानतः ॥ 51
1.m: "One whose mind is joined with conceptual constructs goes to Śiva only upon the falling of the body, / but another [goes] at that very moment"—hence the preeminence of scripture here.

1.s:
jñeyasya hi paraṃ tattvaṃ yaḥ prakāśātmakaḥ śivaḥ /
nahyaprakāśarūpasya prākāśyaṃ vastutāpi vā // 52
1.d:
ज्ञेयस्य हि परं तत्त्वं यः प्रकाशात्मकः शिवः ।
नह्यप्रकाशरूपस्य प्राकाश्यं वस्तुतापि वा ॥ 52
1.m: For the supreme reality of what is to be known is Śiva, who is of the nature of luminosity; / for what is non-luminous has neither manifestation nor even reality.

1.s:
avastutāpi bhāvānāṃ camatkāraikagocarā /
yatkuḍyasadṛśī neyaṃ dhīravastvetadityapi // 53
1.d:
अवस्तुतापि भावानां चमत्कारैकगोचरा ।
यत्कुड्यसदृशी नेयं धीरवस्त्वेतदित्यपि ॥ 53
1.m: Even the unreality of things falls solely within the domain of wonder; / because this thought—"this is an unreal object"—is not like an insentient wall.

1.s:
prakāśo nāma yaścāyaṃ sarvatraiva prakāśate /
anapahnavanīyatvāt kiṃ tasminmānakalpanaiḥ // 54
1.d:
प्रकाशो नाम यश्चायं सर्वत्रैव प्रकाशते ।
अनपह्नवनीयत्वात् किं तस्मिन्मानकल्पनैः ॥ 54
1.m: And this which is called luminosity shines everywhere; / because it cannot be denied, what is the use of conceiving means of knowledge regarding it?

1.s:
pramāṇānyapi vastūnāṃ jīvitaṃ yāni tanvate /
teṣāmapi paro jīvaḥ sa eva parameśvaraḥ // 55
1.d:
प्रमाणान्यपि वस्तूनां जीवितं यानि तन्वते ।
तेषामपि परो जीवः स एव परमेश्वरः ॥ 55
1.m: Even the means of knowledge, which bestow life upon things— / their supreme life is that very Supreme Lord.

1.s:
sarvāpahnavahevākadharmāpyevaṃ hi vartate /
jñānamātmārthamityetanneti māṃ prati bhāsate // 56
1.d:
सर्वापह्नवहेवाकधर्माप्येवं हि वर्तते ।
ज्ञानमात्मार्थमित्येतन्नेति मां प्रति भासते ॥ 56
1.m: For even one whose nature is the obsession with total denial operates thus: / "Knowledge is for oneself—it appears to me that this is not so."

1.s:
apahnutau sādhane vā vastūnāmādyamīdṛśam /
yattatra ke pramāṇānāmupapattyupayogite // 57
1.d:
अपह्नुतौ साधने वा वस्तूनामाद्यमीदृशम् ।
यत्तत्र के प्रमाणानामुपपत्त्युपयोगिते ॥ 57
1.m: In denial or in proof, such is the primary basis of things; / since it is thus, what is the utility or efficacy of means of knowledge there?

1.s:
kāmike tata evoktaṃ hetuvādavivarjitam /
tasya devātidevasya parāpekṣā na vidyate // 59
1.d:
कामिके तत एवोक्तं हेतुवादविवर्जितम् ।
तस्य देवातिदेवस्य परापेक्षा न विद्यते ॥ 59
1.m: Therefore it is stated in the Kāmika, free from speculative argument: / "That God of gods has no dependence on anything else;

1.s:
parasya tadapekṣatvātsvatantro'yamataḥ sthitaḥ /
anapekṣasya vaśino deśakālākṛtikramāḥ // 60
1.d:
परस्य तदपेक्षत्वात्स्वतन्त्रोऽयमतः स्थितः ।
अनपेक्षस्य वशिनो देशकालाकृतिक्रमाः ॥ 60
1.m: because another depends on Him, He stands as autonomous." / Therefore, for Him who is independent and sovereign, successions of space, time, and form

1.s:
niyatā neti sa vibhurnityo viśvākṛtiḥ śivaḥ /
vibhutvātsarvago nityabhāvādādyantavarjitaḥ // 61
1.d:
नियता नेति स विभुर्नित्यो विश्वाकृतिः शिवः ।
विभुत्वात्सर्वगो नित्यभावादाद्यन्तवर्जितः ॥ 61
1.m: are not restricted. Thus He is all-pervading, eternal, manifesting all forms, Śiva; / by being all-pervading He is omnipresent; by being eternal He is devoid of beginning and end;

1.s:
viśvākṛtitvāccidacittadvaicitryāvabhāsakaḥ /
tato'sya bahurūpatvamuktaṃ dīkṣottarādike // 62
1.d:
विश्वाकृतित्वाच्चिदचित्तद्वैचित्र्यावभासकः ।
ततोऽस्य बहुरूपत्वमुक्तं दीक्षोत्तरादिके ॥ 62
1.m: and by having all forms He illuminates the diversity of sentient and insentient. / Therefore, His multiform nature is stated in the Dīkṣottara and other [works]:

1.s:
bhuvanaṃ vigraho jyotiḥ khaṃ śabdo mantra eva ca /
bindunādādisaṃbhinnaḥ ṣaḍvidhaḥ śiva ucyate // 63
1.d:
भुवनं विग्रहो ज्योतिः खं शब्दो मन्त्र एव च ।
बिन्दुनादादिसंभिन्नः षड्विधः शिव उच्यते ॥ 63
1.m: "The world, the body, light, ether, sound, and mantra— / differentiated by the point, resonance, and so forth, Śiva is said to be sixfold.

1.s:
yo yadātmakatāniṣṭhastadbhāvaṃ sa prapadyate /
vyomādiśabdavijñānātparo mokṣo na saṃśayaḥ // 64
1.d:
यो यदात्मकतानिष्ठस्तद्भावं स प्रपद्यते ।
व्योमादिशब्दविज्ञानात्परो मोक्षो न संशयः ॥ 64
1.m: He who is devoted to identity with whatever [form] attains that state; / through the knowledge of sound, ether, and the rest, supreme liberation [is attained], without doubt."

1.s:
viśvākṛtitve devasya tadetaccopalakṣaṇam /
anavacchinnatārūḍhāvavacchedalaye'sya ca // 65
1.d:
विश्वाकृतित्वे देवस्य तदेतच्चोपलक्षणम् ।
अनवच्छिन्नतारूढाववच्छेदलयेऽस्य च ॥ 65
1.m: And this is an indicative sign of the God having all forms: / when unconditionedness is ascended, and His limitation dissolves.

1.s:
uktaṃ ca kāmike devaḥ sarvākṛtirnirākṛtiḥ /
jaladarpaṇavattena sarvaṃ vyāptaṃ carācaram // 66
1.d:
उक्तं च कामिके देवः सर्वाकृतिर्निराकृतिः ।
जलदर्पणवत्तेन सर्वं व्याप्तं चराचरम् ॥ 66
1.m: And it is said in the Kāmika: "The God has all forms and is formless; / like a water mirror, by Him is all that moves and is motionless pervaded."

1.s:
na cāsya vimutādyo'yaṃ dharmo'nyonyaṃ vibhidyate /
eka evāsya dharmo'sau sarvākṣepeṇa vartate // 67
1.d:
न चास्य विमुताद्योऽयं धर्मोऽन्योन्यं विभिद्यते ।
एक एवास्य धर्मोऽसौ सर्वाक्षेपेण वर्तते ॥ 67
1.m: Nor do these attributes of His, such as all-pervasiveness, differ from one another; / this attribute of His is one alone, operating by encompassing everything.

1.s:
tena svātantryaśaktyaiva yukta ityāñjaso vidhiḥ /
bahuśaktitvamapyasya tacchaktyaivāviyuktatā // 68
1.d:
तेन स्वातन्त्र्यशक्त्यैव युक्त इत्याञ्जसो विधिः ।
बहुशक्तित्वमप्यस्य तच्छक्त्यैवावियुक्तता ॥ 68
1.m: Therefore, the direct teaching is that He is endowed with the power of absolute autonomy alone; / His having many powers is also non-separation from that power alone.

1.s:
śaktiśca nāma bhāvasya svaṃ rūpaṃ mātṛkalpitam /
tenādvayaḥ sa evāpi śaktimatparikalpane // 69
1.d:
शक्तिश्च नाम भावस्य स्वं रूपं मातृकल्पितम् ।
तेनाद्वयः स एवापि शक्तिमत्परिकल्पने ॥ 69
1.m: And 'power' means the essential form of a thing imagined by the cogniser; / therefore, even in the conceptualization of the possessor of power, He remains non-dual.

1.s:
mātṛklṛpte hi devasya tatra tatra vapuṣyalam /
ko bhedo vastuto vahnerdagdhṛpaktṛtvayoriva // 70
1.d:
मातृक्लृप्ते हि देवस्य तत्र तत्र वपुष्यलम् ।
को भेदो वस्तुतो वह्नेर्दग्धृपक्तृत्वयोरिव ॥ 70
1.m: For in the various forms of the God imagined by the cogniser, / what real difference is there, like the burning and cooking capacities of fire?

1.s:
na vāsau paramārthena na kiṃcidbhāsanādṛte /
nahyasti kiṃcittacchaktitadvadbhedo'pi vāstavaḥ // 71
1.d:
न वासौ परमार्थेन न किंचिद्भासनादृते ।
नह्यस्ति किंचित्तच्छक्तितद्वद्भेदोऽपि वास्तवः ॥ 71
1.m: Or, in the ultimate sense, it is nothing except manifestation; / for there is nothing, nor is the distinction between power and its possessor real.

1.s:
svaśaktyudrekajanakaṃ tādātmyādvastuno hi yat /
śaktistadapi devyevaṃ bhāntyapyanyasvarūpiṇī // 72
1.d:
स्वशक्त्युद्रेकजनकं तादात्म्याद्वस्तुनो हि यत् ।
शक्तिस्तदपि देव्येवं भान्त्यप्यन्यस्वरूपिणी ॥ 72
1.m: For that which causes the surge of its own power is, through identity, the reality itself; / so too power is the Goddess, shining thus even while having the form of another.

1.s:
śivaścāluptavibhavastathā sṛṣṭo'vabhāsate /
svasaṃvinmātṛmakure svātantryādbhāvanādiṣu // 73
1.d:
शिवश्चालुप्तविभवस्तथा सृष्टोऽवभासते ।
स्वसंविन्मातृमकुरे स्वातन्त्र्याद्भावनादिषु ॥ 73
1.m: And Śiva, whose sovereignty is never lost, appears thus created, / in contemplation and the like, through absolute autonomy, in the mirror of the cogniser which is His own consciousness.

1.s:
tasmādyena mukhenaiṣa bhātyanaṃśo'pi tattathā /
śaktirityeṣa vastveva śaktitadvatkramaḥ sphuṭaḥ // 74
1.d:
तस्माद्येन मुखेनैष भात्यनंशोऽपि तत्तथा ।
शक्तिरित्येष वस्त्वेव शक्तितद्वत्क्रमः स्फुटः ॥ 74
1.m: Therefore, by whatever aspect He shines, even without parts, that is how / power is; thus the sequence of power and possessor of power is evident as reality itself.

1.s:
śrīmatkiraṇaśāstre ca tatpraśnottarapūrvakam /
anubhāvo vikalpo'pi mānaso na manaḥ śive // 75
1.d:
श्रीमत्किरणशास्त्रे च तत्प्रश्नोत्तरपूर्वकम् ।
अनुभावो विकल्पोऽपि मानसो न मनः शिवे ॥ 75
1.m: And in the venerable Kiraṇa scripture, introduced through a question and answer: / "Perception is a mental construct; there is no mind in Śiva.

1.s:
avijñāya śivaṃ dīkṣā kathamityatra cottaram /
kṣudhādyanubhavo naiva vikalpo nahi mānasaḥ // 76
1.d:
अविज्ञाय शिवं दीक्षा कथमित्यत्र चोत्तरम् ।
क्षुधाद्यनुभवो नैव विकल्पो नहि मानसः ॥ 76
1.m: Without knowing Śiva, how can there be initiation?" And the answer to this: / "The experience of hunger and the like is not a conceptual construct, nor is it mental.

1.s:
rasādyanadhyakṣatve'pi rūpādeva yathā tarum /
vikalpo vetti tadvattu nādabindvādinā śivam // 77
1.d:
रसाद्यनध्यक्षत्वेऽपि रूपादेव यथा तरुम् ।
विकल्पो वेत्ति तद्वत्तु नादबिन्द्वादिना शिवम् ॥ 77
1.m: Just as a conceptual construct knows a tree through form alone even when taste and the like are imperceptible, / so too it knows Śiva through resonance, the point, and the like."

1.s:
bahuśaktitvamasyoktaṃ śivasya yadato mahān /
kalātattvapurārṇāṇupadādirbhedavistaraḥ // 78
1.d:
बहुशक्तित्वमस्योक्तं शिवस्य यदतो महान् ।
कलातत्त्वपुरार्णाणुपदादिर्भेदविस्तरः ॥ 78
1.m: Because it is said that this Śiva has many powers, therefore / great is the expansion of differences: parts, principles, worlds, letters, bound souls, words, and so forth;

1.s:
sṛṣṭisthititirodhānasaṃhārānugrahādi ca /
turyamityapi devasya bahuśaktitvajṛmbhitam // 79
1.d:
सृष्टिस्थितितिरोधानसंहारानुग्रहादि च ।
तुर्यमित्यपि देवस्य बहुशक्तित्वजृम्भितम् ॥ 79
1.m: and creation, stasis, concealment, dissolution, and grace, / as well as the Fourth—[all] are the play of the God's possession of many powers.

1.s:
jāgratsvapnasuṣuptānyatadatītāni yānyapi /
tānyapyamuṣya nāthasya svātantryalaharībharaḥ // 80
1.d:
जाग्रत्स्वप्नसुषुप्तान्यतदतीतानि यान्यपि ।
तान्यप्यमुष्य नाथस्य स्वातन्त्र्यलहरीभरः ॥ 80
1.m: Waking, dreaming, deep sleep, and that which transcends them— / these too are the mass of waves of this Lord's absolute autonomy.

1.s:
mahāmantreśamantreśamantrāḥ śivapurogamāḥ /
akalau sakalaśceti śivasyaiva vibhūtayaḥ // 81
1.d:
महामन्त्रेशमन्त्रेशमन्त्राः शिवपुरोगमाः ।
अकलौ सकलश्चेति शिवस्यैव विभूतयः ॥ 81
1.m: The Great Lords of Mantras, the Lords of Mantras, and the Mantras, with Śiva at their head, / the non-embodied and the embodied—are the sovereign manifestations of Śiva alone.

1.s:
tattvagrāmasya sarvasya dharmaḥ syādanapāyavān /
ātmaiva hi svabhāvātmetyuktaṃ śrītriśiromate // 82
1.d:
तत्त्वग्रामस्य सर्वस्य धर्मः स्यादनपायवान् ।
आत्मैव हि स्वभावात्मेत्युक्तं श्रीत्रिशिरोमते ॥ 82
1.m: The essential property of the entire aggregate of principles is imperishable; / for the Self alone is of the nature of one's intrinsic reality, as stated in the venerable Triśiromata:

1.s:
hṛdisthaṃ sarvadehasthaṃ svabhāvasthaṃ susūkṣmakam /
sāmūhyaṃ caiva tattvānāṃ grāmaśabdena kīrtitam // 83
1.d:
हृदिस्थं सर्वदेहस्थं स्वभावस्थं सुसूक्ष्मकम् ।
सामूह्यं चैव तत्त्वानां ग्रामशब्देन कीर्तितम् ॥ 83
1.m: "Residing in the heart, residing in the whole body, residing in one's intrinsic nature, extremely subtle; / the collective totality of principles is designated by the word 'aggregate'.

1.s:
ātmaiva dharma ityuktaḥ śivāmṛtapariplutaḥ /
prakāśāvasthitaṃ jñānaṃ bhāvābhāvādimadhyataḥ // 84
1.d:
आत्मैव धर्म इत्युक्तः शिवामृतपरिप्लुतः ।
प्रकाशावस्थितं ज्ञानं भावाभावादिमध्यतः ॥ 84
1.m: The Self alone is said to be the essential property, bathed in the nectar of Śiva; / knowledge stationed in luminosity within being, non-being, and the rest,

1.s:
svasthāne vartanaṃ jñeyaṃ draṣṭṛtvaṃ vigatāvṛti /
viviktavastukathitaśuddhavijñānanirmalaḥ // 85
1.d:
स्वस्थाने वर्तनं ज्ञेयं द्रष्टृत्वं विगतावृति ।
विविक्तवस्तुकथितशुद्धविज्ञाननिर्मलः ॥ 85
1.m: is to be known as abiding in its own state, the state of the seer, free from veil, / pure through the pure knowledge spoken of as the distinguished reality.

1.s:
grāmadharmavṛttiruktastasya sarvaṃ prasiddhyati /
ūrdhva tyaktvādho viśetsa rāmastho madhyadeśagaḥ // 86
1.d:
ग्रामधर्मवृत्तिरुक्तस्तस्य सर्वं प्रसिद्ध्यति ।
ऊर्ध्व त्यक्त्वाधो विशेत्स रामस्थो मध्यदेशगः ॥ 86
1.m: He is said to operate in the properties of the aggregate; for him everything succeeds. / Having abandoned the upper, he enters below; resting in delight, he goes to the central place.

1.s:
gatiḥ sthānaṃ svapnajāgradunmeṣaṇanimeṣaṇe /
dhāvanaṃ plavanaṃ caiva āyāsaḥ śaktivedanam // 87
1.d:
गतिः स्थानं स्वप्नजाग्रदुन्मेषणनिमेषणे ।
धावनं प्लवनं चैव आयासः शक्तिवेदनम् ॥ 87
1.m: Movement, standing, dreaming, waking, opening and closing of the eyes, / running, jumping, exertion, and the sensing of power,

1.s:
buddhibhedāstathā bhāvāḥ saṃjñāḥ karmāṇyanekaśaḥ /
eṣa rāmo vyāpako'tra śivaḥ paramakāraṇam // 88
1.d:
बुद्धिभेदास्तथा भावाः संज्ञाः कर्माण्यनेकशः ।
एष रामो व्यापकोऽत्र शिवः परमकारणम् ॥ 88
1.m: the varieties of intellect, states of being, concepts, and actions of many kinds— / this all-pervasive delight here is Śiva, the supreme cause.

1.s:
kalmaṣakṣīṇamanasā smṛtimātranirodhanāt /
dhyāyate paramaṃ dhyeyaṃ gamāgamapade sthitam // 89
1.d:
कल्मषक्षीणमनसा स्मृतिमात्रनिरोधनात् ।
ध्यायते परमं ध्येयं गमागमपदे स्थितम् ॥ 89
1.m: With a mind whose impurities are destroyed, by restraining mere memory, / one meditates on the supreme object of meditation, stationed in the state of going and coming.

1.s:
paraṃ śivaṃ tu vrajati bhairavākhyaṃ japādapi /
tatsvarūpaṃ japaḥ prokto bhāvābhāvapadacyutaḥ // 90
1.d:
परं शिवं तु व्रजति भैरवाख्यं जपादपि ।
तत्स्वरूपं जपः प्रोक्तो भावाभावपदच्युतः ॥ 90
1.m: One attains the supreme Śiva, named Bhairava, even through repetition of mantra; / repetition of mantra is declared to be His essential nature, fallen from the states of being and non-being."

1.s:
tadatrāpi tadīyena svātantryeṇopakalpitaḥ /
dūrāsannādiko bhedaścitsvātantryavyapekṣayā // 91
1.d:
तदत्रापि तदीयेन स्वातन्त्र्येणोपकल्पितः ।
दूरासन्नादिको भेदश्चित्स्वातन्त्र्यव्यपेक्षया ॥ 91
1.m:
Therefore, here too, distinction such as distant and near is fashioned
by his own absolute autonomy, with reference to the absolute autonomy of consciousness. // 91

1.s:
evaṃ svātantryapūrṇatvādatidurghaṭakāryayam /
kena nāma na rūpeṇa bhāsate parameśvaraḥ // 92
1.d:
एवं स्वातन्त्र्यपूर्णत्वादतिदुर्घटकार्ययम् ।
केन नाम न रूपेण भासते परमेश्वरः ॥ 92
1.m:
Thus, because he is full of absolute autonomy, achieving what is exceedingly difficult,
by what form indeed does the Supreme Lord not shine forth? // 92

1.s:
nirāvaraṇamābhāti bhātyābṛtanijātmakaḥ /
āvṛtānāvṛto bhāti bahudhā bhedasaṃgamāt // 93
1.d:
निरावरणमाभाति भात्याबृतनिजात्मकः ।
आवृतानावृतो भाति बहुधा भेदसंगमात् ॥ 93
1.m:
He shines unveiled; he shines with his own self veiled;
he shines veiled and unveiled in manifold ways through encounter with differentiation. // 93

1.s:
iti śaktitrayaṃ nāthe svātantryāparanāmakam /
icchādibhirabhikhyābhirgurubhiḥ prakaṭīkṛtam // 94
1.d:
इति शक्तित्रयं नाथे स्वातन्त्र्यापरनामकम् ।
इच्छादिभिरभिख्याभिर्गुरुभिः प्रकटीकृतम् ॥ 94
1.m:
Thus the triad of powers in the Lord, another name for absolute autonomy,
has been revealed by the gurus under designations such as will and the rest. // 94

1.s:
devo hyanvarthaśāstroktaiḥ śabdaiḥ samupadiśyate /
mahābhairavadevo'yaṃ patiryaḥ paramaḥ śivaḥ // 95
1.d:
देवो ह्यन्वर्थशास्त्रोक्तैः शब्दैः समुपदिश्यते ।
महाभैरवदेवोऽयं पतिर्यः परमः शिवः ॥ 95
1.m:
Indeed, the deity is taught by words spoken in scriptures having literal meaning:
this Lord who is the Great Bhairava-deity, who is the Supreme Śiva. // 95

1.s:
viśvaṃ bibharti pūraṇadhāraṇayogena tena ca śriyate /
savimarśatayā rava rūpataśca saṃsārabhīruhitakṛcca // 96
1.d:
विश्वं बिभर्ति पूरणधारणयोगेन तेन च श्रियते ।
सविमर्शतया रव रूपतश्च संसारभीरुहितकृच्च ॥ 96
1.m:
He bears the universe by fullness and maintenance, and is taken refuge in by it;
and by being endowed with reflective awareness, by the form of sound, he does what is beneficial for those fearful of worldly existence. // 96

1.s:
saṃsārabhītijanitādravātparāmarśato'pi hṛdi jātaḥ /
prakaṭībhūtaṃ bhavabhayavimarśanaṃ śaktipātato yena // 97
1.d:
संसारभीतिजनिताद्रवात्परामर्शतोऽपि हृदि जातः ।
प्रकटीभूतं भवभयविमर्शनं शक्तिपाततो येन ॥ 97
1.m:
Born in the heart from the cry produced by the fear of worldly existence, and from awareness,
by whom reflection upon the fear of becoming is made manifest through descent of power; // 97

1.s:
nakṣatraprerakakālatattvasaṃśoṣakāriṇo ye ca /
kālagrāsasamādhānarasikamanaḥsu teṣu ca prakaṭaḥ // 98
1.d:
नक्षत्रप्रेरककालतत्त्वसंशोषकारिणो ये च ।
कालग्राससमाधानरसिकमनःसु तेषु च प्रकटः ॥ 98
1.m:
and he is manifest in the minds of those who desiccate the reality of Time that impels the constellations,
who take delight in absorption in swallowing Time; // 98

1.s:
saṃkocipaśujanabhiye yāsāṃ ravaṇaṃ svakaraṇadevīnām /
antarbahiścaturvidhakhecaryādikagaṇasyāpi // 99
1.d:
संकोचिपशुजनभिये यासां रवणं स्वकरणदेवीनाम् ।
अन्तर्बहिश्चतुर्विधखेचर्यादिकगणस्यापि ॥ 99
1.m:
for the terror of contracting bound souls, there is the roaring of the goddesses of his own faculties,
and also of the fourfold host of Khecarīs and the rest, within and without; // 99

1.s:
tasya svāmī saṃsāravṛttivighaṭanamahābhīmaḥ /
bhairava iti gurubhirimairanvarthaiḥ saṃstutaḥ śāstre // 100
1.d:
तस्य स्वामी संसारवृत्तिविघटनमहाभीमः ।
भैरव इति गुरुभिरिमैरन्वर्थैः संस्तुतः शास्त्रे ॥ 100
1.m:
he is its master, exceedingly terrible in disintegrating worldly existence:
he is praised in scripture by the gurus with these literal meanings as 'Bhairava.' // 100

1.s:
heyopādeyakathāvirahe svānandaghanatayocchalanam /
krīḍā sarvotkarṣeṇavartanecchā tathā svatantratvam // 101
1.d:
हेयोपादेयकथाविरहे स्वानन्दघनतयोच्छलनम् ।
क्रीडा सर्वोत्कर्षेणवर्तनेच्छा तथा स्वतन्त्रत्वम् ॥ 101
1.m:
In the absence of any talk of what is to be abandoned or adopted, there is an overflowing as the mass of his own bliss,
play, the desire to operate with total pre-eminence, and likewise sovereignty, // 101

1.s:
vyavaharaṇamabhinne'pi svātmani bhedena saṃjalpaḥ /
nikhilāvabhāsanācca dyotanamasya stutiryataḥ sakalam // 102
1.d:
व्यवहरणमभिन्नेऽपि स्वात्मनि भेदेन संजल्पः ।
निखिलावभासनाच्च द्योतनमस्य स्तुतिर्यतः सकलम् ॥ 102
1.m:
everyday transactional activity, discursive formulation in terms of distinction even within his undivided self,
and illumination because of manifesting everything; praise belongs to him, since all things // 102

1.s:
tatpravaṇamātmalābhātprabhṛti samaste'pi kartavye /
bodhātmakaḥ samastakriyāmayo dṛkkriyāguṇaśca gatiḥ // 103
1.d:
तत्प्रवणमात्मलाभात्प्रभृति समस्तेऽपि कर्तव्ये ।
बोधात्मकः समस्तक्रियामयो दृक्क्रियागुणश्च गतिः ॥ 103
1.m:
are inclined towards him, beginning from the attainment of their own nature in every task;
he consists of awakening, embodies all action, has knowledge and action as his qualities, and is movement. // 103

1.s:
iti nirvacanaiḥ śivatanuśāstre gurubhiḥ smṛto devaḥ /
śāsanarodhanapālanapācanayogātsa sarvamupakurute /
tena patiḥ śreyomaya eva śivo nāśivaṃ kimapi tatra // 104
1.d:
इति निर्वचनैः शिवतनुशास्त्रे गुरुभिः स्मृतो देवः ।
शासनरोधनपालनपाचनयोगात्स सर्वमुपकुरुते ।
तेन पतिः श्रेयोमय एव शिवो नाशिवं किमपि तत्र ॥ 104

1.s:
īdṛgrūpaṃ kiyadapi rudropendrādiṣu sphuredyena /
tenāvacchedanude paramamahatpadaviśeṣaṇamupāttam // 105
1.d:
ईदृग्रूपं कियदपि रुद्रोपेन्द्रादिषु स्फुरेद्येन ।
तेनावच्छेदनुदे परममहत्पदविशेषणमुपात्तम् ॥ 105
1.m:
Lest such a nature shine to some degree in Rudra, Upendra, and the like,
for the removal of limitation, the qualifying epithets 'supreme' and 'great' have been employed. // 105

1.s:
iti yajjñeyasatattvaṃ darśyate tacchivājñayā /
mayā svasaṃvitsattarkapatiśāstratrikakramāt // 106
1.d:
इति यज्ज्ञेयसतत्त्वं दर्श्यते तच्छिवाज्ञया ।
मया स्वसंवित्सत्तर्कपतिशास्त्रत्रिकक्रमात् ॥ 106
1.m:
Thus the true essence of what is to be known is shown by Śiva's command
by me, in the sequence of the Trika, through my own consciousness, sound reasoning, and the Lord's scriptures. // 106

1.s:
tasya śaktaya evaitāstisro bhānti parādikāḥ /
sṛṣṭau sthitau laye turye tenaitā dvādaśoditāḥ // 107
1.d:
तस्य शक्तय एवैतास्तिस्रो भान्ति परादिकाः ।
सृष्टौ स्थितौ लये तुर्ये तेनैता द्वादशोदिताः ॥ 107
1.m:
These three powers of his shine forth as Supreme and the rest;
in emanation, stasis, dissolution, and the Fourth, these are therefore proclaimed as twelve. // 107

1.s:
tāvānpūrṇasvabhāvo'sau paramaḥ śiva ucyate /
tenātropāsakāḥ sākṣāttatraiva pariniṣṭhitāḥ // 108
1.d:
तावान्पूर्णस्वभावोऽसौ परमः शिव उच्यते ।
तेनात्रोपासकाः साक्षात्तत्रैव परिनिष्ठिताः ॥ 108
1.m:
To such an extent is he of complete nature; he is spoken of as the Supreme Śiva;
therefore worshippers here are directly established in that very [nature]. // 108

1.s:
tāsāmapi ca bhedāṃśanyūnādhikyādiyojanam /
tatsvātantryabalādeva śāstreṣu paribhāṣitam // 109
1.d:
तासामपि च भेदांशन्यूनाधिक्यादियोजनम् ।
तत्स्वातन्त्र्यबलादेव शास्त्रेषु परिभाषितम् ॥ 109
1.m:
Even their differentiation into parts, addition, subtraction, and so forth,
is formulated in the scriptures solely through the power of his absolute autonomy. // 109

1.s:
ekavīro yāmalo'tha triśaktiścaturātmakaḥ /
pañcamūrtiḥ ṣaḍātmāyaṃ saptako'ṣṭakabhūṣitaḥ // 110
1.d:
एकवीरो यामलोऽथ त्रिशक्तिश्चतुरात्मकः ।
पञ्चमूर्तिः षडात्मायं सप्तकोऽष्टकभूषितः ॥ 110
1.m:
The Lone Hero, the Dyad, then the Three Powers, the Fourfold,
the Five-bodied, this Sixfold one, the Septet, adorned as an Octad, // 110

1.s:
navātmā daśadikchaktirekādaśakalātmakaḥ /
dvādaśāramahācakranāyako bhairavastviti // 111
1.d:
नवात्मा दशदिक्छक्तिरेकादशकलात्मकः ।
द्वादशारमहाचक्रनायको भैरवस्त्विति ॥ 111
1.m:
the Ninefold, possessing powers of the ten directions, having the nature of eleven digits,
the leader of the great circle of twelve spokes—such is Bhairava. // 111

1.s:
evaṃ yāvatsahasrāre niḥsaṃkhyāre'pi vā prabhuḥ /
viśvacakre maheśāno viśvaśaktirvijṛmbhate // 112
1.d:
एवं यावत्सहस्रारे निःसंख्यारेऽपि वा प्रभुः ।
विश्वचक्रे महेशानो विश्वशक्तिर्विजृम्भते ॥ 112
1.m:
Thus up to the thousand-spoked or even the spoke-less [circle],
the Master, the Great Sovereign, of universal power, unfolds in the wheel of the universe. // 112

1.s:
teṣāmapi ca cakrāṇā svavargānugamātmanā /
aikyena cakrago bhedastatra tatra nirūpitaḥ // 113
1.d:
तेषामपि च चक्राणा स्ववर्गानुगमात्मना ।
ऐक्येन चक्रगो भेदस्तत्र तत्र निरूपितः ॥ 113
1.m:
Even of these wheels, by conforming to their respective groups,
the distinction residing in the wheels is ascertained here and there in terms of unity. // 113

1.s:
catuṣṣaḍdvirdvigaṇanāyogāttraiśirase mate /
ṣaṭcakreśvaratā nāthasyoktā citranijākṛteḥ // 114
1.d:
चतुष्षड्द्विर्द्विगणनायोगात्त्रैशिरसे मते ।
षट्चक्रेश्वरता नाथस्योक्ता चित्रनिजाकृतेः ॥ 114
1.m:
Through reckoning four, six, twice two, in the Traiśirasa doctrine,
the lordship of six wheels is stated of the Lord whose own form is varied. // 114

1.s:
nāmāni cakradevīnāṃ tatra kṛtyavibhedataḥ /
saumyaraudrākṛtidhyānayogīnyanvarthakalpanāt // 115
1.d:
नामानि चक्रदेवीनां तत्र कृत्यविभेदतः ।
सौम्यरौद्राकृतिध्यानयोगीन्यन्वर्थकल्पनात् ॥ 115
1.m:
There the names of the goddesses of the wheel, according to the division of their functions,
are associated with visualization of mild and fierce forms through literal designation. // 115

1.s:
ekasya saṃvinnāthasya hyāntarī pratibhā tanuḥ /
saumyaṃ vānyanmitaṃ saṃvidūrmicakramupāsyate // 116
1.d:
एकस्य संविन्नाथस्य ह्यान्तरी प्रतिभा तनुः ।
सौम्यं वान्यन्मितं संविदूर्मिचक्रमुपास्यते ॥ 116
1.m:
For the inner intuitive flash is the body of the one Lord of consciousness;
whether mild or otherwise limited, the wheel of waves of consciousness is worshipped. // 116

1.s:
asya syātpuṣṭirityeṣā saṃviddevī tathoditāt /
dhyānātsaṃjalpasaṃmiśrād vyāpārāccāpi bāhyataḥ // 117
1.d:
अस्य स्यात्पुष्टिरित्येषा संविद्देवी तथोदितात् ।
ध्यानात्संजल्पसंमिश्राद् व्यापाराच्चापि बाह्यतः ॥ 117
1.m:
'May nourishment come to him'—this goddess of consciousness, [arising] thus from the stated
visualization mixed with mental articulation, and also from external activity, // 117

1.s:
sphuṭībhūtā satī bhāti tasya tādṛkphalapradā /
puṣṭiḥ śuṣkasya sarasībhāvo jalamataḥ sitam // 118
1.d:
स्फुटीभूता सती भाति तस्य तादृक्फलप्रदा ।
पुष्टिः शुष्कस्य सरसीभावो जलमतः सितम् ॥ 118
1.m:
shines when she has become distinct, bestowing such fruit upon him;
nourishment is the moistening of what is dry, and therefore water is white. // 118

1.s:
anugamya tato dhyānaṃ tatpradhānaṃ pratanyate /
ye ca svabhāvato varṇā rasaniḥṣyandino yathā // 119
1.d:
अनुगम्य ततो ध्यानं तत्प्रधानं प्रतन्यते ।
ये च स्वभावतो वर्णा रसनिःष्यन्दिनो यथा ॥ 119
1.m:
Pursuing that, visualization primarily consisting of it is expanded;
and those phonemes which by nature exude fluid, such as // 119

1.s:
dantyauṣṭhyadantyaprāyāste kaiścidvarṇaiḥ kṛtāḥ saha /
taṃ bījabhāvamāgatya saṃvidaṃ sphuṭayanti tām // 120
1.d:
दन्त्यौष्ठ्यदन्त्यप्रायास्ते कैश्चिद्वर्णैः कृताः सह ।
तं बीजभावमागत्य संविदं स्फुटयन्ति ताम् ॥ 120
1.m:
those predominantly dental and labiodental, combined with certain phonemes,
attaining the state of a seed-syllable, make that consciousness distinct. // 120

1.s:
puṣṭiṃ kuru rasenainamāpyāyaya tarāmiti /
saṃjalpo'pi vikalpātmā kiṃ tāmeva na pūrayet // 121
1.d:
पुष्टिं कुरु रसेनैनमाप्यायय तरामिति ।
संजल्पोऽपि विकल्पात्मा किं तामेव न पूरयेत् ॥ 121
1.m:
'Create nourishment, replenish him further with fluid'—
would not even such discursive thought consisting of conceptual construct fulfil that very [deity]? // 121

1.s:
amṛteyamidaṃ kṣīramidaṃ sarpirbalāvaham /
tenāsya bījaṃ puṣṇīyāmityenāṃ pūrayetkriyām // 122
1.d:
अमृतेयमिदं क्षीरमिदं सर्पिर्बलावहम् ।
तेनास्य बीजं पुष्णीयामित्येनां पूरयेत्क्रियाम् ॥ 122
1.m:
'This is nectar, this is milk, this is strength-bearing ghee;
therefore I should nourish his seed'—with this he should fulfil the rite. // 122

1.s:
tasmādviśveśvaro bodhabhairavaḥ samupāsyate /
avacchedānavacchidbhyāṃ bhogamokṣārthibhirjanaiḥ // 123
1.d:
तस्माद्विश्वेश्वरो बोधभैरवः समुपास्यते ।
अवच्छेदानवच्छिद्भ्यां भोगमोक्षार्थिभिर्जनैः ॥ 123
1.m:
Therefore the Lord of the universe, Bhairava as awakening, is worshipped
by limited and non-limited means by people desiring enjoyment and liberation. // 123

1.s:
ye'pyanyadevatābhaktā ityato gururādiśat /
ye bodhādvyatiriktaṃ hi kiṃcidyājyatayā viduḥ // 124
1.d:
येऽप्यन्यदेवताभक्ता इत्यतो गुरुरादिशत् ।
ये बोधाद्व्यतिरिक्तं हि किंचिद्याज्यतया विदुः ॥ 124
1.m:
Hence the guru taught: 'Even those devoted to other deities...';
for those who know something separate from awakening as the object of sacrifice, // 124

1.s:
te'pi vedyaṃ viviñcānā bodhābhedena manvate /
tenāvicchinnatāmarśarūpāhantāprathātmanaḥ // 125
1.d:
तेऽपि वेद्यं विविञ्चाना बोधाभेदेन मन्वते ।
तेनाविच्छिन्नतामर्शरूपाहन्ताप्रथात्मनः ॥ 125
1.m:
they too, discerning the knowable, regard it as non-different from awakening;
therefore, of that self-manifesting one whose essence is the expansion of I-awareness in the form of uninterrupted apprehension, // 125

1.s:
svayaṃ-prathasya na vidhiḥ sṛṣṭyātmāsya ca pūrvagaḥ /
vedyā hi devatāsṛṣṭiḥ śakterhetoḥ samutthitā // 126
1.d:
स्वयं-प्रथस्य न विधिः सृष्ट्यात्मास्य च पूर्वगः ।
वेद्या हि देवतासृष्टिः शक्तेर्हेतोः समुत्थिता ॥ 126
1.m:
there is no injunctive rule, nor is his nature emanation, nor does it precede [awareness];
for the creation of deities as objects of knowledge has arisen on account of power. // 126

1.s:
ahaṃrūpā tu saṃvittirnityā svaprathanātmikā /
vidhirniyogastryaṃśā ca bhāvanā codanātmikā // 127
1.d:
अहंरूपा तु संवित्तिर्नित्या स्वप्रथनात्मिका ।
विधिर्नियोगस्त्र्यंशा च भावना चोदनात्मिका ॥ 127
1.m:
Consciousness consisting of 'I,' however, is eternal, consisting of its own self-expansion;
whereas an injunction is an obligation, and mental realization consisting of an urging has three parts. // 127

1.s:
tadekasiddhā indrādyā vidhipūrvā hi devatāḥ /
ahaṃbodhastu na tathā te tu saṃvedyarūpatām // 128
1.d:
तदेकसिद्धा इन्द्राद्या विधिपूर्वा हि देवताः ।
अहंबोधस्तु न तथा ते तु संवेद्यरूपताम् ॥ 128
1.m:
Established solely by that, the deities such as Indra are indeed preceded by an injunction;
the awareness of 'I,' however, is not so; but they, beholding [the deities] // 128

1.s:
unmagnāmeva paśyantastaṃ vidanto'pi no viduḥ /
taduktaṃ na vidurmāṃ tu tattvenātaścalanti te // 129
1.d:
उन्मग्नामेव पश्यन्तस्तं विदन्तोऽपि नो विदुः ।
तदुक्तं न विदुर्मां तु तत्त्वेनातश्चलन्ति ते ॥ 129
1.m:
as only an emergent knowable form, though knowing him, do not know [him].
Hence it is said: 'They do not know me in truth, and therefore they fall.' // 129

1.s:
calanaṃ tu vyavacchinnarūpatāpattireva yā /
devāndevayajo yāntītyādi tena nyarūpyata // 130
1.d:
चलनं तु व्यवच्छिन्नरूपतापत्तिरेव या ।
देवान्देवयजो यान्तीत्यादि तेन न्यरूप्यत ॥ 130
1.m:
Fall, however, is merely the lapse into a limited form;
by this, 'Those who sacrifice to the gods go to the gods' and so forth was explained. // 130

1.s:
nimajjya vedyatāṃ ye tu tatra saṃvinmayīṃ sthitim /
viduste hyanavacchinnaṃ tadbhaktā api yānti mām // 131
1.d:
निमज्ज्य वेद्यतां ये तु तत्र संविन्मयीं स्थितिम् ।
विदुस्ते ह्यनवच्छिन्नं तद्भक्ता अपि यान्ति माम् ॥ 131
1.m:
Those, however, who submerge knowability and know therein the state consisting of consciousness,
they, though devoted to them, attain me who am unconditioned. // 131

1.s:
sarvatrātra hyahaṃśabdo bodhamātraikavācakaḥ /
sa bhoktṛprabhuśabdābhyāṃ yājyayaṣṭṭatayoditaḥ // 132
1.d:
सर्वत्रात्र ह्यहंशब्दो बोधमात्रैकवाचकः ।
स भोक्तृप्रभुशब्दाभ्यां याज्ययष्ट्टतयोदितः ॥ 132
1.m:
For everywhere here the word 'I' denotes nothing other than consciousness alone;
it is proclaimed by the words 'enjoyer' and 'lord' as the object of sacrifice and the sacrificer. // 132

1.s:
yājamānī saṃvideva yājyā nānyeti coditam /
na tvākṛtiḥ kuto'pyanyā devatā na hi socitā // 133
1.d:
याजमानी संविदेव याज्या नान्येति चोदितम् ।
न त्वाकृतिः कुतोऽप्यन्या देवता न हि सोचिता ॥ 133
1.m:
It is enjoined that the sacrificer's own consciousness alone is the object of sacrifice, nothing else;
nor is there an external form from anywhere else, for no other deity is appropriate. // 133

1.s:
vidhiśca noktaḥ ko'pyatra mantrādi vṛttidhāma vā /
so'yamātmānamāvṛtya sthito jaḍapadaṃ gataḥ // 134
1.d:
विधिश्च नोक्तः कोऽप्यत्र मन्त्रादि वृत्तिधाम वा ।
सोऽयमात्मानमावृत्य स्थितो जडपदं गतः ॥ 134
1.m:
Nor is any injunction stated here, nor a mantra and the rest, nor a sphere of activity;
he, veiling himself, remains lapsed into the state of insentience. // 134

1.s:
āvṛtānāvṛtātmā tu devādisthāvarāntagaḥ /
jaḍājaḍasyāpyetasya dvairūpyasyāsti citratā // 135
1.d:
आवृतानावृतात्मा तु देवादिस्थावरान्तगः ।
जडाजडस्याप्येतस्य द्वैरूप्यस्यास्ति चित्रता ॥ 135
1.m:
Having a veiled and unveiled nature, however, he extends from the gods down to stationary objects;
even of this duality of sentient and insentient, there is manifold variety. // 135

1.s:
tasya svatantrabhāvo hi kiṃ kiṃ yanna vicintayet /
taduktaṃ triśiraḥśāstre saṃbuddha iti vetti yaḥ // 136
jñeyabhāvo hi ciddharmastacchāyācchādayenna tām // 136
1.d:
तस्य स्वतन्त्रभावो हि किं किं यन्न विचिन्तयेत् ।
तदुक्तं त्रिशिरःशास्त्रे संबुद्ध इति वेत्ति यः ॥ 136
ज्ञेयभावो हि चिद्धर्मस्तच्छायाच्छादयेन्न ताम् ॥ 136
1.m: For what might His autonomous nature not conceive? / As has been stated in the Triśirobhairavatantra: "He who knows that he is fully awakened, / for the nature of knowable reality is an attribute of consciousness, and its reflection cannot conceal consciousness."

1.s:
tenājaḍasya bhāgasya pudgalāṇvādisaṃjñinaḥ /
anāvaraṇabhāgāṃśe vaicitryaṃ bahudhā sthitam // 137
1.d:
तेनाजडस्य भागस्य पुद्गलाण्वादिसंज्ञिनः ।
अनावरणभागांशे वैचित्र्यं बहुधा स्थितम् ॥ 137
1.m: Therefore, with respect to the conscious part known as the soul, atom, and so forth, / a diversity exists in many ways in the portion that is unobscured.

1.s:
saṃvidrūpe na bhedo'sti vāstavo yadyapi dhruve /
tathāpyāvṛtinirhāsatāratamyātsa lakṣyate // 138
1.d:
संविद्रूपे न भेदोऽस्ति वास्तवो यद्यपि ध्रुवे ।
तथाप्यावृतिनिर्हासतारतम्यात्स लक्ष्यते ॥ 138
1.m: Even though in the eternal nature of consciousness there is no real difference, / nevertheless it appears [different] according to the gradations of the diminishing of obscuration.

1.s:
tadvistareṇa vakṣyāmaḥ śaktipātavinirṇaye /
samāpya paratāṃ sthaulyaprasaṃge carcayiṣyate // 139
1.d:
तद्विस्तरेण वक्ष्यामः शक्तिपातविनिर्णये ।
समाप्य परतां स्थौल्यप्रसंगे चर्चयिष्यते ॥ 139
1.m: We shall explain that at length in the determination of the descent of power; / having concluded [our discussion of] transcendence, it will be examined in the context of grossness.

1.s:
ataḥ kaṃcitpramātāraṃ prati prathayate vibhuḥ /
pūrṇameva nijaṃ rūpaṃ kaṃcidaṃśāṃśikākramāt // 140
1.d:
अतः कंचित्प्रमातारं प्रति प्रथयते विभुः ।
पूर्णमेव निजं रूपं कंचिदंशांशिकाक्रमात् ॥ 140
1.m: Therefore, the all-pervading Lord reveals His very own full form / to some knowing subject, and to another [He reveals it] gradually, part by part.

1.s:
viśvabhāvaikabhāvātmasvarūpaprathanaṃ hi yat /
aṇūnāṃ tatparaṃ jñānaṃ tadanyadaparaṃ bahu // 141
1.d:
विश्वभावैकभावात्मस्वरूपप्रथनं हि यत् ।
अणूनां तत्परं ज्ञानं तदन्यदपरं बहु ॥ 141
1.m: For that manifestation of one's own essential nature as identical with the singular nature of all entities / is higher knowledge for bound souls; that which is other than it is lower and manifold.

1.s:
tacca sākṣādupāyena tadupāyādināpi ca /
prathamānaṃ vicitrābhirbhaṃgībhiriha bhidyate // 142
1.d:
तच्च साक्षादुपायेन तदुपायादिनापि च ।
प्रथमानं विचित्राभिर्भंगीभिरिह भिद्यते ॥ 142
1.m: And that [knowledge], manifesting directly by a means, or by the means of that [means] and so forth, / is differentiated here through varied modes.

1.s:
tatrāpi svaparadvāradvāritvātsarvaśoṃśaśaḥ /
vyavadhānāvyavadhinā bhūyānbhedaḥ pravartate // 143
1.d:
तत्रापि स्वपरद्वारद्वारित्वात्सर्वशोंशशः ।
व्यवधानाव्यवधिना भूयान्भेदः प्रवर्तते ॥ 143
1.m: Even there, because of being the instrument or the mediated through itself or another, in all respects and in parts, / through mediation and immediacy, an extensive difference proceeds.

1.s:
jñānasya cābhyupāyo yo na tadajñānamucyate /
jñānameva tu tatsūkṣmaṃ paraṃ tvicchātmakaṃ matam // 144
1.d:
ज्ञानस्य चाभ्युपायो यो न तदज्ञानमुच्यते ।
ज्ञानमेव तु तत्सूक्ष्मं परं त्विच्छात्मकं मतम् ॥ 144
1.m: And the means to knowledge is not called ignorance; / rather, it is subtle knowledge itself, but the supreme [means] is held to consist of will.

1.s:
upāyopeyabhāvastu jñānasya sthaulyaviśramaḥ /
eṣaiva ca kriyāśaktirbandhamokṣaikakāraṇam // 145
1.d:
उपायोपेयभावस्तु ज्ञानस्य स्थौल्यविश्रमः ।
एषैव च क्रियाशक्तिर्बन्धमोक्षैककारणम् ॥ 145
1.m: The relation of means and end, however, is a resting in the grossness of knowledge; / and this very power of action is the sole cause of bondage and liberation.

1.s:
tatrādye svaparāmarśe nirvikalpaikadhāmani /
yatsphuretprakaṭaṃ sākṣāttadicchākhyaṃ prakīrtitam // 146
1.d:
तत्राद्ये स्वपरामर्शे निर्विकल्पैकधामनि ।
यत्स्फुरेत्प्रकटं साक्षात्तदिच्छाख्यं प्रकीर्तितम् ॥ 146
1.m: There, what shines forth directly and openly / in the initial self-awareness, in the sole abode of the non-conceptual, is proclaimed to be called will.

1.s:
yathā visphuritadṛśāmanusandhiṃ vināpyalam /
bhāti bhāvaḥ sphuṭastadvatkeṣāmapi śivātmatā // 147
1.d:
यथा विस्फुरितदृशामनुसन्धिं विनाप्यलम् ।
भाति भावः स्फुटस्तद्वत्केषामपि शिवात्मता ॥ 147
1.m: Just as an object shines clearly to those whose eyes are open, even without any synthesising thought, / just so the state of being Śiva shines to certain people.

1.s:
bhūyo bhūyo vikalpāṃśaniścayakramacarcanāt /
yatparāmarśamabhyeti jñānopāyaṃ tu tadviduḥ // 148
1.d:
भूयो भूयो विकल्पांशनिश्चयक्रमचर्चनात् ।
यत्परामर्शमभ्येति ज्ञानोपायं तु तद्विदुः ॥ 148
1.m: That which attains awareness through the examination of the sequential determination of components of conceptual constructs / repeatedly, however, they know as the means of knowledge.

1.s:
yattu tatkalpanāklṛptabahirbhūtārthasādhanam /
kriyopāyaṃ tadāmnātaṃ bhedo nātrāpavargagaḥ // 149
1.d:
यत्तु तत्कल्पनाक्लृप्तबहिर्भूतार्थसाधनम् ।
क्रियोपायं तदाम्नातं भेदो नात्रापवर्गगः ॥ 149
1.m: That which accomplishes through external objects fashioned by its conceptualisation / is handed down in tradition as the means of action; herein, there is no difference with respect to liberation.

1.s:
yato nānyā kriyā nāma jñānameva hi tattathā /
rūḍheryogāntatāṃ prāptamiti śrīgamaśāsane // 150
1.d:
यतो नान्या क्रिया नाम ज्ञानमेव हि तत्तथा ।
रूढेर्योगान्ततां प्राप्तमिति श्रीगमशासने ॥ 150
1.m: Because action is nothing other than knowledge itself; / it has reached the state of being yoga through established convention, as stated in the venerable scripture of the Āgama:

1.s:
yogo nānyaḥ kriyā nānyā tattvārūḍhā hi yā matiḥ /
svacittavāsanāśāntau sā kriyetyabhidhīyate // 151
1.d:
योगो नान्यः क्रिया नान्या तत्त्वारूढा हि या मतिः ।
स्वचित्तवासनाशान्तौ सा क्रियेत्यभिधीयते ॥ 151
1.m: "Yoga is nothing else, action is nothing else; for that thought which is established in reality / when the latencies of one's own mind are pacified, is called action.

1.s:
svacitte vāsanāḥ karmamalamāyāprasūtayaḥ /
tāsāṃ śāntinimittaṃ yā matiḥ saṃvitsvabhāvikā // 152
1.d:
स्वचित्ते वासनाः कर्ममलमायाप्रसूतयः ।
तासां शान्तिनिमित्तं या मतिः संवित्स्वभाविका ॥ 152
1.m: The latencies in one's own mind are born of karma, impurity, and māyā; / the thought whose nature is consciousness, which is for the sake of their pacification,

1.s:
sā dehārambhibāhyasthatattvabrātādhiśāyinī /
kriyā saiva ca yogaḥ syāttattvānāṃ cillayīkṛtau // 153
1.d:
सा देहारम्भिबाह्यस्थतत्त्वब्राताधिशायिनी ।
क्रिया सैव च योगः स्यात्तत्त्वानां चिल्लयीकृतौ ॥ 153
1.m: and which rests upon the multitude of tattvas situated externally and initiating the body, / is itself action and yoga in the dissolving of the tattvas into consciousness."

1.s:
loke'pi kila gacchāmītyevamantaḥ sphuraiva yā /
sā dehaṃ deśamakṣāṃścāpyāviśantī gatikriyā // 154
1.d:
लोकेऽपि किल गच्छामीत्येवमन्तः स्फुरैव या ।
सा देहं देशमक्षांश्चाप्याविशन्ती गतिक्रिया ॥ 154
1.m: Even in ordinary life, that which is an inner pulsing awareness such as 'I am going', / entering the body, space, and the senses, is indeed the action of movement.

1.s:
tasmātkriyāpi yā nāma jñānameva hi sā tataḥ /
jñānameva vimokṣāya yuktaṃ caitadudāhṛtam // 155
1.d:
तस्मात्क्रियापि या नाम ज्ञानमेव हि सा ततः ।
ज्ञानमेव विमोक्षाय युक्तं चैतदुदाहृतम् ॥ 155
1.m: Therefore, even what is called action is indeed knowledge itself; consequently, / knowledge alone leads to liberation, and this has rightly been declared.

1.s:
mokṣo hi nāma naivānyaḥ svarūpaprathanaṃ hi saḥ /
svarūpaṃ cātmanaḥ saṃvinnānyattatra tu yāḥ punaḥ // 156
1.d:
मोक्षो हि नाम नैवान्यः स्वरूपप्रथनं हि सः ।
स्वरूपं चात्मनः संविन्नान्यत्तत्र तु याः पुनः ॥ 156
1.m: For liberation is nothing other than the manifestation of one's own essential nature; / and the essential nature of the self is consciousness, nothing else. In that regard, however, those powers,

1.s:
kriyādikāḥ śaktayastāḥ saṃvidrūpādhikā nahi /
asaṃvidrūpatāyogāddharmiṇaścānirūpaṇāt // 157
1.d:
क्रियादिकाः शक्तयस्ताः संविद्रूपाधिका नहि ।
असंविद्रूपतायोगाद्धर्मिणश्चानिरूपणात् ॥ 157
1.m: such as action, are not something additional to the nature of consciousness, / because they cannot be of an unconscious nature, and because a possessor of attributes cannot be established [apart from them].

1.s:
parameśvaraśāstre hi na ca kāṇādadṛṣṭivat /
śaktīnāṃ dharmarūpāṇāmāśrayaḥ ko'pi kathyate // 158
1.d:
परमेश्वरशास्त्रे हि न च काणाददृष्टिवत् ।
शक्तीनां धर्मरूपाणामाश्रयः कोऽपि कथ्यते ॥ 158
1.m: For in the scripture of the Supreme Lord, unlike the Kaṇādan view, / no substratum whatsoever is asserted for the powers which have the nature of attributes.

1.s:
tataśca dṛkkriyecchādyā bhinnāścecchaktayastathā /
ekaḥ śiva itīyaṃ vāgvastuśūnyaiva jāyate // 159
1.d:
ततश्च दृक्क्रियेच्छाद्या भिन्नाश्चेच्छक्तयस्तथा ।
एकः शिव इतीयं वाग्वस्तुशून्यैव जायते ॥ 159
1.m: And therefore, if the powers such as perception, action, and will are distinct [from Him], / then the statement that 'Śiva is one' becomes entirely devoid of real substance.

1.s:
tasmātsaṃvittvamevaitatsvātantryaṃ yattadapyalam /
vivicyamānaṃ bahvīṣu paryavasyati śaktiṣu // 160
1.d:
तस्मात्संवित्त्वमेवैतत्स्वातन्त्र्यं यत्तदप्यलम् ।
विविच्यमानं बह्वीषु पर्यवस्यति शक्तिषु ॥ 160
1.m: Therefore, this very state of being consciousness is absolute autonomy; that too, when fully / analysed, culminates in manifold powers.

1.s:
yataścātmaprathā mokṣastannehāśaṅkyamīdṛśam /
nāvaśyaṃ kāraṇātkārya tajjñānyapi na mucyate // 161
1.d:
यतश्चात्मप्रथा मोक्षस्तन्नेहाशङ्क्यमीदृशम् ।
नावश्यं कारणात्कार्य तज्ज्ञान्यपि न मुच्यते ॥ 161
1.m: And since liberation is the manifestation of the self, such an objection cannot be raised here: / 'An effect does not necessarily follow from a cause, so even one who possesses that knowledge might not be liberated.'

1.s:
yato jñānena mokṣasya yā hetuphalatoditā /
na sā mukhyā tato nāyaṃ prasaṃga iti niścitam // 162
1.d:
यतो ज्ञानेन मोक्षस्य या हेतुफलतोदिता ।
न सा मुख्या ततो नायं प्रसंग इति निश्चितम् ॥ 162
1.m: Because the relation of cause and effect between knowledge and liberation that has been stated / is not primary; hence it is certain that this objection does not apply.

1.s:
evaṃ jñānasvabhāvaiva kriyā sthūlatvamātmani /
yato vahati tenāsyāṃ citratā dṛśyatāṃ kila // 163
1.d:
एवं ज्ञानस्वभावैव क्रिया स्थूलत्वमात्मनि ।
यतो वहति तेनास्यां चित्रता दृश्यतां किल ॥ 163
1.m: Thus action, whose essential nature is knowledge, takes on grossness in itself; / for that reason, let its diversity indeed be observed.

1.s:
kriyopāye'bhyupāyānāṃ grāhyabāhyavibhedinām /
bhedopabhedavaividhyānniḥsaṃkhyatvamavāntarāt // 164
1.d:
क्रियोपायेऽभ्युपायानां ग्राह्यबाह्यविभेदिनाम् ।
भेदोपभेदवैविध्यान्निःसंख्यत्वमवान्तरात् ॥ 164
1.m: In the means of action, the subordinate means, which are differentiated by apprehended and external [objects], / are countless through their primary and secondary divisions, from intermediate [distinctions].

1.s:
anena caitatpradhvastaṃ yatkecana śaśaṅkire /
upāyabhedānmokṣe'pi bhedaḥ syāditi sūrayaḥ // 165
1.d:
अनेन चैतत्प्रध्वस्तं यत्केचन शशङ्किरे ।
उपायभेदान्मोक्षेऽपि भेदः स्यादिति सूरयः ॥ 165
1.m: And by this is refuted that which certain scholars suspected, / namely that there would be a difference even in liberation because of the difference of means.

1.s:
malatacchaktividhvaṃsatirobhūcyutimadhyataḥ /
hetubhede'pi no bhinnā ghaṭadhvaṃsādivṛttivat // 166
1.d:
मलतच्छक्तिविध्वंसतिरोभूच्युतिमध्यतः ।
हेतुभेदेऽपि नो भिन्ना घटध्वंसादिवृत्तिवत् ॥ 166
1.m: Among the destruction, obscuration, and eradication of impurity and its powers, / even when the causes differ, there is no difference, just as in the occurrence of the destruction of a pot and the like.

1.s:
tadetattrividhatvaṃ hi śāstre śrīpūrvanāmani /
ādeśi parameśitrā samāveśavinirṇaye // 167
1.d:
तदेतत्त्रिविधत्वं हि शास्त्रे श्रीपूर्वनामनि ।
आदेशि परमेशित्रा समावेशविनिर्णये ॥ 167
1.m: Indeed, this threefold nature was taught by the Supreme Lord / in the scripture named the venerable Pūrva (Mālinīvijayottara) in the determination of absorption:

1.s:
akiṃciccintakasyaiva guruṇā pratibodhataḥ /
utpadyate ya āveśaḥ śāmbhavo'sāvidīritaḥ // 168
1.d:
अकिंचिच्चिन्तकस्यैव गुरुणा प्रतिबोधतः ।
उत्पद्यते य आवेशः शाम्भवोऽसाविदीरितः ॥ 168
1.m: "That absorption which arises for one who is thinking of nothing at all, / solely through awakening by the guru, is declared to be Śāmbhava.

1.s:
uccārarahitaṃ vastu cetasaiva vicintayan /
yaṃ samāveśamāpnoti śāktaḥ so'trābhidhīyate // 169
1.d:
उच्चाररहितं वस्तु चेतसैव विचिन्तयन् ।
यं समावेशमाप्नोति शाक्तः सोऽत्राभिधीयते ॥ 169
1.m: Contemplating with the mind alone that reality which is devoid of recitation, / that absorption which one attains is here called Śākta.

1.s:
uccārakaraṇadhyānavarṇasthānaprakalpanaiḥ /
yo bhavetsa samāveśaḥ samyagāṇava ucyate // 170
1.d:
उच्चारकरणध्यानवर्णस्थानप्रकल्पनैः ।
यो भवेत्स समावेशः सम्यगाणव उच्यते ॥ 170
1.m: That absorption which occurs through recitation, bodily postures, meditation, letters, / and the conceptualisation of loci is properly called Āṇava."

1.s:
akiṃciccintakasyeti vikalpānupayogitā /
tayā ca jhaṭiti jñeyasamāpattirnirūpyate // 171
1.d:
अकिंचिच्चिन्तकस्येति विकल्पानुपयोगिता ।
तया च झटिति ज्ञेयसमापत्तिर्निरूप्यते ॥ 171
1.m: By the phrase 'for one who is thinking of nothing at all', the non-utility of conceptual constructs is indicated; / and by that, the sudden attainment of the object of knowledge is demonstrated.

1.s:
sā kathaṃ bhavatītyāha guruṇātigarīyasā /
jñeyābhimukhabodhena drākprarūḍhatvaśālinā // 172
1.d:
सा कथं भवतीत्याह गुरुणातिगरीयसा ।
ज्ञेयाभिमुखबोधेन द्राक्प्ररूढत्वशालिना ॥ 172
1.m: He states how that happens: 'through the guru', who is exceedingly weighty, / meaning: through awakening directed towards the knowable, quickly possessing rootedness.

1.s:
tṛtīyārthe tasi vyākhyā vā vaiyadhikaraṇyataḥ /
āveśaścāsvatantrasya svatadrūpanimajjanāt // 173
1.d:
तृतीयार्थे तसि व्याख्या वा वैयधिकरण्यतः ।
आवेशश्चास्वतन्त्रस्य स्वतद्रूपनिमज्जनात् ॥ 173
1.m: The suffix -tasi is explained in the sense of the instrumental case, or through syntactic non-co-reference. / And absorption of one who is not autonomous [consists] in the immersion of one's own nature into that [Supreme] nature,

1.s:
paratadrūpatā śambhorādyācchaktyavibhāginaḥ /
tenāyamatra vākyārtho vijñeyaṃ pronmiṣatsvayam // 174
1.d:
परतद्रूपता शम्भोराद्याच्छक्त्यविभागिनः ।
तेनायमत्र वाक्यार्थो विज्ञेयं प्रोन्मिषत्स्वयम् ॥ 174
1.m: the supreme nature of Śambhu being indivisible from His primordial power. / Therefore, this is the meaning of the statement here: the object of knowledge, expanding by itself,

1.s:
vināpi niścayena drāk mātṛdarpaṇabimbitam /
mātāramadharīkurvat svāṃ vibhūtiṃ pradarśayat // 175
1.d:
विनापि निश्चयेन द्राक् मातृदर्पणबिम्बितम् ।
मातारमधरीकुर्वत् स्वां विभूतिं प्रदर्शयत् ॥ 175
1.m: suddenly reflected in the mirror of the subject even without determinate cognition, / subordinating the subject, displaying its own sovereign glory,

1.s:
āste hṛdayanairmalyātiśaye tāratamyataḥ /
jñeyaṃ dvidhā ca cinmātraṃ jaḍaṃ cādyaṃ ca kalpitam // 176
1.d:
आस्ते हृदयनैर्मल्यातिशये तारतम्यतः ।
ज्ञेयं द्विधा च चिन्मात्रं जडं चाद्यं च कल्पितम् ॥ 176
1.m: abides according to the degree of exceptional purity of the heart. / And the knowable is twofold: pure consciousness and insentient matter; and the first is imagined,

1.s:
itarattu tathā satyaṃ tadvibhāgo'yamīdṛśaḥ /
jaḍena yaḥ samāveśaḥ sapraticchandakākṛtiḥ // 177
1.d:
इतरत्तु तथा सत्यं तद्विभागोऽयमीदृशः ।
जडेन यः समावेशः सप्रतिच्छन्दकाकृतिः ॥ 177
1.m: whereas the other is true in that way. Such is this distinction: / absorption with an insentient object has the form of a reflected image,

1.s:
caitanyena samāveśastādātmyaṃ nāparaṃ kila /
tenāvikalpā saṃvittirbhāvanādyanapekṣiṇī // 178
1.d:
चैतन्येन समावेशस्तादात्म्यं नापरं किल ।
तेनाविकल्पा संवित्तिर्भावनाद्यनपेक्षिणी ॥ 178
1.m: whereas absorption with consciousness is identity itself, nothing other. / Therefore, non-conceptual consciousness, independent of meditation and the like,

1.s:
śivatādātmyamāpannā samāveśo'tra śāṃbhavaḥ /
tatprasādātpunaḥ paścādbhāvino'tra viniścayāḥ // 179
1.d:
शिवतादात्म्यमापन्ना समावेशोऽत्र शांभवः ।
तत्प्रसादात्पुनः पश्चाद्भाविनोऽत्र विनिश्चयाः ॥ 179
1.m: which has attained identity with Śiva, is the Śāmbhava absorption here. / Determinate cognitions which may occur subsequently here through its grace—

1.s:
santu tādātmyamāpannā na tu teṣāmupāyatā /
vikalpāpekṣayā mānamavikalpamiti bruvan // 180
1.d:
सन्तु तादात्म्यमापन्ना न तु तेषामुपायता ।
विकल्पापेक्षया मानमविकल्पमिति ब्रुवन् ॥ 180
1.m: let them attain identity, but they do not have the status of being a means [to it]. / One who says that a non-conceptual means of valid cognition depends upon a conceptual construct

1.s:
pratyukta eva siddhaṃ hi vikalpenānugamyate /
gṛhītamiti suspaṣṭā niścayasya yataḥ prathā // 181
1.d:
प्रत्युक्त एव सिद्धं हि विकल्पेनानुगम्यते ।
गृहीतमिति सुस्पष्टा निश्चयस्य यतः प्रथा ॥ 181
1.m: is refuted indeed; for what is already established is followed by a conceptual construct, / since the manifestation of determinate judgment is clearly evident as: 'This has been grasped.'

1.s:
gṛhṇāmītyavikalpaikyabalāttu pratipadyate /
avikalpātmasaṃvittau yā sphurattaiva vastunaḥ // 182
1.d:
गृह्णामीत्यविकल्पैक्यबलात्तु प्रतिपद्यते ।
अविकल्पात्मसंवित्तौ या स्फुरत्तैव वस्तुनः ॥ 182
1.m: Yet, [the knower] understands through the force of identity with the non-conceptual, [thinking] ‘I apprehend’; / for what is the very vibrant radiance of an object in non-conceptual consciousness,

1.s:
sā siddhirna vikalpāttu vastvapekṣāvivarjitāt /
kevalaṃ saṃvidaḥ so'yaṃ nairmalyetaraviśramaḥ // 183
1.d:
सा सिद्धिर्न विकल्पात्तु वस्त्वपेक्षाविवर्जितात् ।
केवलं संविदः सोऽयं नैर्मल्येतरविश्रमः ॥ 183
1.m: that is its establishment, but not through a conceptual construct devoid of regard for the real object. / It is merely that consciousness rests in purity or otherwise,

1.s:
yadvikalpānapekṣatvasāpekṣatve nijātmani /
niśīthe'pi maṇijñānī vidyutkālapradarśitān // 184
1.d:
यद्विकल्पानपेक्षत्वसापेक्षत्वे निजात्मनि ।
निशीथेऽपि मणिज्ञानी विद्युत्कालप्रदर्शितान् ॥ 184
1.m: in that in its own nature there is independence or dependence upon conceptual constructs. / Even in the dead of night, a connoisseur of jewels distinguishes those various distinct features

1.s:
tāṃstānviśeṣāṃścinute ratnānāṃ bhūyasāmapi /
nairmalyaṃ saṃvidaścedaṃ pūrvābhyāsavaśādatho // 185
1.d:
तांस्तान्विशेषांश्चिनुते रत्नानां भूयसामपि ।
नैर्मल्यं संविदश्चेदं पूर्वाभ्यासवशादथो ॥ 185
1.m: even of many gems, when revealed by a flash of lightning. / And this purity of consciousness, whether by force of prior practice

1.s:
aniyantreśvarecchāta ityetaccarcayiṣyate /
pañcāśadvidhatā cāsya samāveśasya varṇitā // 186
1.d:
अनियन्त्रेश्वरेच्छात इत्येतच्चर्चयिष्यते ।
पञ्चाशद्विधता चास्य समावेशस्य वर्णिता ॥ 186
1.m: or from the unrestrained will of the Lord, will be examined. / And the fiftyfold division of this absorption was described

1.s:
tattvaṣaṭtriṃśakaitatsthasphuṭabhedābhisandhitaḥ /
etattattvāntare yatpuṃvidyāśaktyātmakaṃ trayam // 187
1.d:
तत्त्वषट्त्रिंशकैतत्स्थस्फुटभेदाभिसन्धितः ।
एतत्तत्त्वान्तरे यत्पुंविद्याशक्त्यात्मकं त्रयम् ॥ 187
1.m: with a view to the distinct divisions inherent in this group of thirty-six principles. / Among these other principles, the triad consisting of the person, vidyā, and power [is counted],

1.s:
ambhodhikāṣṭhājvalanasaṃkhyairbhedairyataḥ kramāt /
puṃvidyāśaktisaṃjñaṃ yattatsarvavyāpakaṃ yataḥ // 188
1.d:
अम्भोधिकाष्ठाज्वलनसंख्यैर्भेदैर्यतः क्रमात् ।
पुंविद्याशक्तिसंज्ञं यत्तत्सर्वव्यापकं यतः ॥ 188
1.m: because of the divisions [numbering] respectively four, ten, and three. / For that which is called the person, vidyā, and power is all-pervading;

1.s:
avyāpakebhyastenedaṃ bhedena gaṇitaṃ kila /
aśuddhiśuddhyamānatvaśuddhitastu mitho'pi tat // 189
1.d:
अव्यापकेभ्यस्तेनेदं भेदेन गणितं किल ।
अशुद्धिशुद्ध्यमानत्वशुद्धितस्तु मिथोऽपि तत् ॥ 189
1.m: therefore it is indeed counted separately from the non-pervading [principles], / and mutually too, based on being impure, being purified, and being pure.

1.s:
bhūtānyadhyakṣasiddhāni kāryahetvanumeyataḥ /
tattvavargātpṛthagbhūtasamākhyānyata eva hi // 190
1.d:
भूतान्यध्यक्षसिद्धानि कार्यहेत्वनुमेयतः ।
तत्त्ववर्गात्पृथग्भूतसमाख्यान्यत एव हि ॥ 190
1.m: The gross elements are established through direct perception; through inferring causes from effects, / [they are distinguished] from the group of principles, and for that very reason their designations are distinct.

1.s:
sarvapratītisadbhāvagocaraṃ bhūtameva hi /
viduścatuṣṭaye cātra sāvakāśe tadāsthitim // 191
1.d:
सर्वप्रतीतिसद्भावगोचरं भूतमेव हि ।
विदुश्चतुष्टये चात्र सावकाशे तदास्थितिम् ॥ 191
1.m: Indeed, what is within the scope of the existence of every perception is just an element; / and here, in this tetrad which provides room, they know its presence.

1.s:
rudraśaktisamāveśaḥ pañcadhā nanu carcyate /
ko'vakāśo bhavettatra bhautāveśādivarṇane // 192
1.d:
रुद्रशक्तिसमावेशः पञ्चधा ननु चर्च्यते ।
कोऽवकाशो भवेत्तत्र भौतावेशादिवर्णने ॥ 192
1.m: [Objection:] Surely the absorption into Rudra's power is treated as fivefold. / What room could there be in describing an absorption into the gross elements and the like?

1.s:
prasaṃgādetaditicetsamādhiḥ saṃbhavannayam /
nāsmākaṃ mānasāvarjī loko bhinnaruciryataḥ // 193
1.d:
प्रसंगादेतदितिचेत्समाधिः संभवन्नयम् ।
नास्माकं मानसावर्जी लोको भिन्नरुचिर्यतः ॥ 193
1.m: If [you say]: ‘This [is mentioned] in passing,’ such a proposed answer, / although possible, does not captivate our mind, since people have different tastes.

1.s:
ucyate dvaitaśāstreṣu parameśādvibheditā /
bhūtādīnāṃ yathā sātra na tathā dvayavarjite // 194
1.d:
उच्यते द्वैतशास्त्रेषु परमेशाद्विभेदिता ।
भूतादीनां यथा सात्र न तथा द्वयवर्जिते ॥ 194
1.m: In reply it is said: The differentiation of the gross elements and so on from the Supreme Lord / taught in the dualistic scriptures is not so here, in [the teaching] devoid of duality.

1.s:
yāvānṣaṭtriṃśakaḥ so'yaṃ yadanyadapi kiṃcana /
etāvatī mahādevī rudraśaktiranargalā // 195
1.d:
यावान्षट्त्रिंशकः सोऽयं यदन्यदपि किंचन ।
एतावती महादेवी रुद्रशक्तिरनर्गला ॥ 195
1.m: As far as this thirty-six-principle [reality] extends, and whatever else there may be, / that whole extent is the Great Goddess, the unrestrained power of Rudra.

1.s:
tata eva dvitīye'sminnadhikāre nyarūpyata /
dharāderviśvarūpatvaṃ pāñcadaśyādibhedataḥ // 196
1.d:
तत एव द्वितीयेऽस्मिन्नधिकारे न्यरूप्यत ।
धरादेर्विश्वरूपत्वं पाञ्चदश्यादिभेदतः ॥ 196
1.m: For this very reason, in this second chapter was explained / the omniform nature of earth and the other principles through divisions such as the fifteenfold.

1.s:
tasmādyathā purasthe'rthe guṇādyaṃśāṃśikāmukhāt /
niraṃśabhāvasaṃbodhastathaivātrāpi budhyatām // 197
1.d:
तस्माद्यथा पुरस्थेऽर्थे गुणाद्यंशांशिकामुखात् ।
निरंशभावसंबोधस्तथैवात्रापि बुध्यताम् ॥ 197
1.m: Therefore, just as in an object present before [one], by way of partial aspects such as qualities, / there is cognition of the impartite entity, let it be understood in the very same way here too.

1.s:
ata evāvikalpatvadhrauvyaprābhavavaibhavaiḥ /
anyairvā śaktirūpatvāddharmaiḥ svasamavāyibhiḥ // 198
1.d:
अत एवाविकल्पत्वध्रौव्यप्राभववैभवैः ।
अन्यैर्वा शक्तिरूपत्वाद्धर्मैः स्वसमवायिभिः ॥ 198
1.m: For this very reason, through their own inherent attributes—such as non-conceptuality, constancy, / preeminence, and majesty, or others—because they are of the nature of power,

1.s:
sarvaśo'pyatha vāṃśena taṃ vibhuṃ parameśvaram /
upāsate vikalpaughasaṃskārādye śrutotthitāt // 199
1.d:
सर्वशोऽप्यथ वांशेन तं विभुं परमेश्वरम् ।
उपासते विकल्पौघसंस्काराद्ये श्रुतोत्थितात् ॥ 199
1.m: those who, from the impression of a flood of conceptual constructs arising from scripture, / worship that all-pervading Supreme Lord in His entirety or in part,

1.s:
te tattatsvavikalpāntaḥsphurattaddharmapāṭavāt /
dharmiṇaṃ pūrṇadharmaughamabhedenādhiśerate // 200
1.d:
ते तत्तत्स्वविकल्पान्तःस्फुरत्तद्धर्मपाटवात् ।
धर्मिणं पूर्णधर्मौघमभेदेनाधिशेरते ॥ 200
1.m: they, by the dexterity of that attribute vibrant within their respective conceptual constructs, / non-differently take their rest in the possessor of attributes, the full flood of attributes.

1.s:
ūcivānata eva śrīvidyādhipatirādarāt /
tvatsvarūpamavikalpamakṣajā kalpane na viṣayīkaroti cet /
antarullikhitacitrasaṃvido no bhaveyuranubhūtayaḥ sphuṭāḥ // 201
1.d:
ऊचिवानत एव श्रीविद्याधिपतिरादरात् ।
त्वत्स्वरूपमविकल्पमक्षजा कल्पने न विषयीकरोति चेत् ।
अन्तरुल्लिखितचित्रसंविदो नो भवेयुरनुभूतयः स्फुटाः ॥ 201
1.m: Hence the venerable Vidyādhipati respectfully said: / ‘If sense-born conceptual construct does not make your non-conceptual nature its object, / the distinct experiences of the manifold consciousness internally depicted would not exist.’

1.s:
taduktaṃ śrīmataṅgādau svaśaktikiraṇātmakam /
atha patyuradhiṣṭhānamityādyuktaṃ viśeṣaṇaiḥ // 202
1.d:
तदुक्तं श्रीमतङ्गादौ स्वशक्तिकिरणात्मकम् ।
अथ पत्युरधिष्ठानमित्याद्युक्तं विशेषणैः ॥ 202
1.m: That is stated in the venerable Mataṅga and elsewhere: ‘consisting of the rays of His own power, / and the station of the Lord,’ and so on, described through qualifiers:

1.s:
tasyāṃ divi sudīptātmā niṣkampo'calamūrtimān /
kāṣṭhā saiva parā sūkṣmā sarvadikkāmṛtātmikā // 203
1.d:
तस्यां दिवि सुदीप्तात्मा निष्कम्पोऽचलमूर्तिमान् ।
काष्ठा सैव परा सूक्ष्मा सर्वदिक्कामृतात्मिका ॥ 203
1.m: ‘In that heaven, intensely blazing, unmoving, having an unshakable form, / she is the supreme, subtle goal, consisting of nectar in all directions,

1.s:
pradhvastāvaraṇā śāntā vastumātrātilālasā /
ādyantoparatā sādhvī mūrtitvenopacaryate // 204
1.d:
प्रध्वस्तावरणा शान्ता वस्तुमात्रातिलालसा ।
आद्यन्तोपरता साध्वी मूर्तित्वेनोपचर्यते ॥ 204
1.m: her coverings destroyed, tranquil, ardently longing only for the real object, / having ceased from beginning and end, auspicious; she is metaphorically called a form.’

1.s:
tathopacārasyātraitannimitaṃ saprayojanam /
tanmukhā sphuṭatā dharmiṇyāśu tanmayatāsthitiḥ // 205
1.d:
तथोपचारस्यात्रैतन्निमितं सप्रयोजनम् ।
तन्मुखा स्फुटता धर्मिण्याशु तन्मयतास्थितिः ॥ 205
1.m: Here, this is the cause, possessed of purpose, for such a metaphorical expression: / clarity regarding the possessor of attributes through its medium, [and] swift abidance in identity with it.

1.s:
ta eva dharmāḥ śaktyākhyāstaistairucitarūpakaiḥ /
ākāraiḥ paryupāsyante tanmayībhāvasiddhaye // 206
1.d:
त एव धर्माः शक्त्याख्यास्तैस्तैरुचितरूपकैः ।
आकारैः पर्युपास्यन्ते तन्मयीभावसिद्धये ॥ 206
1.m: Those very attributes, called powers, are worshipped through various suitable / forms for the sake of achieving identity with it.

1.s:
tatra kācitpunaḥ śaktiranantā vā mitāśca vā /
ākṣipeddhavatāsattvanyāyāddūrāntikatvataḥ // 207
1.d:
तत्र काचित्पुनः शक्तिरनन्ता वा मिताश्च वा ।
आक्षिपेद्धवतासत्त्वन्यायाद्दूरान्तिकत्वतः ॥ 207
1.m: In that context, a certain power—whether infinite or limited—/ would imply [the others] through proximity or distance, according to the rule of the runner's existence.

1.s:
tena pūrṇasvabhāvatvaṃ prakāśatvaṃ cidātmatā /
bhairavatvaṃ viśvaśaktīrākṣipedvyāpakatvataḥ // 208
1.d:
तेन पूर्णस्वभावत्वं प्रकाशत्वं चिदात्मता ।
भैरवत्वं विश्वशक्तीराक्षिपेद्व्यापकत्वतः ॥ 208
1.m: Therefore, having a complete nature, being luminosity, being of the nature of consciousness, / and being Bhairava would imply all powers because of their all-pervasive nature.

1.s:
sadāśivādayastūrdhvavyāptyabhāvādadhojuṣaḥ /
śaktīḥ samākṣipeyustadupāsāntikadūrataḥ // 209
1.d:
सदाशिवादयस्तूर्ध्वव्याप्त्यभावादधोजुषः ।
शक्तीः समाक्षिपेयुस्तदुपासान्तिकदूरतः ॥ 209
1.m: Sadāśiva and the rest, however, lacking upward pervasion, would imply / the lower-dwelling powers according to the proximity or distance of their worship.

1.s:
itthaṃ-bhāve ca śāktākhyo vaikalpikapathakramaḥ /
iha tūkto yatastasmāt pratiyogyavikalpakam // 210
1.d:
इत्थं-भावे च शाक्ताख्यो वैकल्पिकपथक्रमः ।
इह तूक्तो यतस्तस्मात् प्रतियोग्यविकल्पकम् ॥ 210
1.m: And when it is of this kind, [it is] the succession of the path of conceptual constructs known as the śākta [means]. / But since it is stated here, therefore its counterpart is the non-conceptual.

1.s:
avikalpapathārūḍho yena yena pathā viśet /
dharāsadāśivāntena tena tena śivībhavet // 211
1.d:
अविकल्पपथारूढो येन येन पथा विशेत् ।
धरासदाशिवान्तेन तेन तेन शिवीभवेत् ॥ 211
1.m: Ascended to the non-conceptual path, through whatever path one enters—/ ending with earth or Sadāśiva—through that very [path] one becomes Śiva.

1.s:
nirmale hṛdaye prāgryasphuradbhūmyaṃśabhāsini /
prakāśe tanmukhenaiva saṃvitparaśivātmatā // 212
1.d:
निर्मले हृदये प्राग्र्यस्फुरद्भूम्यंशभासिनि ।
प्रकाशे तन्मुखेनैव संवित्परशिवात्मता ॥ 212
1.m: In a pure heart, in luminosity shining with an eminent, vibrant aspect of the earth, / consciousness has the nature of Supreme Śiva through that very portal.

1.s:
evaṃ parecchāśaktyaṃśasadupāyamimaṃ viduḥ /
śāmbhavākhyaṃ samāveśaṃ sumatyantenivāsinaḥ // 213
1.d:
