एवं परेच्छाशक्त्यंशसदुपायमिमं विदुः ।
शाम्भवाख्यं समावेशं सुमत्यन्तेनिवासिनः ॥ 213
1.m: Thus, the discerning disciples understand this absorption called śāmbhava, / which has as its true means an aspect of the Supreme Will-power.

1.s:
śākto'tha bhaṇyate cetodhī-manohaṃkṛti sphuṭam /
savikalpatayā māyāmayamicchādi vastutaḥ // 214
1.d:
शाक्तोऽथ भण्यते चेतोधी-मनोहंकृति स्फुटम् ।
सविकल्पतया मायामयमिच्छादि वस्तुतः ॥ 214
1.m: Now the śākta [absorption] is described: distinctly having intellect, mind, and ego, / by being conceptual it consists of māyā, [though] in truth it is will and the rest.

1.s:
abhimānena saṃkalpādhyavasāyakrameṇa yaḥ /
śāktaḥ sa māyopāyo'pi tadante nirvikalpakaḥ // 215
1.d:
अभिमानेन संकल्पाध्यवसायक्रमेण यः ।
शाक्तः स मायोपायोऽपि तदन्ते निर्विकल्पकः ॥ 215
1.m: That which proceeds through self-appropriation, by the succession of conception and determination, / is the śākta [absorption], which, although having māyā as its means, is non-conceptual at its culmination.

1.s:
paśorvai yāvikalpā bhūrdaśā sā śāmbhavī param /
apūrṇā mātṛdaurātmyāttadapāye vikasvarā // 216
1.d:
पशोर्वै याविकल्पा भूर्दशा सा शाम्भवी परम् ।
अपूर्णा मातृदौरात्म्यात्तदपाये विकस्वरा ॥ 216
1.m: The non-conceptual plane of the bound soul is indeed the śāmbhava state, but / incomplete due to the wickedness of the knowing subject; when that departs, it blossoms forth.

1.s:
evaṃ vaikalpikī bhūmiḥ śākte kartṛtvavedane /
yasyāṃ sphuṭe paraṃ tvasyāṃ saṃkocaḥ pūrvanītitaḥ // 217
1.d:
एवं वैकल्पिकी भूमिः शाक्ते कर्तृत्ववेदने ।
यस्यां स्फुटे परं त्वस्यां संकोचः पूर्वनीतितः ॥ 217
1.m: Thus the conceptual plane is in the śākta [means], in the awareness of agency / wherein, although it is manifest, contraction remains supreme according to the former rule.

1.s:
tathā saṃkocasaṃbhāravilāyanaparasya tu /
sā yatheṣṭāntarābhāsakāriṇī śaktirujjvalā // 218
1.d:
तथा संकोचसंभारविलायनपरस्य तु ।
सा यथेष्टान्तराभासकारिणी शक्तिरुज्ज्वला ॥ 218
1.m: And so, for one devoted to dissolving the mass of contraction, / that radiant power brings about internal appearances at will.

1.s:
nanu vaikalpikī kiṃ dhīrāṇave nāsti tatra sā /
anyopāyātra tūccārarahitatvaṃ nyarūpayat // 219
1.d:
ननु वैकल्पिकी किं धीराणवे नास्ति तत्र सा ।
अन्योपायात्र तूच्चाररहितत्वं न्यरूपयत् ॥ 219
1.m: [Objection:] Does not conceptual cognition belong to the āṇava [means]? [Reply:] There, it / has another means; but here, it was explained as being devoid of articulation.

1.s:
uccāraśabdenātroktā bahvantena tadādayaḥ /
śaktyupāye na santyete bhedābhedau hi śaktitā // 220
1.d:
उच्चारशब्देनात्रोक्ता बह्वन्तेन तदादयः ।
शक्त्युपाये न सन्त्येते भेदाभेदौ हि शक्तिता ॥ 220
1.m: By the word ‘articulation’ here, those [practices] ending with the gross body are spoken of, beginning with that; / these do not exist in the śākta means, for the nature of power is indeed difference-in-non-difference.

1.s:
aṇurnāma sphuṭo bhedastadupāya ihāṇavaḥ /
vikalpaniścayātmaiva paryante nirvikalpakaḥ // 221
1.d:
अणुर्नाम स्फुटो भेदस्तदुपाय इहाणवः ।
विकल्पनिश्चयात्मैव पर्यन्ते निर्विकल्पकः ॥ 221
1.m: The aṇu is manifest difference; its means here is the āṇava [means], / which consists entirely of conceptual determination, becoming non-conceptual at the culmination.

1.s:
nanu dhī-mānasāhaṃkṛtpumāṃso vyāpnuyuḥ śivam /
nādhovartitayā tena kathitaṃ kathamīdṛśam // 222
1.d:
ननु धी-मानसाहंकृत्पुमांसो व्याप्नुयुः शिवम् ।
नाधोवर्तितया तेन कथितं कथमीदृशम् ॥ 222
1.m: [Objection:] Surely, could intellect, mind, ego, and the person pervade Śiva? / Not by being lower-dwelling; how then is such a thing stated?

1.s:
ucyate vastuto'smākaṃ śiva eva tathāvidhaḥ /
svarūpagopanaṃ kṛtvā svaprakāśaḥ punastathā // 223
1.d:
उच्यते वस्तुतोऽस्माकं शिव एव तथाविधः ।
स्वरूपगोपनं कृत्वा स्वप्रकाशः पुनस्तथा ॥ 223
1.m: In reply it is said: In reality, in our view Śiva Himself is of such a nature; / having concealed His own nature, He is again self-luminous in that very way.

1.s:
dvaitaśāstre mataṅgādau cāpyetatsunirūpitam /
adhovyāptuḥ śivasyaiva sa prakāśo vyavasthitaḥ // 224
1.d:
द्वैतशास्त्रे मतङ्गादौ चाप्येतत्सुनिरूपितम् ।
अधोव्याप्तुः शिवस्यैव स प्रकाशो व्यवस्थितः ॥ 224
1.m: And this is well demonstrated in the dualistic scripture, the Mataṅga and others: / it is the luminosity of Śiva alone, who pervades below, that is established,

1.s: yena buddhi-manobhūmāvapi bhāti paraṃ padam // 225
1.d: येन बुद्धि-मनोभूमावपि भाति परं पदम् ॥ 225
1.m: by which the supreme state shines even on the plane of intellect and mind.

1.s:
dvāvapyetau samāveśau nirvikalpārṇavaṃ prati /
prayāta eva tadrūḍhiṃ vinā naiva hi kiṃcana // 226
1.d:
द्वावप्येतौ समावेशौ निर्विकल्पार्णवं प्रति ।
प्रयात एव तद्रूढिं विना नैव हि किंचन ॥ 226
1.m: Both these absorptions certainly lead toward the ocean of the non-conceptual; / for without establishing themselves in that, nothing at all [can exist].

1.s:
saṃvittiphalabhiccātra na prakalpyetyato'bravīt /
kalpanāyāśca mukhyatvamatraiva kila sūcitam // 227
1.d:
संवित्तिफलभिच्चात्र न प्रकल्प्येत्यतोऽब्रवीत् ।
कल्पनायाश्च मुख्यत्वमत्रैव किल सूचितम् ॥ 227
1.m: And here the division between consciousness and fruit is not to be imagined; therefore he said / that the preeminence of mental construction is indeed indicated right here.

1.s:
vikalpāpekṣayā yo'pi prāmāṇyaṃ prāha tanmate /
tadvikalpakramopāttanirvikalpapramāṇatā // 228
1.d:
विकल्पापेक्षया योऽपि प्रामाण्यं प्राह तन्मते ।
तद्विकल्पक्रमोपात्तनिर्विकल्पप्रमाणता ॥ 228
1.m: Even [a thinker] who asserts that valid cognition occurs by relying on conceptual construct [holds], in his system, / that valid cognition is [ultimately] non-conceptual, reached through the stages of that conceptual construct. // 228

1.s:
ratnatattvamavidvānprāṅniścayopāyacarcanāt /
anupāyāvikalpāptau ratnajña iti bhaṇyate // 229
1.d:
रत्नतत्त्वमविद्वान्प्राङ्निश्चयोपायचर्चनात् ।
अनुपायाविकल्पाप्तौ रत्नज्ञ इति भण्यते ॥ 229
1.m: One who does not know the true nature of a gem, before investigating the means to ascertain it, / is called an expert on gems once he attains the non-conceptual without means. // 229

1.s:
abhedopāyamatroktaṃ śāmbhavaṃ śāktamucyate /
bhedābhedātmakopāyaṃ bhedopāyaṃ tadāṇavam // 230
1.d:
अभेदोपायमत्रोक्तं शाम्भवं शाक्तमुच्यते ।
भेदाभेदात्मकोपायं भेदोपायं तदाणवम् ॥ 230
1.m: Here, the Śāmbhava means is said to consist in non-duality; the Śākta means / is said to consist in duality-in-non-duality; and the Āṇava means consists in duality. // 230

1.s:
ante jñāne'tra sopāye samastaḥ karmavistaraḥ /
prasphuṭenaiva rūpeṇa bhāvī so'ntarbhaviṣyati // 231
1.d:
अन्ते ज्ञानेऽत्र सोपाये समस्तः कर्मविस्तरः ।
प्रस्फुटेनैव रूपेण भावी सोऽन्तर्भविष्यति ॥ 231
1.m: At the end, in this knowledge accompanied by means, the entire expansion of ritual action / will be included, occurring in an utterly manifest form. // 231

1.s:
kriyā hi nāma vijñānānnānyadvastu kramātmatām /
upāyavaśataḥ prāptaṃ tatkriyeti puroditam // 232
1.d:
क्रिया हि नाम विज्ञानान्नान्यद्वस्तु क्रमात्मताम् ।
उपायवशतः प्राप्तं तत्क्रियेति पुरोदितम् ॥ 232
1.m: For action is indeed nothing other than consciousness; that consciousness has assumed the nature of succession / through the power of means: this is what was previously called action. // 232

1.s:
samyagjñānaṃ ca muktyekakāraṇaṃ svaparasthitam /
yato hi kalpanāmātraṃ svaparādivibhūtayaḥ // 233
1.d:
सम्यग्ज्ञानं च मुक्त्येककारणं स्वपरस्थितम् ।
यतो हि कल्पनामात्रं स्वपरादिविभूतयः ॥ 233
1.m: And correct knowledge, abiding in oneself or in another, is the sole cause of liberation; / for distinctions such as 'self' and 'other' are merely conceptual constructs. // 233

1.s:
tulye kālpanikatve ca yadaikyasphuraṇātmakaḥ /
guruḥ sa tāvadekātmā siddho muktaśca bhaṇyate // 234
1.d:
तुल्ये काल्पनिकत्वे च यदैक्यस्फुरणात्मकः ।
गुरुः स तावदेकात्मा सिद्धो मुक्तश्च भण्यते ॥ 234
1.m: And since conceptual construct applies equally, when the guru consists in the vibrant radiance of that oneness, / he is spoken of as having a single self, accomplished and liberated. // 234

1.s:
yāvānasya hi saṃtāno gurustāvatsa kīrtitaḥ /
samyagjñānamayaśceti svātmanā mucyate tataḥ // 235
1.d:
यावानस्य हि संतानो गुरुस्तावत्स कीर्तितः ।
सम्यग्ज्ञानमयश्चेति स्वात्मना मुच्यते ततः ॥ 235
1.m: For as far as his lineage extends, so far is he proclaimed as the guru; / and because he consists of correct knowledge, [the disciple] is liberated by that very Self. // 235

1.s:
tata eva svasaṃtānaṃ jñānī tārayatītyadaḥ /
yuktyāgamābhyāṃ saṃsiddhaṃ tāvāneko yato muniḥ // 236
1.d:
तत एव स्वसंतानं ज्ञानी तारयतीत्यदः ।
युक्त्यागमाभ्यां संसिद्धं तावानेको यतो मुनिः ॥ 236
1.m: For this very reason, that a knower rescues his own lineage / is thoroughly established by reasoning and scripture, since the sage is one to that entire extent. // 236

1.s:
tenātra ye codayanti nanu jñānādvimuktatā /
dīkṣādikā kriyā ceyaṃ sā kathaṃ muktaye bhavet // 237
1.d:
तेनात्र ये चोदयन्ति ननु ज्ञानाद्विमुक्तता ।
दीक्षादिका क्रिया चेयं सा कथं मुक्तये भवेत् ॥ 237
1.m: Therefore, regarding this, those who object: 'Surely liberation arises from knowledge, / and action such as initiation—how could that lead to liberation? // 237

1.s:
jñānātmā seti cejjñānaṃ yatrasthaṃ taṃ vimocayet /
anyasya mocane vāpi bhavetkiṃ nāsamañjasam /
iti te mūlataḥ kṣiptā yattvatrānyaiḥ samarthitam // 238
1.d:
ज्ञानात्मा सेति चेज्ज्ञानं यत्रस्थं तं विमोचयेत् ।
अन्यस्य मोचने वापि भवेत्किं नासमञ्जसम् ।
इति ते मूलतः क्षिप्ता यत्त्वत्रान्यैः समर्थितम् ॥ 238
1.m: If it is said that it consists of knowledge, [then] knowledge would liberate that person in whom it abides; / or if it liberates another, would that not be incongruous?'— / thus they are refuted at the root. But as for what is maintained here by others: // 238

1.s:
malo nāma kila dravyaṃ cakṣuḥsthapaṭalādivat /
tadvihantrī kriyā dīkṣā tvañjanādikakarmavat // 239
1.d:
मलो नाम किल द्रव्यं चक्षुःस्थपटलादिवत् ।
तद्विहन्त्री क्रिया दीक्षा त्वञ्जनादिककर्मवत् ॥ 239
1.m: 'Impurity is indeed a substance, like a cataract or the like in the eye; / action such as initiation destroys it, like the application of collyrium or the like'— // 239

1.s:
tatpurastānniṣetsyāmo yuktyāgamavigarhitam /
malamāyākarmaṇāṃ ca darśayiṣyāmahe sthitim // 240
1.d:
तत्पुरस्तान्निषेत्स्यामो युक्त्यागमविगर्हितम् ।
मलमायाकर्मणां च दर्शयिष्यामहे स्थितिम् ॥ 240
1.m: We shall refute that later on as censured by reasoning and scripture; / and we shall demonstrate the true nature of impurity, māyā, and karma. // 240

1.s:
evaṃ śaktitrayopāyaṃ yajjñānaṃ tatra paścimam /
mūlaṃ taduttaraṃ madhyamuttarottaramādimam // 241
1.d:
एवं शक्तित्रयोपायं यज्ज्ञानं तत्र पश्चिमम् ।
मूलं तदुत्तरं मध्यमुत्तरोत्तरमादिमम् ॥ 241
1.m: Thus, among that knowledge which possesses the three powers as means, the last / is the root; that which follows it is intermediate, and the very first is the highest of all. // 241

1.s:
tato'pi paramaṃ jñānamupāyādivivarjitam /
ānandaśaktiviśrāntamanuttaramihocyate // 242
1.d:
ततोऽपि परमं ज्ञानमुपायादिविवर्जितम् ।
आनन्दशक्तिविश्रान्तमनुत्तरमिहोच्यते ॥ 242
1.m: Higher even than that is the supreme knowledge devoid of means and the like, / resting in the power of bliss; it is called here the unexcelled. // 242

1.s:
tatsvaprakāśaṃ vijñānaṃ vidyāvidyeśvarādibhiḥ /
api durlabhasadbhāvaṃ śrīsiddhātantra ucyate // 243
1.d:
तत्स्वप्रकाशं विज्ञानं विद्याविद्येश्वरादिभिः ।
अपि दुर्लभसद्भावं श्रीसिद्धातन्त्र उच्यते ॥ 243
1.m: That self-luminous consciousness, whose true reality is difficult to attain / even for Vidyās, Vidyeśvaras, and the like, is described in the venerable Siddhātantra. // 243

1.s:
mālinyāṃ sūcitaṃ caitatpaṭale'ṣṭādaśe sphuṭam /
na caitadaprasannena śaṃkareṇeti vākyataḥ // 244
1.d:
मालिन्यां सूचितं चैतत्पटलेऽष्टादशे स्फुटम् ।
न चैतदप्रसन्नेन शंकरेणेति वाक्यतः ॥ 244
1.m: And this is clearly indicated in the eighteenth chapter of the Mālinī[vijayottara], / through the statement: 'Nor [can this be obtained] by an ungracious Śaṅkara.' // 244

1.s:
ityanenaiva pāṭhena mālinīvijayottare /
iti jñānacatuṣkaṃ yatsiddhimuktimahodayam /
tanmayā tantryate tantrālokanāmnyatra śāsane // 245
1.d:
इत्यनेनैव पाठेन मालिनीविजयोत्तरे ।
इति ज्ञानचतुष्कं यत्सिद्धिमुक्तिमहोदयम् ।
तन्मया तन्त्र्यते तन्त्रालोकनाम्न्यत्र शासने ॥ 245
1.m: Thus, by this very reading in the Mālinīvijayottara, / this tetrad of knowledges that yields the great dawn of spiritual accomplishment and liberation / is expounded by me in this teaching named the Tantrāloka. // 245

1.s:
tatreha yadyadantarvā bahirvā parimṛśyate /
anudghāṭitarūpaṃ tatpūrvameva prakāśate // 246
1.d:
तत्रेह यद्यदन्तर्वा बहिर्वा परिमृश्यते ।
अनुद्घाटितरूपं तत्पूर्वमेव प्रकाशते ॥ 246
1.m: In that regard, whatever is reflected upon here, whether internally or externally, / first appears with its form unrevealed. // 246

1.s:
tathānudghāṭitākārā nirvācyenātmanā prathā /
saṃśayaḥ kutracidrūpe niścite sati nānyathā // 247
1.d:
तथानुद्घाटिताकारा निर्वाच्येनात्मना प्रथा ।
संशयः कुत्रचिद्रूपे निश्चिते सति नान्यथा ॥ 247
1.m: Such manifestation of an unrevealed form, with an indefinable nature, / is doubt, once some aspect of its form is determined, and not otherwise. // 247

1.s:
etatkimiti mukhye'sminnetadaṃśaḥ suniścitaḥ /
saṃśayo'stitvanāstyādidharmānudghāṭitātmakaḥ // 248
1.d:
एतत्किमिति मुख्येऽस्मिन्नेतदंशः सुनिश्चितः ।
संशयोऽस्तित्वनास्त्यादिधर्मानुद्घाटितात्मकः ॥ 248
1.m: In the primary [doubt], 'What is this?', the part 'this' is well determined; / doubt has the nature of not having revealed attributes such as existence or non-existence. // 248

1.s:
kimityetasya śabdasya nādhiko'rthaḥ prakāśate /
kiṃ tvanunmudritākāraṃ vastvevābhidadhātyayam // 249
1.d:
किमित्येतस्य शब्दस्य नाधिकोऽर्थः प्रकाशते ।
किं त्वनुन्मुद्रिताकारं वस्त्वेवाभिदधात्ययम् ॥ 249
1.m: No additional meaning shines forth from this word 'what'; / rather, it designates the entity itself whose form is not yet sealed open. // 249

1.s:
sthāṇurvā puruṣo veti na mukhyo'styeṣa saṃśayaḥ /
bhūyaḥsthadharmajāteṣu niścayotpāda eva hi // 250
1.d:
स्थाणुर्वा पुरुषो वेति न मुख्योऽस्त्येष संशयः ।
भूयःस्थधर्मजातेषु निश्चयोत्पाद एव हि ॥ 250
1.m: 'Is it a post or a person?'—this is not primary doubt; / for it is merely the arising of determination concerning sets of commonly co-occurring attributes. // 250

1.s:
āmarśanīyadvairūpyānudghāṭanavaśātpunaḥ /
saṃśayaḥ sa kimityaṃśe vikalpastvanyathā sphuṭaḥ // 251
1.d:
आमर्शनीयद्वैरूप्यानुद्घाटनवशात्पुनः ।
संशयः स किमित्यंशे विकल्पस्त्वन्यथा स्फुटः ॥ 251
1.m: Moreover, doubt arises through not revealing the duality of forms to be reflected upon / in the part 'what'; but otherwise, the conceptual construct is distinct. // 251

1.s:
tenānudghāṭitātmatvabhāvaprathanameva yat /
prathamaṃ sa ihoddeśaḥ praśnaḥ saṃśaya eva ca // 252
1.d:
तेनानुद्घाटितात्मत्वभावप्रथनमेव यत् ।
प्रथमं स इहोद्देशः प्रश्नः संशय एव च ॥ 252
1.m: Therefore, that which is the very first manifestation of an entity whose nature is unrevealed / is here enunciation, question, and doubt. // 252

1.s:
tathānudghāṭitākārabhāvaprasaravartmanā /
prasarantī svasaṃvittiḥ praṣṭrī śiṣyātmatāṃ gatā // 253
1.d:
तथानुद्घाटिताकारभावप्रसरवर्त्मना ।
प्रसरन्ती स्वसंवित्तिः प्रष्ट्री शिष्यात्मतां गता ॥ 253
1.m: So, expanding by way of the expansion of entities whose forms are unrevealed, / one's own consciousness, becoming the questioner, assumes the nature of the disciple. // 253

1.s:
tathāntaraparāmarśaniścayātmatirohiteḥ /
prasarānantarodbhūtasaṃhārodayabhāgapi // 254
1.d:
तथान्तरपरामर्शनिश्चयात्मतिरोहितेः ।
प्रसरानन्तरोद्भूतसंहारोदयभागपि ॥ 254
1.m: So too, from the concealment that consists in the determination of internal reflective awareness, / even while participating in the arising of reabsorption that occurs immediately after expansion, // 254

1.s:
yāvatyeva bhavedbāhyaprasare prasphuṭātmani /
anunmīlitarūpā sā praṣṭrī tāvati bhaṇyate // 255
1.d:
यावत्येव भवेद्बाह्यप्रसरे प्रस्फुटात्मनि ।
अनुन्मीलितरूपा सा प्रष्ट्री तावति भण्यते ॥ 255
1.m: to whatever extent she exists with her form unopened / in the external expansion that is manifest, to that extent she is called the questioner. // 255

1.s:
svayamevaṃ vibodhaśca tathā praśnottarātmakaḥ /
guruśiṣyapade'pyeṣa dehabhedo hyatāttvikaḥ // 256
1.d:
स्वयमेवं विबोधश्च तथा प्रश्नोत्तरात्मकः ।
गुरुशिष्यपदेऽप्येष देहभेदो ह्यतात्त्विकः ॥ 256
1.m: Thus awareness itself consists of question and answer in this manner; / even in the status of guru and disciple, this division of bodies is indeed unreal. // 256

1.s:
bodho hi bodharūpatvādantarnānākṛtīḥ sthitāḥ /
bahirābhāsayatyeva drāksāmānyaviśeṣataḥ // 257
1.d:
बोधो हि बोधरूपत्वादन्तर्नानाकृतीः स्थिताः ।
बहिराभासयत्येव द्राक्सामान्यविशेषतः ॥ 257
1.m: For awareness, because of its nature as awareness, immediately brings to manifestation externally, / by way of the general and the particular, the manifold forms residing within. // 257

1.s:
srakṣyamāṇaviśeṣāṃśākāṃkṣāyogyasya kasyacit /
dharmasya sṛṣṭiḥ sāmānyasṛṣṭiḥ sā saṃśayātmikā // 258
1.d:
स्रक्ष्यमाणविशेषांशाकांक्षायोग्यस्य कस्यचित् ।
धर्मस्य सृष्टिः सामान्यसृष्टिः सा संशयात्मिका ॥ 258
1.m: The emission of some attribute capable of desiring the particular aspect about to be emitted / is the emission of the general; that consists of doubt. // 258

1.s:
srakṣyamāṇo viśeṣāṃśo yadā tūparamettadā /
nirṇayo mātṛrucito nānyathā kalpakoṭibhiḥ // 259
1.d:
स्रक्ष्यमाणो विशेषांशो यदा तूपरमेत्तदा ।
निर्णयो मातृरुचितो नान्यथा कल्पकोटिभिः ॥ 259
1.m: When, however, the particular aspect about to be emitted comes to rest, / then ascertainment, desired by the subject, [occurs], and not otherwise even in millions of aeons. // 259

1.s:
tasyātha vastunaḥ svātmavīryākramaṇapāṭavāt /
unmudraṇaṃ tayākṛtyā lakṣaṇottaranirṇayāḥ // 260
1.d:
तस्याथ वस्तुनः स्वात्मवीर्याक्रमणपाटवात् ।
उन्मुद्रणं तयाकृत्या लक्षणोत्तरनिर्णयाः ॥ 260
1.m: Then, through the skill of forcefully seizing upon its own vitality, the unsealing / of that entity with that form constitutes definition, answer, and ascertainment. // 260

1.s:
nirṇītatāvaddharmāṃśapṛṣṭhapātitayā punaḥ /
bhūyo bhūyaḥ samuddeśalakṣaṇātmaparīkṣaṇam // 261
1.d:
निर्णीततावद्धर्मांशपृष्ठपातितया पुनः ।
भूयो भूयः समुद्देशलक्षणात्मपरीक्षणम् ॥ 261
1.m: Then, following closely upon the heels of those aspects of attributes already ascertained, / examination repeatedly assumes the nature of enunciation and definition. // 261

1.s:
dṛṣṭānumānaupamyāptavacanādiṣu sarvataḥ /
uddeśalakṣaṇāvekṣātritayaṃ prāṇināṃ sphuret // 262
1.d:
दृष्टानुमानौपम्याप्तवचनादिषु सर्वतः ।
उद्देशलक्षणावेक्षात्रितयं प्राणिनां स्फुरेत् ॥ 262
1.m: In perception, inference, analogy, authoritative testimony, and so forth, everywhere, / the triad of enunciation, definition, and examination pulses in living beings. // 262

1.s:
nirvikalpitamuddeśo vikalpo lakṣaṇaṃ punaḥ /
parīkṣaṇaṃ tathādhyakṣe vikalpānāṃ paramparā // 263
1.d:
निर्विकल्पितमुद्देशो विकल्पो लक्षणं पुनः ।
परीक्षणं तथाध्यक्षे विकल्पानां परम्परा ॥ 263
1.m: Enunciation is non-conceptual, definition is conceptual construct, / and examination, in perception likewise, is the succession of conceptual constructs. // 263

1.s:
nago'yamiti coddeśo dhūmitvādagnimāniti /
lakṣyaṃ vyāptyādivijñānajālaṃ tvatra parīkṣaṇam // 264
1.d:
नगोऽयमिति चोद्देशो धूमित्वादग्निमानिति ।
लक्ष्यं व्याप्त्यादिविज्ञानजालं त्वत्र परीक्षणम् ॥ 264
1.m: 'This is a mountain' is the enunciation; 'it has fire because it has smoke' / is the defined; while the network of cognitions such as pervasion is here the examination. // 264

1.s:
uddeśo'yamiti prācyo gotulyo gavayābhidhaḥ /
iti vā lakṣaṇaṃ śeṣaḥ parīkṣopamitau bhavet // 265
1.d:
उद्देशोऽयमिति प्राच्यो गोतुल्यो गवयाभिधः ।
इति वा लक्षणं शेषः परीक्षोपमितौ भवेत् ॥ 265
1.m: The prior 'this' is enunciation; 'it resembles a cow, named gavaya'— / this is definition; the remainder in analogy is examination. // 265

1.s:
svaḥkāma īdṛguddeśo yajetetyasya lakṣaṇam /
agniṣṭomādinetyeṣā parīkṣā śeṣavartinī // 266
1.d:
स्वःकाम ईदृगुद्देशो यजेतेत्यस्य लक्षणम् ।
अग्निष्टोमादिनेत्येषा परीक्षा शेषवर्तिनी ॥ 266
1.m: 'One desirous of heaven' is such an enunciation; 'should sacrifice' is its definition; / 'by means of the Agniṣṭoma and the like' is the examination that occupies the remainder. // 266

1.s:
vikalpasrakṣyamāṇānyarucitāṃśasahiṣṇunaḥ /
vastuno yā tathātvena sṛṣṭiḥ soddeśasaṃjñitā // 267
1.d:
विकल्पस्रक्ष्यमाणान्यरुचितांशसहिष्णुनः ।
वस्तुनो या तथात्वेन सृष्टिः सोद्देशसंज्ञिता ॥ 267
1.m: The emission of an entity in that manner, capable of enduring another desired aspect / about to be emitted by conceptual construct, is called enunciation. // 267

1.s:
tadaiva saṃviccinute yāvataḥ srakṣyamāṇatā /
yato hyakālakalitā saṃdhatte sārvakālikam // 268
1.d:
तदैव संविच्चिनुते यावतः स्रक्ष्यमाणता ।
यतो ह्यकालकलिता संधत्ते सार्वकालिकम् ॥ 268
1.m: At that very moment, consciousness gathers whatever is about to be emitted; / for, unconditioned by time, it synthesizes what belongs to all time. // 268

1.s:
srakṣyamāṇasya yā sṛṣṭiḥ prāksṛṣṭāṃśasya saṃhṛtiḥ /
anūdyamāne dharme sā saṃvillakṣaṇamucyate // 269
1.d:
स्रक्ष्यमाणस्य या सृष्टिः प्राक्सृष्टांशस्य संहृतिः ।
अनूद्यमाने धर्मे सा संविल्लक्षणमुच्यते ॥ 269
1.m: When an attribute is being restated, the emission of what is about to be emitted / and the withdrawal of what was previously emitted is called the definition by consciousness. // 269

1.s:
tatpṛṣṭhapātibhūyoṃśasṛṣṭisaṃhāraviśramāḥ /
parīkṣā kathyate mātṛrucitā kalpitāvadhiḥ // 270
1.d:
तत्पृष्ठपातिभूयोंशसृष्टिसंहारविश्रमाः ।
परीक्षा कथ्यते मातृरुचिता कल्पितावधिः ॥ 270
1.m: The emission, withdrawal, and rest of further aspects following closely upon that / is called examination, whose boundary is conceived as desired by the knowing subject. // 270

1.s:
prākpaśyantyatha madhyānyā vaikharī ceti tā imāḥ /
parā parāparā devī caramā tvaparātmikā // 271
1.d:
प्राक्पश्यन्त्यथ मध्यान्या वैखरी चेति ता इमाः ।
परा परापरा देवी चरमा त्वपरात्मिका ॥ 271
1.m: First is Paśyantī, then the intermediate, Madhyamā, and the other is Vaikharī; / these are the goddesses: the Supreme, the Supreme-Non-Supreme, and the final one consists of the Non-Supreme. // 271

1.s:
icchādi śaktitritayamidameva nigadyate /
etatprāṇita evāyaṃ vyavahāraḥ pratāyate // 272
1.d:
इच्छादि शक्तित्रितयमिदमेव निगद्यते ।
एतत्प्राणित एवायं व्यवहारः प्रतायते ॥ 272
1.m: This very triad of powers beginning with will is proclaimed [here]; / vivified by this alone, all communicative activity unfolds. // 272

1.s:
etatpraśnottarātmatve pārameśvaraśāsane /
parasaṃbandharūpatvamabhisaṃbandhapañcake // 273
1.d:
एतत्प्रश्नोत्तरात्मत्वे पारमेश्वरशासने ।
परसंबन्धरूपत्वमभिसंबन्धपञ्चके ॥ 273
1.m: In the Lord's teaching, because it consists of question and answer in this manner, / there is the nature of the supreme connection among the five connections. // 273

1.s:
yathoktaṃ ratnamālāyāṃ sarvaḥ parakalātmakaḥ /
mahānavāntaro divyo miśro'nyo'nyastu pañcamaḥ // 274
1.d:
यथोक्तं रत्नमालायां सर्वः परकलात्मकः ।
महानवान्तरो दिव्यो मिश्रोऽन्योऽन्यस्तु पञ्चमः ॥ 274
1.m: As is stated in the Ratnamālā: “All is essentially the highest part: / the great, the intermediate, the divine, the mixed, and the mutual as the fifth.”

1.s:
bhinnayoḥ praṣṭṛtadvaktroścaikātmyaṃ yatsa ucyate /
saṃbandhaḥ paratā cāsya pūrṇaikātmyaprathāmayī // 275
1.d:
भिन्नयोः प्रष्टृतद्वक्त्रोश्चैकात्म्यं यत्स उच्यते ।
संबन्धः परता चास्य पूर्णैकात्म्यप्रथामयी ॥ 275
1.m: That which is the unity of identity between the two distinct [parties], the questioner and the speaker, is called / the relation; and its supremacy consists in the manifestation of complete non-duality.

1.s:
anenaiva nayena syātsaṃbandhāntaramapyalam /
śāstravācyaṃ phalādīnāṃ paripūrṇatvayogataḥ // 276
1.d:
अनेनैव नयेन स्यात्संबन्धान्तरमप्यलम् ।
शास्त्रवाच्यं फलादीनां परिपूर्णत्वयोगतः ॥ 276
1.m: By this very method, the other relations also would adequately be / expressible by the scripture, through their connection with the completeness of the fruit and other [factors].

1.s:
itthaṃ saṃvidiyaṃ devī svabhāvādeva sarvadā /
uddeśāditrayaprāṇā sarvaśāstrasvarūpiṇī // 277
1.d:
इत्थं संविदियं देवी स्वभावादेव सर्वदा ।
उद्देशादित्रयप्राणा सर्वशास्त्रस्वरूपिणी ॥ 277
1.m: Thus this Goddess, consciousness, inherently and at all times, / animated by the triad of enunciation and the rest, embodies the essence of all scriptures.

1.s:
tatrocyate puroddeśaḥ pūrvajānujabhedavān /
vijñānabhidgatopāyaḥ paropāyastṛtīyakaḥ // 278
1.d:
तत्रोच्यते पुरोद्देशः पूर्वजानुजभेदवान् ।
विज्ञानभिद्गतोपायः परोपायस्तृतीयकः ॥ 278
1.m: In that regard, the initial enunciation is stated first, divided into the preceding and the subsequent: / the discrimination of knowledge, the non-means, the highest means as the third,

1.s:
śāktopāyo naropāyaḥ kālopāyo'tha saptamaḥ /
cakrodayo'tha deśādhvā tattvādhvā tattvabhedanam // 279
1.d:
शाक्तोपायो नरोपायः कालोपायोऽथ सप्तमः ।
चक्रोदयोऽथ देशाध्वा तत्त्वाध्वा तत्त्वभेदनम् ॥ 279
1.m: the means of power, the means of the limited person, the means of time as the seventh, / the rising of the wheels, the path of space, the path of principles, the differentiation of principles,

1.s:
kalādyadhvādhvopayogaḥ śaktipātatirohitī /
dīkṣopakramaṇaṃ dīkṣā sāmayī pautrike vidhau // 280
1.d:
कलाद्यध्वाध्वोपयोगः शक्तिपाततिरोहिती ।
दीक्षोपक्रमणं दीक्षा सामयी पौत्रिके विधौ ॥ 280
1.m: the path of parts and the rest, the application of the path, the descent of power and concealment, / the preliminaries of initiation, the initiation of an initiate into the rule, in the rite of the spiritual son,

1.s:
prameyaprakriyā sūkṣmā dīkṣā sadyaḥsamutkramaḥ /
tulādīkṣātha pārokṣī liṅgoddhāro'bhiṣecanam // 281
1.d:
प्रमेयप्रक्रिया सूक्ष्मा दीक्षा सद्यःसमुत्क्रमः ।
तुलादीक्षाथ पारोक्षी लिङ्गोद्धारोऽभिषेचनम् ॥ 281
1.m: the detailed exposition of the objects of knowledge, subtle initiation, immediate departure [of the soul], / balance-scale initiation, remote initiation, the removal of the linga, consecration,

1.s:
antyeṣṭiḥ śrāddhaklṛptiśca śeṣavṛttinirūpaṇam /
liṅgārcā bahubhitparvapavitrādi nimittajam // 282
1.d:
अन्त्येष्टिः श्राद्धक्लृप्तिश्च शेषवृत्तिनिरूपणम् ।
लिङ्गार्चा बहुभित्पर्वपवित्रादि निमित्तजम् ॥ 282
1.m: the last sacrifice [funerary rites] and the arrangement of ancestor-offerings, the description of post-initiatory conduct, / worship of the linga in many ways, occasional rites occasioned by festivals, holy cloths and the like,

1.s:
rahasyacaryā mantraugho maṇḍalaṃ mudrikāvidhiḥ /
ekīkāraḥ svasvarūpe praveśaḥ śāstramelanam // 283
1.d:
रहस्यचर्या मन्त्रौघो मण्डलं मुद्रिकाविधिः ।
एकीकारः स्वस्वरूपे प्रवेशः शास्त्रमेलनम् ॥ 283
1.m: secret conduct, the aggregate of mantras, the maṇḍala, the rule of gestures, / unification, entry into one's own nature, the confluence of scriptures,

1.s:
āyātikathanaṃ śāstropādeyatvanirūpaṇam /
iti saptādhikāmenāṃ triṃśataṃ yaḥ sadā budhaḥ // 284
1.d:
आयातिकथनं शास्त्रोपादेयत्वनिरूपणम् ।
इति सप्ताधिकामेनां त्रिंशतं यः सदा बुधः ॥ 284
1.m: the exposition of transmission, and the determination of the scripture's authoritativeness. / Thus, the wise person who constantly studies

1.s:
āhnikānāṃ samabhyasyet sa sākṣādbhairavo bhavet /
saptatriṃśatsu saṃpūrṇabodho yadbhairavo bhavet // 285
1.d:
आह्निकानां समभ्यस्येत् स साक्षाद्भैरवो भवेत् ।
सप्तत्रिंशत्सु संपूर्णबोधो यद्भैरवो भवेत् ॥ 285
1.m: these thirty-seven daily lessons will become Bhairava directly. / Since one who has complete awakening across the thirty-seven becomes Bhairava,

1.s:
kiṃ citramaṇavo'pyasya dṛśā bhairavatāmiyuḥ /
ityeṣa pūrvajoddeśaḥ kathyate tvanujo'dhunā // 286
1.d:
किं चित्रमणवोऽप्यस्य दृशा भैरवतामियुः ।
इत्येष पूर्वजोद्देशः कथ्यते त्वनुजोऽधुना ॥ 286
1.m: what wonder is it that even limited beings attain the state of Bhairava through his gaze? / Thus this preceding enunciation is stated; now, however, the subsequent is told.

1.s:
vijñānabhitprakaraṇe bharvasyoddeśanaṃ kramāt /
dvitīyasminprakaraṇe gatopāyatvabheditā // 287
1.d:
विज्ञानभित्प्रकरणे भर्वस्योद्देशनं क्रमात् ।
द्वितीयस्मिन्प्रकरणे गतोपायत्वभेदिता ॥ 287
1.m: In the chapter on the discrimination of knowledge, there is the enunciation of fullness in succession; / in the second chapter, the varieties of the state of non-means [are explained].

1.s:
viśvacitpratibinbatvaṃ parāmarśodayakramaḥ /
mantrādyabhinnarūpatvaṃ paropāye vivicyate // 288
1.d:
विश्वचित्प्रतिबिन्बत्वं परामर्शोदयक्रमः ।
मन्त्राद्यभिन्नरूपत्वं परोपाये विविच्यते ॥ 288
1.m: The universe as a reflection in consciousness, the sequence of the emergence of reflective awareness, / and the non-difference from mantra and the rest are examined in the highest means.

1.s:
vikalpasaṃskriyā tarkatattvaṃ gurusatattvakam /
yogāṅgānupayogitvaṃ kalpitārcādyanādaraḥ // 289
1.d:
विकल्पसंस्क्रिया तर्कतत्त्वं गुरुसतत्त्वकम् ।
योगाङ्गानुपयोगित्वं कल्पितार्चाद्यनादरः ॥ 289
1.m: The purification of conceptual constructs, the reality of intuitive reasoning, the true nature of the guru, / the uselessness of the limbs of yoga, disregard for artificial worship and the like,

1.s:
saṃviccakrodayo mantravīrya japyādi vāstavam /
niṣedhavidhitulyatvaṃ śāktopāye'tra carcyate // 290
1.d:
संविच्चक्रोदयो मन्त्रवीर्य जप्यादि वास्तवम् ।
निषेधविधितुल्यत्वं शाक्तोपायेऽत्र चर्च्यते ॥ 290
1.m: the rising of the wheel of consciousness, the potency of mantra, true recitation and so forth, / and the equality of prohibition and injunction are examined here in the means of power.

1.s:
buddhidhyānaṃ prāṇatattvasamuccāraścidātmatā /
uccāraḥ paratattvāntaḥpraveśapathalakṣaṇam // 291
1.d:
बुद्धिध्यानं प्राणतत्त्वसमुच्चारश्चिदात्मता ।
उच्चारः परतत्त्वान्तःप्रवेशपथलक्षणम् ॥ 291
1.m: Mental contemplation, the pronunciation of the reality of breath, being identical with consciousness, / pronunciation, the characteristic of the path of entry into the highest reality,

1.s:
karaṇaṃ varṇatattvaṃ cetyāṇave tu nirūpyate /
cāramānamahorātrasaṃkrāntyādivikalpanam // 292
1.d:
करणं वर्णतत्त्वं चेत्याणवे तु निरूप्यते ।
चारमानमहोरात्रसंक्रान्त्यादिविकल्पनम् ॥ 292
1.m: the ritual bodily gesture, and the reality of phonemes are described in the [means] pertaining to the limited soul; / while the movement, the measure, day and night, the conceptualisation of transitions and so forth,

1.s:
saṃhāracitratā varṇodayaḥ kālādhvakalpane /
cakrabhinmantravidyābhidetaccakrodaye bhavet // 293
1.d:
संहारचित्रता वर्णोदयः कालाध्वकल्पने ।
चक्रभिन्मन्त्रविद्याभिदेतच्चक्रोदये भवेत् ॥ 293
1.m: the diversity of resorption, and the rising of phonemes [are explained] in the conceptualisation of the path of time. / The differentiation of wheels, the differentiation of mantras and vidyās, occur in this rising of the wheels.

1.s:
parimāṇaṃ purāṇāṃ ca saṃgrahastattvayojanam /
etaddeśādhvanirdeśe dvayaṃ tattvādhvanirṇaye // 294
1.d:
परिमाणं पुराणां च संग्रहस्तत्त्वयोजनम् ।
एतद्देशाध्वनिर्देशे द्वयं तत्त्वाध्वनिर्णये ॥ 294
1.m: The extent and compilation of the worlds, and the integration of principles: / these two are in the determination of the path of space; in the determination of the path of principles,

1.s:
kāryakāraṇabhāvaśca tattvakramanirūpaṇam /
vastudharmastattvavidhirjāgradādinirūpaṇam // 295
1.d:
कार्यकारणभावश्च तत्त्वक्रमनिरूपणम् ।
वस्तुधर्मस्तत्त्वविधिर्जाग्रदादिनिरूपणम् ॥ 295
1.m: the relation of cause and effect, the description of the sequence of principles, / the essential property of real entities, the rule of principles, the description of waking and other [states],

1.s:
pramātṛbheda ityetat tattvabhede vicāryate /
kalāsvarūpamekatripañcādyaistattvakalpanam // 296
1.d:
प्रमातृभेद इत्येतत् तत्त्वभेदे विचार्यते ।
कलास्वरूपमेकत्रिपञ्चाद्यैस्तत्त्वकल्पनम् ॥ 296
1.m: and the differentiation of subjects: this is examined in the differentiation of principles. / The nature of the parts, the conceptualisation of principles in groups of one, three, five, and so forth,

1.s:
varṇabhedakramaḥ sarvādhāraśaktinirūpaṇam /
kalādyadhvavicārāntaretāvatpravivicyate // 297
1.d:
वर्णभेदक्रमः सर्वाधारशक्तिनिरूपणम् ।
कलाद्यध्वविचारान्तरेतावत्प्रविविच्यते ॥ 297
1.m: the sequence of the division of phonemes, and the description of the power that is the support of all: / this much is thoroughly examined in the analysis of the path of parts and the rest.

1.s:
abhedabhāvanākampahāsau tvadhvopayojane /
saṃkhyādhikyaṃ malādīnāṃ tattvaṃ śaktivicitratā // 298
1.d:
अभेदभावनाकम्पहासौ त्वध्वोपयोजने ।
संख्याधिक्यं मलादीनां तत्त्वं शक्तिविचित्रता ॥ 298
1.m: The contemplation of non-duality, trembling, and laughter are [treated] in the application of the path; / the excess of number, the reality of impurities and the like, the diversity of power,

1.s:
anapekṣitvasiddhiśca tirobhāvavicitratā /
śaktipātaparīkṣāyāmetāvānvācyasaṃgrahaḥ // 299
1.d:
अनपेक्षित्वसिद्धिश्च तिरोभावविचित्रता ।
शक्तिपातपरीक्षायामेतावान्वाच्यसंग्रहः ॥ 299
1.m: and the establishment of independence, and the variety of concealment: / this is the summary of topics in the examination of the descent of power.

1.s:
tirobhāvavyapagamo jñānena paripūrṇatā /
utkrāntyanupayogitvaṃ dīkṣopakramaṇe sthitam // 300
1.d:
तिरोभावव्यपगमो ज्ञानेन परिपूर्णता ।
उत्क्रान्त्यनुपयोगित्वं दीक्षोपक्रमणे स्थितम् ॥ 300
1.m: The departure of concealment, completeness through knowledge, / and the uselessness of the departure of the soul are established in the preliminaries of initiation.

1.s:
śiṣyaucityaparīkṣādau sthānabhitsthānakalpanam /
sāmānyanyāsabhedo'rghapātraṃ caitatprayojanam // 301
1.d:
शिष्यौचित्यपरीक्षादौ स्थानभित्स्थानकल्पनम् ।
सामान्यन्यासभेदोऽर्घपात्रं चैतत्प्रयोजनम् ॥ 301
1.m: The examination of the disciple's fitness and so forth, the division of locations, the conceptualisation of the site, / the varieties of general imposition, the offering vessel and its purpose,

1.s:
dravyayogyatvamarcā ca bahirdvārārcanaṃ kramāt /
praveśo diksvarūpaṃ ca dehaprāṇādiśodhanam // 302
1.d:
द्रव्ययोग्यत्वमर्चा च बहिर्द्वारार्चनं क्रमात् ।
प्रवेशो दिक्स्वरूपं च देहप्राणादिशोधनम् ॥ 302
1.m: the suitability of substances, worship, outer worship at the doors in sequence, / entry, the nature of the directions, the purification of body, breath, and the like,

1.s:
viśeṣanyāsavaicitryaṃ saviśeṣārghabhājanam /
dehapūjā prāṇabuddhicitsvadhvanyāsapūjane // 303
1.d:
विशेषन्यासवैचित्र्यं सविशेषार्घभाजनम् ।
देहपूजा प्राणबुद्धिचित्स्वध्वन्यासपूजने ॥ 303
1.m: the diversity of specific impositions, the specific offering vessel, / the worship of the body, and the imposition and worship of one's own path in breath, intellect, and consciousness,

1.s:
anyaśāstragaṇotkarṣaḥ pūjā cakrasya sarvataḥ /
kṣetragrahaḥ pañcagavyaṃ pūjanaṃ bhūgaṇeśayoḥ // 304
1.d:
अन्यशास्त्रगणोत्कर्षः पूजा चक्रस्य सर्वतः ।
क्षेत्रग्रहः पञ्चगव्यं पूजनं भूगणेशयोः ॥ 304
1.m: the preeminence of the collection of other scriptures, the all-around worship of the wheel, / taking possession of the ground, the five products of the cow, the worship of the earth and the lord of gaṇas,

1.s:
astrārcā vahnikāryaṃ cāpyadhivāsanamagnigam /
tarpaṇaṃ carusaṃsiddhirdantakāṣṭhāntasaṃskriyā // 305
1.d:
अस्त्रार्चा वह्निकार्यं चाप्यधिवासनमग्निगम् ।
तर्पणं चरुसंसिद्धिर्दन्तकाष्ठान्तसंस्क्रिया ॥ 305
1.m: the worship of the weapon, the work with fire, the consecration in the fire, / libation, the preparation of the sacrificial dish, the purification ending with the tooth-stick,

1.s:
śivahastavidhiścāpi śayyāklṛptivicāraṇam /
svapnasya sāmayaṃ karma samayāśceti saṃgrahaḥ // 306
1.d:
शिवहस्तविधिश्चापि शय्याक्लृप्तिविचारणम् ।
स्वप्नस्य सामयं कर्म समयाश्चेति संग्रहः ॥ 306
1.m: the rite of the hand of Śiva, the examination of the preparation of the couch, / the ritual action of dreams, and the rules: such is the summary.

1.s:
samayitvavidhāvasminsyātpañcadaśa āhnike /
maṇḍalātmānusandhānaṃ nivedyapaśuvistaraḥ // 307
1.d:
समयित्वविधावस्मिन्स्यात्पञ्चदश आह्निके ।
मण्डलात्मानुसन्धानं निवेद्यपशुविस्तरः ॥ 307
1.m: This is in the rite of the initiate into the rule, in the fifteenth daily lesson. / Contemplation of the essence of the maṇḍala, the extent of the offering and sacrificial beast,

1.s:
agnitṛptiḥ svasvabhāvadīpanaṃ śiṣyadehagaḥ /
adhvanyāsavidhiḥ śodhyaśodhakādivicitratā // 308
1.d:
अग्नितृप्तिः स्वस्वभावदीपनं शिष्यदेहगः ।
अध्वन्यासविधिः शोध्यशोधकादिविचित्रता ॥ 308
1.m: the satisfaction of the fire, the kindling of one's own essential nature, the rule of the imposition / of the paths located in the body of the disciple, the diversity of the purified and the purifier and so forth,

1.s:
dīkṣābhedaḥ paro nyāso mantrasattāprayojanam /
bhedo yojanikādeśca ṣoḍaśe syādihāhnike // 309
1.d:
दीक्षाभेदः परो न्यासो मन्त्रसत्ताप्रयोजनम् ।
भेदो योजनिकादेश्च षोडशे स्यादिहाह्निके ॥ 309
1.m: the divisions of initiation, the higher imposition, the purpose of the existence of mantras, / and the difference of the unitive integration and the like: this is in the sixteenth daily lesson here.

1.s:
sūtraklṛptistattvaśuddhiḥ pāśadāho'tha yojanam /
adhvabhedastathetyevaṃ kathitaṃ pautrike vidhau // 310
1.d:
सूत्रक्लृप्तिस्तत्त्वशुद्धिः पाशदाहोऽथ योजनम् ।
अध्वभेदस्तथेत्येवं कथितं पौत्रिके विधौ ॥ 310
1.m: The preparation of the thread, the purification of principles, the burning of bonds, the unitive integration, / and likewise the divisions of the path: thus it is described in the rite of the spiritual son.

1.s:
jananādivihīnatvaṃ mantrabhedo'tha susphuṭaḥ /
iti saṃkṣiptadīkṣākhye syādaṣṭādaśa āhnike // 311
1.d:
जननादिविहीनत्वं मन्त्रभेदोऽथ सुस्फुटः ।
इति संक्षिप्तदीक्षाख्ये स्यादष्टादश आह्निके ॥ 311
1.m: Freedom from birth and so forth, and the distinct classification of mantras: / this is in the eighteenth daily lesson, called brief initiation.

1.s:
kalāvekṣā kṛpāṇyādinyāsaścāraḥ śarīragaḥ /
brahmavidyāvidhiścaivamuktaṃ sadyaḥsamutkrame // 312
1.d:
कलावेक्षा कृपाण्यादिन्यासश्चारः शरीरगः ।
ब्रह्मविद्याविधिश्चैवमुक्तं सद्यःसमुत्क्रमे ॥ 312
1.m: The observation of the parts, the imposition of the sword and the like, the movement within the body, / and the rule of the Brahmavidyā: thus it is stated in immediate departure.

1.s:
adhikāraparīkṣāntaḥsaṃskāro'tha tulāvidhiḥ /
ityetadvācyasarvasvaṃ syādviṃśatitamāhnike // 313
1.d:
अधिकारपरीक्षान्तःसंस्कारोऽथ तुलाविधिः ।
इत्येतद्वाच्यसर्वस्वं स्याद्विंशतितमाह्निके ॥ 313
1.m: The examination of eligibility, inner refinement, and the rite of the balance-scale: / this whole subject matter is in the twentieth daily lesson.

1.s:
mṛtajīvadvidhirjālo padeśaḥ saṃskriyāgaṇaḥ /
balābalavicāraścetyekaviṃśāhnike vidhiḥ // 314
1.d:
मृतजीवद्विधिर्जालो पदेशः संस्क्रियागणः ।
बलाबलविचारश्चेत्येकविंशाह्निके विधिः ॥ 314
1.m: The rite for the dead and the living, the transmission across lineages, the group of consecrations, / and the investigation of relative strength: this is the rule in the twenty-first daily lesson.

1.s:
śravaṇaṃ cābhyanujñānaṃ śodhanaṃ pātakacyutiḥ /
śaṅkāccheda iti spaṣṭaṃ vācyaṃ liṅgoddhṛtikrame // 315
1.d:
श्रवणं चाभ्यनुज्ञानं शोधनं पातकच्युतिः ।
शङ्काच्छेद इति स्पष्टं वाच्यं लिङ्गोद्धृतिक्रमे ॥ 315
1.m: Hearing, formal permission, purification, the falling away of sin, / and the severing of doubt: this is the explicit subject matter in the sequence of the removal of the linga.

1.s:
parīkṣācāryakaraṇaṃ tadvrataṃ haraṇaṃ mateḥ /
tadvibhāgaḥ sādhakatvamabhiṣekavidhau tviyat // 316
1.d:
परीक्षाचार्यकरणं तद्व्रतं हरणं मतेः ।
तद्विभागः साधकत्वमभिषेकविधौ त्वियत् ॥ 316
1.m: Examination, making an ācārya, his vow, the taking away of mental disposition, / its division, and the status of an adept: this much is in the rite of consecration.

1.s:
adhikāryatha saṃskārastatprayojanamityadaḥ /
caturviṃśe'ntyayāgākhye vaktavyaṃ paricarcyate // 317
1.d:
अधिकार्यथ संस्कारस्तत्प्रयोजनमित्यदः ।
चतुर्विंशेऽन्त्ययागाख्ये वक्तव्यं परिचर्च्यते ॥ 317
1.m: The eligible person, the consecration, and its purpose: this / subject matter to be stated is thoroughly examined in the twenty-fourth [daily lesson], named the final sacrifice.

1.s:
prayojanaṃ bhogamokṣadānenātra vidhiḥ sphuṭaḥ /
pañcaviṃśāhnike śrāddhaprakāśe vastusaṃgrahaḥ // 318
1.d:
प्रयोजनं भोगमोक्षदानेनात्र विधिः स्फुटः ।
पञ्चविंशाह्निके श्राद्धप्रकाशे वस्तुसंग्रहः ॥ 318
1.m: The purpose is clear here in the rite by the granting of enjoyment and liberation: / in the twenty-fifth daily lesson, which clarifies ancestor-offerings, there is the summary of topics.

1.s:
prayojanaṃ śeṣavṛtternityārcā sthaṇḍile parā /
liṅgasvarūpaṃ bahudhā cākṣasūtranirūpaṇam // 319
1.d:
प्रयोजनं शेषवृत्तेर्नित्यार्चा स्थण्डिले परा ।
लिङ्गस्वरूपं बहुधा चाक्षसूत्रनिरूपणम् ॥ 319
1.m: The purpose of post-initiatory conduct, the highest regular worship on an altar, / the nature of the linga in many ways, the description of the rosary,

1.s:
pūjābheda iti vācyaṃ liṅgārcāsaṃprakāśane /
naimittikavibhāgastatprayojanavidhistataḥ // 320
1.d:
पूजाभेद इति वाच्यं लिङ्गार्चासंप्रकाशने ।
नैमित्तिकविभागस्तत्प्रयोजनविधिस्ततः ॥ 320
1.m: and the varieties of worship: this is the subject matter in the elucidation of linga-worship. / Next, the division of occasional rites and the rule of their purpose;

1.s:
parvabhedāstadviśeṣaścakracarcā tadarcanam /
gurvādyantadinādyarcāprayojananirūpaṇam // 321
1.d:
पर्वभेदास्तद्विशेषश्चक्रचर्चा तदर्चनम् ।
गुर्वाद्यन्तदिनाद्यर्चाप्रयोजननिरूपणम् ॥ 321
1.m:
The divisions of holy occasions and their specific rules, deliberation on the cakra and its worship,
the purpose and determination of worship beginning on the day of the guru's origin and end; // 321

1.s:
mṛteḥ parīkṣā yogīśīmelakādividhistathā /
vyākhyāvidhiḥ śrutavidhirgurupūjāvidhistviyat // 322
1.d:
मृतेः परीक्षा योगीशीमेलकादिविधिस्तथा ।
व्याख्याविधिः श्रुतविधिर्गुरुपूजाविधिस्त्वियत् ॥ 322
1.m:
The testing of death, the rule of the confluence of the mistresses of yoga and the like,
the rule for exposition, the rule for hearing, and the rule for worshipping the guru—this much // 322

1.s:
naimittikaprakāśākhye 'pyaṣṭāviṃśāhnike sthitam /
adhikāryātmano bhedaḥ siddhapatnīkulakramaḥ // 323
1.d:
नैमित्तिकप्रकाशाख्ये ऽप्यष्टाविंशाह्निके स्थितम् ।
अधिकार्यात्मनो भेदः सिद्धपत्नीकुलक्रमः ॥ 323
1.m:
is established in the twenty-eighth daily lesson, named the exposition of occasional rites.
The division of eligible persons, the lineage tradition of the wives of the Siddhas, // 323

1.s:
arcāvidhirdautavidhī rahasyopaniṣatkramaḥ /
dīkṣābhiṣekau bodhaścetyekonatriṃśa āhnike // 324
1.d:
अर्चाविधिर्दौतविधी रहस्योपनिषत्क्रमः ।
दीक्षाभिषेकौ बोधश्चेत्येकोनत्रिंश आह्निके ॥ 324
1.m:
the rite of worship, the rites concerning the female messenger, the transmission of the secret Upanisad,
initiation, consecration, and awakening: in the twenty-ninth daily lesson. // 324

1.s:
mantrasvarūpaṃ tadvīryamiti triṃśe nirūpitam /
śūlābjabhedo vyomaśasvastikādinirūpaṇam // 325
1.d:
मन्त्रस्वरूपं तद्वीर्यमिति त्रिंशे निरूपितम् ।
शूलाब्जभेदो व्योमशस्वस्तिकादिनिरूपणम् ॥ 325
1.m:
The true nature of mantra and its potency is set forth in the thirtieth.
The varieties of the trident-lotus mandala, the determination of the vyoma, the svastika, and the rest // 325

1.s:
vistareṇābhidhātavyamityekatriṃśa āhnike /
guṇapradhānatābhedāḥ svarūpaṃ vīryacarcanam // 326
1.d:
विस्तरेणाभिधातव्यमित्येकत्रिंश आह्निके ।
गुणप्रधानताभेदाः स्वरूपं वीर्यचर्चनम् ॥ 326
1.m:
are to be explained at length in the thirty-first daily lesson.
The divisions of secondary and primary, intrinsic nature, the examination of potency, // 326

1.s:
kalābheda iti proktaṃ mudrāṇāṃ saṃprakāśane /
dvātriṃśatattvādīśākhyātprabhṛti prasphuṭo yataḥ // 327
1.d:
कलाभेद इति प्रोक्तं मुद्राणां संप्रकाशने ।
द्वात्रिंशतत्त्वादीशाख्यात्प्रभृति प्रस्फुटो यतः ॥ 327
1.m:
and the variety of elements are stated in the exposition of mudras.
Because beginning from the thirty-second [daily lesson] up to the one called the Lord, it is clearly evident // 327

1.s:
na bhedo'sti tato noktamuddeśāntaramatra tat /
mukhyatvena ca vedyatvādadhikārāntarakramaḥ // 328
1.d:
न भेदोऽस्ति ततो नोक्तमुद्देशान्तरमत्र तत् ।
मुख्यत्वेन च वेद्यत्वादधिकारान्तरक्रमः ॥ 328
1.m:
that there is no difference [of doctrine], another enumeration is therefore not stated here;
and because it is primarily to be known, the sequence of further eligibility [is omitted]. // 328

1.s:
ityuddeśavidhiḥ proktaḥ sukhasaṃgrahahetave /
athāsya lakṣaṇāvekṣe nirūpyete yathākramam // 329
1.d:
इत्युद्देशविधिः प्रोक्तः सुखसंग्रहहेतवे ।
अथास्य लक्षणावेक्षे निरूप्येते यथाक्रमम् ॥ 329
1.m:
Thus the rule of enumeration has been stated for the sake of easy comprehension.
Now its definition and examination are set forth in due order: // 329

1.s:
ātmā saṃvitprakāśasthitiranavayavā saṃvidityāttaśaktivrātaṃ tasya svarūpaṃ sa ca nija mahasaśchādanādbaddharūpaḥ /
ātmajyotiḥsvabhāvaprakaṭanavidhinā tasya mokṣaḥ sa cāyaṃ citrākārasya citraḥ prakaṭita iha yatsaṃgraheṇārtha eṣaḥ // 330
1.d:
आत्मा संवित्प्रकाशस्थितिरनवयवा संविदित्यात्तशक्तिव्रातं तस्य स्वरूपं स च निज महसश्छादनाद्बद्धरूपः ।
आत्मज्योतिःस्वभावप्रकटनविधिना तस्य मोक्षः स चायं चित्राकारस्य चित्रः प्रकटित इह यत्संग्रहेणार्थ एषः ॥ 330
1.m:
The self is consciousness; the status of luminosity is undivided consciousness—thus its essential nature consists of an assemblage of assumed powers, and, due to concealing its own splendour, it assumes the form of the bound soul;
its liberation occurs by means of the manifestation of the nature of the self's light, and this [liberation] of the multiform one is multiform; because this entire teaching has been set forth here in summary. // 330

1.s:
mithyājñānaṃ timiramasamān dṛṣṭidoṣānprasūte tatsadbhāvādvimalamapi tadbhāti mālinyadhāma /
yattu prekṣyaṃ dṛśi parigataṃ taimirīṃ doṣamudrāṃ dūraṃ runddhetprabhavatu kathaṃ tatra mālinyaśaṅkā // 331
1.d:
मिथ्याज्ञानं तिमिरमसमान् दृष्टिदोषान्प्रसूते तत्सद्भावाद्विमलमपि तद्भाति मालिन्यधाम ।
यत्तु प्रेक्ष्यं दृशि परिगतं तैमिरीं दोषमुद्रां दूरं रुन्द्धेत्प्रभवतु कथं तत्र मालिन्यशङ्का ॥ 331
1.m:
False knowledge is darkness; it produces unequalled defects of vision; due to its presence, even that which is immaculate appears as an abode of impurity;
but as for that which is to be seen: when it is grasped in vision, it dispels from afar the seal of defective cataract—how could a suspicion of impurity have power there? // 331

1.s:
bhāvavrāta? haṭhājjanasya hṛdayānyākramya yannartayan bhaṅgībhirvividhābhirātmahṛdayaṃ pracchādya saṃkrīḍase /
yastvāmāha jaḍaṃ jaḍaḥ sahṛdayaṃmanyatvaduḥśikṣito manye'muṣya jaḍātmatā stutipadaṃ tvatsāmyasaṃbhāvanāt // 332
1.d:
भावव्रात? हठाज्जनस्य हृदयान्याक्रम्य यन्नर्तयन् भङ्गीभिर्विविधाभिरात्महृदयं प्रच्छाद्य संक्रीडसे ।
यस्त्वामाह जडं जडः सहृदयंमन्यत्वदुःशिक्षितो मन्येऽमुष्य जडात्मता स्तुतिपदं त्वत्साम्यसंभावनात् ॥ 332
1.m:
O assemblage of entities! Forcibly seizing the hearts of people, you play, setting them dancing with various turns, while concealing your own heart.
Whoever, dull-witted and ill-instructed by pretending to be sensitive, calls you dull-witted—I consider that his dull-wittedness is a locus of praise, since it conceives an equality with you! // 332

1.s:
iha galitamalāḥ parāvarajñāḥ śivasadbhāvamayā adhikriyante /
guravaḥ pravicāraṇe yatastadviphalā dveṣakalaṃkahāniyācñā // 333
1.d:
इह गलितमलाः परावरज्ञाः शिवसद्भावमया अधिक्रियन्ते ।
गुरवः प्रविचारणे यतस्तद्विफला द्वेषकलंकहानियाच्ञा ॥ 333
1.m:
Here, gurus whose impurities have fallen away, who know the higher and lower, and who are composed of the true reality of Siva, are authoritative
in critical examination; for that reason, a plea for the removal of the stain of malice is useless. // 333

2.s:
yattatrādyaṃ padamaviratānuttarajñaptirūpaṃ /
tannirṇetuṃ prakaraṇamidamārabhe'haṃ dvitīyam // 1
2.d:
यत्तत्राद्यं पदमविरतानुत्तरज्ञप्तिरूपं ।
तन्निर्णेतुं प्रकरणमिदमारभेऽहं द्वितीयम् ॥ 1
2.m:
That primal state which consists of uninterrupted, unexcelled knowledge—
in order to determine that, I begin this second chapter. // 1

2.s:
anupāyaṃ hi yadrūpaṃ ko'rtho deśanayātra vai /
sakṛtsyāddeśanā paścādanupāyatvamucyayate // 2
2.d:
अनुपायं हि यद्रूपं कोऽर्थो देशनयात्र वै ।
सकृत्स्याद्देशना पश्चादनुपायत्वमुच्ययते ॥ 2
2.m:
Indeed, what purpose is there in teaching with regard to that form which is without means?
Teaching might occur once; subsequently, [the condition of] being without means is stated. // 2

2.s:
anupāyamidaṃ tattvamityupāyaṃ vinā kutaḥ /
svayaṃ tu teṣāṃ tattādṛk kiṃ brūmaḥ kila tānprati // 3
2.d:
अनुपायमिदं तत्त्वमित्युपायं विना कुतः ।
स्वयं तु तेषां तत्तादृक् किं ब्रूमः किल तान्प्रति ॥ 3
2.m:
'This reality is without means'—how [could this be known] without a means?
Yet for them it is naturally like that; what, indeed, can we say to them? // 3

2.s:
yaccaturdhoditaṃ rūpaṃ vijñānasya vibhorasau /
svabhāva eva mantavyaḥ sa hi nityodito vibhuḥ // 4
2.d:
यच्चतुर्धोदितं रूपं विज्ञानस्य विभोरसौ ।
स्वभाव एव मन्तव्यः स हि नित्योदितो विभुः ॥ 4
2.m:
That fourfold form of consciousness which has been declared should be considered
as the very nature of the all-pervading Lord, for the all-pervading Lord is eternally arisen. // 4

2.s:
etāvadbhirasaṃkhyātaiḥ svabhāvairyatprakāśate /
ke'pyaṃśāṃśikayā tena viśantyanye niraṃśataḥ // 5
2.d:
एतावद्भिरसंख्यातैः स्वभावैर्यत्प्रकाशते ।
केऽप्यंशांशिकया तेन विशन्त्यन्ये निरंशतः ॥ 5
2.m:
Since it shines with so many innumerable natures,
some enter [it] part by part, while others enter it without parts. // 5

2.s:
tatrāpi cābhyupāyādisāpekṣānyatvayogataḥ /
upāyasyāpi no vāryā tadanyatvādvicitratā // 6
2.d:
तत्रापि चाभ्युपायादिसापेक्षान्यत्वयोगतः ।
उपायस्यापि नो वार्या तदन्यत्वाद्विचित्रता ॥ 6
2.m:
There too, because of the connection with otherness dependent on means and the like,
the multiplicity even of the means cannot be denied, on account of difference from that [goal]. // 6

2.s:
tatra ye nirmalātmāno bhairavīyāṃ svasaṃvidam /
nirupāyāmupāsīnāstadvidhiḥ praṇigadyate // 7
2.d:
तत्र ये निर्मलात्मानो भैरवीयां स्वसंविदम् ।
निरुपायामुपासीनास्तद्विधिः प्रणिगद्यते ॥ 7
2.m:
Among them, for those immaculate souls who attend to their own consciousness
pertaining to Bhairava, which is without means, the method is now fully declared. // 7

2.s:
tatra tāvatkriyāyogo nābhyupāyatvamarhati /
sa hi tasmātsamudbhūtaḥ pratyuta pravibhāvyate // 8
2.d:
तत्र तावत्क्रियायोगो नाभ्युपायत्वमर्हति ।
स हि तस्मात्समुद्भूतः प्रत्युत प्रविभाव्यते ॥ 8
2.m:
In that regard, the application of action does not deserve to be an approach;
for it is, on the contrary, clearly perceived as having arisen from that [consciousness]. // 8

2.s:
jñaptāvupāya eva syāditi cejjñaptirucyate /
prakāśatvaṃ svaprakāśe tacca tatrānyataḥ katham // 9
2.d:
ज्ञप्तावुपाय एव स्यादिति चेज्ज्ञप्तिरुच्यते ।
प्रकाशत्वं स्वप्रकाशे तच्च तत्रान्यतः कथम् ॥ 9
2.m:
If it is said: 'A means could indeed apply in cognition,' cognition is declared
to be luminous; and in that which is self-luminous, how could that [luminosity] come from another? // 9

2.s:
saṃvittattvaṃ svaprakāśamityasminkaṃ nu yuktibhiḥ /
tadabhāve bhavedviśvaṃ jaḍatvādaprakāśakam // 10
2.d:
संवित्तत्त्वं स्वप्रकाशमित्यस्मिन्कं नु युक्तिभिः ।
तदभावे भवेद्विश्वं जडत्वादप्रकाशकम् ॥ 10
2.m:
The reality of consciousness is self-luminous—what [other] thing could one establish in this regard by logical arguments?
In its absence, the universe would be unilluminating, because of its insentience. // 10

2.s:
yāvānupāyo bāhyaḥ syādāntaro vāpi kaścana /
sa sarvastanmukhaprekṣī tatropāyatvabhākkatham // 11
2.d:
यावानुपायो बाह्यः स्यादान्तरो वापि कश्चन ।
स सर्वस्तन्मुखप्रेक्षी तत्रोपायत्वभाक्कथम् ॥ 11
2.m:
Whatever means there might be, external or internal,
every one of them looks to the face of that [consciousness]; how could it possess the quality of being a means toward that? // 11

2.s:
tyajāvadhānāni nanu kva nāma dhatse'vadhānaṃ vicinu svayaṃ tat /
pūrṇe'vadhānaṃ na hi nāma yuktaṃ nāpūrṇamabhyeti ca satyabhāvam // 12
2.d:
त्यजावधानानि ननु क्व नाम धत्सेऽवधानं विचिनु स्वयं तत् ।
पूर्णेऽवधानं न हि नाम युक्तं नापूर्णमभ्येति च सत्यभावम् ॥ 12
2.m:
Abandon acts of attention! Where, pray, do you place your attention? Examine that for yourself:
attention to the full is not appropriate, nor does that which is not full attain real existence. // 12

2.s:
tenāvadhānaprāṇasya bhāvanādeḥ pare pathi /
bhairavīye kathaṃkāraṃ bhavetsākṣādupāyatā // 13
2.d:
तेनावधानप्राणस्य भावनादेः परे पथि ।
भैरवीये कथंकारं भवेत्साक्षादुपायता ॥ 13
2.m:
Therefore, on the supreme path of Bhairava, how could contemplation and the like,
whose very life is attention, directly have the quality of being a means? // 13

2.s:
ye'pi sākṣādupāyena tadrūpaṃ praviviñcate /
nūnaṃ te sūryasaṃvittyai khadyotādhitsavo jaḍāḥ // 14
2.d:
येऽपि साक्षादुपायेन तद्रूपं प्रविविञ्चते ।
नूनं ते सूर्यसंवित्त्यै खद्योताधित्सवो जडाः ॥ 14
2.m:
Those who would discern that nature directly through a means
are surely dull fools wishing to set up a firefly to perceive the sun. // 14

2.s:
kiṃ ca yāvadidaṃ bāhyamāntaropāyasaṃmatam /
tatprakāśātmatāmātraṃ śivasyaiva nijaṃ vapuḥ // 15
2.d:
किं च यावदिदं बाह्यमान्तरोपायसंमतम् ।
तत्प्रकाशात्मतामात्रं शिवस्यैव निजं वपुः ॥ 15
2.m:
Moreover, all this which is accepted as an external or internal means
is merely the state of luminosity, the very body of Siva. // 15

2.s:
nīlaṃ pītaṃ sukhamiti prakāśaḥ kevalaḥ śivaḥ /
amuṣminparamādvaite prakāśātmani ko'paraḥ // 16
2.d:
नीलं पीतं सुखमिति प्रकाशः केवलः शिवः ।
अमुष्मिन्परमाद्वैते प्रकाशात्मनि कोऽपरः ॥ 16
2.m:
Blue, yellow, pleasure: this is pure luminosity, Siva.
In this supreme non-duality consisting of luminosity, what other [thing] could there be? // 16

2.s: upāyopeyabhāvaḥ syātprakāśaḥ kevalaṃ hi saḥ // 17
2.d: उपायोपेयभावः स्यात्प्रकाशः केवलं हि सः ॥ 17
2.m: How could there be the relation of means and end? For it is pure luminosity. // 17

2.s:
idaṃ dvaitama'yaṃ bheda idamadvaitamityapi /
prakāśavapurevāyaṃ bhāsate parameśvaraḥ // 18
2.d:
इदं द्वैतमऽयं भेद इदमद्वैतमित्यपि ।
प्रकाशवपुरेवायं भासते परमेश्वरः ॥ 18
2.m:
Even as 'this is duality', 'this is difference', 'this is non-duality',
this supreme Lord shines solely as the form of luminosity. // 18

2.s:
asyāṃ bhūmau sukhaṃ duḥkhaṃ bandho mokṣaścitarjaḍaḥ /
ghaṭakumbhavadekārthāḥ śabdāste'pyekameva ca // 19
2.d:
अस्यां भूमौ सुखं दुःखं बन्धो मोक्षश्चितर्जडः ।
घटकुम्भवदेकार्थाः शब्दास्तेऽप्येकमेव च ॥ 19
2.m:
On this level, pleasure, pain, bondage, liberation, conscious and insentient
are words with a single referent, like 'pot' and 'pitcher'; and they are only one. // 19

2.s:
praśāśe hyaprakāśāṃśaḥ kathaṃ nāma prakāśatām /
prakāśamāne tasminvā taddvaitāstasya lopitāḥ // 20
2.d:
प्रशाशे ह्यप्रकाशांशः कथं नाम प्रकाशताम् ।
प्रकाशमाने तस्मिन्वा तद्द्वैतास्तस्य लोपिताः ॥ 20
2.m:
Indeed, how could a portion of non-luminosity shine in luminosity?
Or, if it does shine, its duality is destroyed. // 20

2.s:
aprakāśe'tha tasminvā vastutā kathamucyate /
na prakāśaviśeṣatvamata evopapadyate // 21
2.d:
अप्रकाशेऽथ तस्मिन्वा वस्तुता कथमुच्यते ।
न प्रकाशविशेषत्वमत एवोपपद्यते ॥ 21
2.m:
Or, if it is non-luminous, how can substantial reality be attributed to it?
For this very reason, a differentiation of luminosity is not tenable. // 21

2.s:
ata ekaprakāśo'yamiti vāde'tra susthite /
dūrādāvāritāḥ satyaṃ vibhinnajñānavādinaḥ // 22
2.d:
अत एकप्रकाशोऽयमिति वादेऽत्र सुस्थिते ।
दूरादावारिताः सत्यं विभिन्नज्ञानवादिनः ॥ 22
2.m:
Therefore, once this doctrine that 'luminosity is one' is firmly established,
those who advocate differentiated cognitions are truly repelled from afar. // 22

2.s:
prakāśamātramuditamaprakāśaniṣedhanāt /
ekaśabdasya na tvarthaḥ saṃkhyā cidvyaktibhedabhāk // 23
2.d:
प्रकाशमात्रमुदितमप्रकाशनिषेधनात् ।
एकशब्दस्य न त्वर्थः संख्या चिद्व्यक्तिभेदभाक् ॥ 23
2.m:
Mere luminosity is proclaimed, because of the negation of non-luminosity;
but the meaning of the word 'one' is not a number involving divisions of individual consciousnesses. // 23

2.s:
naiṣa śaktirmahādevī na paratrāśrito yataḥ /
na caiṣa śaktimāndevo na kasyāpyāśrayo yataḥ // 24
2.d:
नैष शक्तिर्महादेवी न परत्राश्रितो यतः ।
न चैष शक्तिमान्देवो न कस्याप्याश्रयो यतः ॥ 24
2.m:
This is not power, the Great Goddess, because it is not resting upon another;
nor is this the Lord who possesses power, because he is not the resting place of anything. // 24

2.s:
naiṣa dhyeyo dhyātrabhāvānna dhyātā dhyeyavarjanāt /
na pūjyaḥ pūjakābhāvātpūjyābhāvānna pūjakaḥ // 25
2.d:
नैष ध्येयो ध्यात्रभावान्न ध्याता ध्येयवर्जनात् ।
न पूज्यः पूजकाभावात्पूज्याभावान्न पूजकः ॥ 25
2.m:
This is not the object of meditation, due to the absence of a meditator; nor is it the meditator, due to the exclusion of an object of meditation;
it is not the object of worship, due to the absence of a worshipper; nor is it the worshipper, due to the absence of an object of worship. // 25

2.s:
na mantro na ca mantryo'sau na ca mantrayitā prabhuḥ /
na dīkṣā dīkṣako vāpi na dīkṣāvānmaheśvaraḥ // 26
2.d:
न मन्त्रो न च मन्त्र्योऽसौ न च मन्त्रयिता प्रभुः ।
न दीक्षा दीक्षको वापि न दीक्षावान्महेश्वरः ॥ 26
2.m:
The Sovereign is neither the mantra, nor the deity invoked by mantra, nor the reciter of mantra;
nor is the Great Lord initiation, the initiator, or the initiated. // 26

2.s:
sthānāsananirodhārghasaṃghānāvāhanādikam /
visarjanāntaṃ nāstyatra kartṛkarmakriyojjhite // 27
2.d:
स्थानासननिरोधार्घसंघानावाहनादिकम् ।
विसर्जनान्तं नास्त्यत्र कर्तृकर्मक्रियोज्झिते ॥ 27
2.m:
Place, seat, restraint, the collection of oblations, invocation, and the like,
ending with dismissal, do not exist here, where agent, object, and action are abandoned. // 27

2.s:
na sanna cāsatsadasanna ca tannobhayojjhitam /
durvijñeyā hi sāvasthā kimapyetadanuttaram // 28
2.d:
न सन्न चासत्सदसन्न च तन्नोभयोज्झितम् ।
दुर्विज्ञेया हि सावस्था किमप्येतदनुत्तरम् ॥ 28
2.m:
It is neither existent nor non-existent, nor existent-and-non-existent, nor devoid of both;
for that state is difficult to discern, an indescribable unexcelled reality. // 28

2.s:
ayamityavabhāso hi yo bhāvo'vacchidātmakaḥ /
sa eva ghaṭavalloke saṃstathā naiṣa bhairavaḥ // 29
2.d:
अयमित्यवभासो हि यो भावोऽवच्छिदात्मकः ।
स एव घटवल्लोके संस्तथा नैष भैरवः ॥ 29
2.m: For that manifestation which is [conceived as] 'this', being an entity whose nature is limited, / is existent in the world just like a pot; Bhairava is not like that.

2.s:
asattvaṃ cāprakāśatvaṃ na kutrāpyupayogitā /
viśvasya jīvitaṃ satyaṃ prakāśaikātmakaśca saḥ // 30
2.d:
असत्त्वं चाप्रकाशत्वं न कुत्राप्युपयोगिता ।
विश्वस्य जीवितं सत्यं प्रकाशैकात्मकश्च सः ॥ 30
2.m: Non-existence is non-luminosity, lacking efficacy anywhere; / but he is the true life of the universe, and his nature is solely luminosity.

2.s:
ābhyāmeva tu hetubhyāṃ na dvyātmā na dvayojjhitaḥ /
sarvātmanā hi bhātyeṣa kena rūpeṇa mantryatām // 31
2.d:
आभ्यामेव तु हेतुभ्यां न द्व्यात्मा न द्वयोज्झितः ।
सर्वात्मना हि भात्येष केन रूपेण मन्त्र्यताम् ॥ 31
2.m: For these two reasons, he is neither dual-natured nor free from duality; / for he shines as all things: in what form could he be formulated through mantra?

2.s:
śrīmattriśirasi proktaṃ parajñānasvarūpakam /
śaktyā garbhāntarvartinyā śaktigarbha paraṃ padam // 32
2.d:
श्रीमत्त्रिशिरसि प्रोक्तं परज्ञानस्वरूपकम् ।
शक्त्या गर्भान्तर्वर्तिन्या शक्तिगर्भ परं पदम् ॥ 32
2.m: It is stated in the venerable Triśiro[bhairava] that the essential nature of supreme knowledge, / through the power abiding within its womb, is the supreme state containing power within its womb:

2.s:
na bhāvo nāpyabhāvo na dvayaṃ vācāmagocarāt /
akathyapadavīrūḍhaṃ śaktisthaṃ śaktivarjitam // 33
2.d:
न भावो नाप्यभावो न द्वयं वाचामगोचरात् ।
अकथ्यपदवीरूढं शक्तिस्थं शक्तिवर्जितम् ॥ 33
2.m: "Neither entity nor non-entity, nor a pair, because it is beyond the range of words; / ascended to the ineffable realm, abiding in power, devoid of power."

2.s:
iti ye rūḍhasaṃvittiparamārthapavitritāḥ /
anuttarapathe rūḍhāste'bhyupāyāniyantritāḥ // 34
2.d:
इति ये रूढसंवित्तिपरमार्थपवित्रिताः ।
अनुत्तरपथे रूढास्तेऽभ्युपायानियन्त्रिताः ॥ 34
2.m: Thus, those who are purified by the supreme reality of firmly established consciousness, / who have ascended to the path of the unexcelled, are unrestricted by means.

2.s:
teṣāmidaṃ samābhāti sarvato bhāvamaṇḍalam /
puraḥsthameva saṃvittibhairavāgnivilāpitam // 35
2.d:
तेषामिदं समाभाति सर्वतो भावमण्डलम् ।
पुरःस्थमेव संवित्तिभैरवाग्निविलापितम् ॥ 35
2.m: To them this entire sphere of entities shines forth from all sides, / right before them, dissolved in the fire of Bhairava-consciousness.

2.s:
eteṣāṃ sukhaduḥkhāṃśaśaṃkātaṃkavikalpanāḥ /
nirvikalpaparāveśamātraśeṣatvamāgatāḥ // 36
2.d:
एतेषां सुखदुःखांशशंकातंकविकल्पनाः ।
निर्विकल्पपरावेशमात्रशेषत्वमागताः ॥ 36
2.m: Their conceptual constructs consisting in portions of pleasure, pain, doubt, and distress / have come to have as their sole remainder immersion in the supreme non-conceptual state.

2.s:
eṣāṃ na mantro na dhyānaṃ na pūjā nāpi kalpanā /
na samayyādikācāryaparyantaḥ ko'pi viśramaḥ // 37
2.d:
एषां न मन्त्रो न ध्यानं न पूजा नापि कल्पना ।
न समय्यादिकाचार्यपर्यन्तः कोऽपि विश्रमः ॥ 37
2.m: For them there is no mantra, no meditation, no worship, nor any conceptualisation; / no resting-place whatsoever from the initiate into the rule up to the master.

2.s:
samastayantraṇātantratroṭanāṭaṃkadharmiṇaḥ /
nānugrahātparaṃ kiṃciccheṣavṛttau prayojanam // 38
2.d:
समस्तयन्त्रणातन्त्रत्रोटनाटंकधर्मिणः ।
नानुग्रहात्परं किंचिच्छेषवृत्तौ प्रयोजनम् ॥ 38
2.m: Having the nature of destroying the fear that breaks the web of all constraints, / there is no purpose in their remaining life other than grace.

2.s:
svaṃ kartavyaṃ kimapi kalayaṃlloka eṣa prayatnānno pārārthyaṃ prati ghaṭayate kāṃcana svapravṛttim /
yastu dhvastākhilabhavamalo bhairavībhāvapūrṇaḥ kṛtyaṃ tasya sphuṭamidamiyallokakartavyamātram // 39
2.d:
स्वं कर्तव्यं किमपि कलयंल्लोक एष प्रयत्नान्नो पारार्थ्यं प्रति घटयते कांचन स्वप्रवृत्तिम् ।
यस्तु ध्वस्ताखिलभवमलो भैरवीभावपूर्णः कृत्यं तस्य स्फुटमिदमियल्लोककर्तव्यमात्रम् ॥ 39
2.m: Considering some duty of his own, this worldly person exerts himself and never engages in any activity for the sake of others; / but for him whose worldly impurities are all destroyed and who is full of the state of Bhairava, his clear duty is only this much: worldly duty [for others].

2.s:
taṃ ye paśyanti tādrūpyakrameṇāmalasaṃvidaḥ /
te'pi tadrūpiṇastāvatyevāsyānugrahātmatā // 40
2.d:
तं ये पश्यन्ति ताद्रूप्यक्रमेणामलसंविदः ।
तेऽपि तद्रूपिणस्तावत्येवास्यानुग्रहात्मता ॥ 40
2.m: Those whose consciousness is spotless, who see him in accordance with that nature, / they too assume that nature; his essence as grace extends precisely this far.

2.s:
etattattvaparijñānaṃ mukhyaṃ yāgādi kathyate /
dīkṣāntaṃ vibhunā śrīmatsiddhayogīśvarīmate // 41
2.d:
एतत्तत्त्वपरिज्ञानं मुख्यं यागादि कथ्यते ।
दीक्षान्तं विभुना श्रीमत्सिद्धयोगीश्वरीमते ॥ 41
2.m: This thorough comprehension of reality is taught by the all-pervading Lord in the venerable Siddhayogīśvarīmata / as the primary [practice], beginning with sacrificial worship and ending with initiation:

2.s:
sthaṇḍilāduttaraṃ tūraṃ tūrāduttarataḥ paṭaḥ /
paṭāddhyānaṃ tato dhyeyaṃ tataḥ syāddhāraṇottarā // 42
2.d:
स्थण्डिलादुत्तरं तूरं तूरादुत्तरतः पटः ।
पटाद्ध्यानं ततो ध्येयं ततः स्याद्धारणोत्तरा ॥ 42
2.m: "Higher than the bare ground is the altar; higher than the altar is the cloth; / higher than the cloth is meditation; higher than that is the object of meditation; higher than that is retention;

2.s:
tato'pi yogajaṃ rūpaṃ tato'pi jñānamuttaram /
jñānena hi mahāsiddho bhavedyogīśvarastviti // 43
2.d:
ततोऽपि योगजं रूपं ततोऽपि ज्ञानमुत्तरम् ।
ज्ञानेन हि महासिद्धो भवेद्योगीश्वरस्त्विति ॥ 43
2.m: higher than even that is the form born of yoga; higher than even that is knowledge; / for by knowledge the lord of yoga becomes a great adept."

2.s:
so'pi svātantryadhāmnā cedapyanirmalasaṃvidām /
anugrahaṃ cikīrṣustadbhāvinaṃ vidhimāśrayet // 44
2.d:
सोऽपि स्वातन्त्र्यधाम्ना चेदप्यनिर्मलसंविदाम् ।
अनुग्रहं चिकीर्षुस्तद्भाविनं विधिमाश्रयेत् ॥ 44
2.m: Even so, if by the power of his absolute autonomy he desires to bestow grace / upon those whose consciousness is not spotless, he may resort to the procedure that brings that about.

2.s:
anugrāhyānusāreṇa vicitraḥ sa ca kathyate /
parāparādyupāyaughasaṃkīrṇatvavibhedataḥ // 45
2.d:
अनुग्राह्यानुसारेण विचित्रः स च कथ्यते ।
परापराद्युपायौघसंकीर्णत्वविभेदतः ॥ 45
2.m: And that [procedure] is said to be manifold according to the recipient of grace, / through the division of mixture among the flood of supreme, non-supreme, and other means.

2.s:
tadarthameva cāsyāpi parameśvararūpiṇaḥ /
tadabhyupāyaśāstrādiśravaṇādhyayanādaraḥ // 46
2.d:
तदर्थमेव चास्यापि परमेश्वररूपिणः ।
तदभ्युपायशास्त्रादिश्रवणाध्ययनादरः ॥ 46
2.m: And for this reason alone, even for him who embodies the Supreme Lord, / there is regard for hearing, studying, and so forth the scriptures of those means.

2.s:
nahi tasya svatantrasya kāpi kutrāpi khaṇḍanā /
nānirmalacitaḥ puṃso'nugrahastvanupāyakaḥ // 47
2.d:
नहि तस्य स्वतन्त्रस्य कापि कुत्रापि खण्डना ।
नानिर्मलचितः पुंसोऽनुग्रहस्त्वनुपायकः ॥ 47
2.m: For there is no limitation anywhere for that autonomous one; / yet there is no grace without means for a person whose mind is not spotless.

2.s:
śrīmadūrmimahāśāstre siddhasaṃtānarūpake /
idamuktaṃ tathā śrīmatsomānandādidaiśikaiḥ // 48
2.d:
श्रीमदूर्मिमहाशास्त्रे सिद्धसंतानरूपके ।
इदमुक्तं तथा श्रीमत्सोमानन्दादिदैशिकैः ॥ 48
2.m: This was stated in the venerable Ūrmimahāśāstra, which embodies the lineage of the Siddhas, / and likewise by the teachers beginning with the venerable Somānanda:

2.s:
gurorvākyādyuktipracayaracanonmārjanavaśāt samāśvāsācchāstraṃ prati samuditādvāpi kathitāt /
vilīne śaṃkābhre tdṛdayagaganodbhāsimahasaḥ prabhoḥ sūryasyeva spṛśata caraṇāndhvāntajayinaḥ // 49
2.d:
गुरोर्वाक्याद्युक्तिप्रचयरचनोन्मार्जनवशात् समाश्वासाच्छास्त्रं प्रति समुदिताद्वापि कथितात् ।
विलीने शंकाभ्रे त्दृदयगगनोद्भासिमहसः प्रभोः सूर्यस्येव स्पृशत चरणान्ध्वान्तजयिनः ॥ 49
2.m: "Through the word of the guru, through the cleaning effect of composing a multitude of arguments, / or through the confidence arising from or stated in the scripture, / when the cloud of doubt has dissolved, touch the feet of the Lord, who, like the sun conquering darkness, / has his light shining in the sky of that heart."

2.s: idamanuttaradhāmavivecakaṃ vigalitaupayikaṃ kṛtamāhnikam // 50
2.d: इदमनुत्तरधामविवेचकं विगलितौपयिकं कृतमाह्निकम् ॥ 50
2.m:
This daily lesson, which investigates the unexcelled realm and in which means have dissolved, is concluded. // 50
Chapter 3: The third daily lesson of the Śrī Tantrāloka.

3.s: atha paraupayikaṃ praṇigadyate padamanuttarameva maheśituḥ //
3.d: अथ परौपयिकं प्रणिगद्यते पदमनुत्तरमेव महेशितुः ॥
3.m: Now the supreme unexcelled state of the Great Lord, which possesses supreme means, is proclaimed.

3.s:
prakāśamātraṃ yatproktaṃ bhairavīyaṃ paraṃ mahaḥ /
tatra svatantratāmātramadhikaṃ pravivicyate // 1
3.d:
प्रकाशमात्रं यत्प्रोक्तं भैरवीयं परं महः ।
तत्र स्वतन्त्रतामात्रमधिकं प्रविविच्यते ॥ 1
3.m: Regarding that supreme Bhairavian light which has been described as pure luminosity, / its aspect of absolute autonomy alone is now further examined.

3.s:
yaḥ prakāśaḥ sa sarvasya prakāśatvaṃ prayacchati /
na ca tadvyatirekyasti viśvaṃ sadvāvabhāsate // 2
3.d:
यः प्रकाशः स सर्वस्य प्रकाशत्वं प्रयच्छति ।
न च तद्व्यतिरेक्यस्ति विश्वं सद्वावभासते ॥ 2
3.m: The luminosity that is, grants luminosity to everything; / nor does the universe exist or appear distinct from it.

3.s:
ato'sau parameśānaḥ svātmavyomanyanargalaḥ /
iyataḥ sṛṣṭisaṃhārāḍambarasya pradarśakaḥ // 3
3.d:
अतोऽसौ परमेशानः स्वात्मव्योमन्यनर्गलः ।
इयतः सृष्टिसंहाराडम्बरस्य प्रदर्शकः ॥ 3
3.m: Therefore, this Supreme Lord, unimpeded in the space of his own self, / displays the spectacle of this extent of creation and dissolution.

3.s:
nirmale makure yadvadbhānti bhūmijalādayaḥ /
amiśrāstadvadekasmiṃścinnāthe viśvavṛttayaḥ // 4
3.d:
निर्मले मकुरे यद्वद्भान्ति भूमिजलादयः ।
अमिश्रास्तद्वदेकस्मिंश्चिन्नाथे विश्ववृत्तयः ॥ 4
3.m: Just as earth, water, and other [reflections] appear unmixed in a spotless mirror, / so do the states of the universe [appear] in the single Lord of Consciousness.

3.s:
sadṛśaṃ bhāti nayanadarpaṇāmbaravāriṣu /
tathā hi nirmale rūpe rūpamevāvabhāsate // 5
3.d:
सदृशं भाति नयनदर्पणाम्बरवारिषु ।
तथा हि निर्मले रूपे रूपमेवावभासते ॥ 5
3.m: A similar [reflection] appears in the eye, in a mirror, in the sky, and in water; / for indeed, in a pure form only form is manifested.

3.s:
pracchannarāgiṇī kāntapratibimbitasundaram /
darpaṇaṃ kucakumbhābhyāṃ spṛśantyapi na tṛpyati // 6
3.d:
प्रच्छन्नरागिणी कान्तप्रतिबिम्बितसुन्दरम् ।
दर्पणं कुचकुम्भाभ्यां स्पृशन्त्यपि न तृप्यति ॥ 6
3.m: A woman concealing her passion, even while touching with her pitcher-like breasts / a mirror beautified by the reflection of her lover, is not satisfied.

3.s:
na hi sparśo'sya vimalo rūpameva tathā yataḥ /
nairmalyaṃ cātiniviḍasajātīyaikasaṃgatiḥ // 7
3.d:
न हि स्पर्शोऽस्य विमलो रूपमेव तथा यतः ।
नैर्मल्यं चातिनिविडसजातीयैकसंगतिः ॥ 7
3.m: For its touch is not pure, whereas its visual form is such; / and purity is the extremely dense unification of homogeneous things.

3.s:
svasminnabhedādbhinnasya darśanakṣamataiva yā /
atyaktasvaprakāśasya nairmalyaṃ tadgurūditam // 8
3.d:
स्वस्मिन्नभेदाद्भिन्नस्य दर्शनक्षमतैव या ।
अत्यक्तस्वप्रकाशस्य नैर्मल्यं तद्गुरूदितम् ॥ 8
3.m: That capacity to reveal what is distinct within oneself without difference, / while not abandoning one's own luminosity, is called purity by the guru.

3.s:
nairmalyaṃ mukhyamekasya saṃvinnāthasya sarvataḥ /
aṃśāṃśikātaḥ kvāpyanyadvimalaṃ tattadicchayā // 9
3.d:
नैर्मल्यं मुख्यमेकस्य संविन्नाथस्य सर्वतः ।
अंशांशिकातः क्वाप्यन्यद्विमलं तत्तदिच्छया ॥ 9
3.m: Purity belongs primarily to the single Lord of Consciousness universally; / anything else is pure in a partial degree here and there by his will.

3.s:
bhāvānāṃ yatpratīghāti vapurmāyātmakaṃ hi tat /
teṣāmevāsti sadvidyāmayaṃ tvapratighātakam // 10
3.d:
भावानां यत्प्रतीघाति वपुर्मायात्मकं हि तत् ।
तेषामेवास्ति सद्विद्यामयं त्वप्रतिघातकम् ॥ 10
3.m: That body of entities which is obstructive is indeed of the nature of māyā; / but of those very entities there is [another body] composed of pure knowledge, which is unobstructed.

3.s:
tadevamubhayākāramavabhāsaṃ prakāśayan /
vibhāti varado bimbapratibimbadṛśākhile // 11
3.d:
तदेवमुभयाकारमवभासं प्रकाशयन् ।
विभाति वरदो बिम्बप्रतिबिम्बदृशाखिले ॥ 11
3.m: Thus, illuminating this manifestation of twofold form, / the boon-giver shines in the whole through the perspective of original and reflection.

3.s:
yastvāha netratejāṃsi svacchātpratiphalantyalam /
viparyasya svakaṃ vaktraṃ gṛhṇantīti sa pṛcchyate // 12
3.d:
यस्त्वाह नेत्रतेजांसि स्वच्छात्प्रतिफलन्त्यलम् ।
विपर्यस्य स्वकं वक्त्रं गृह्णन्तीति स पृच्छ्यते ॥ 12
3.m: Now, he who says: 'The rays of light from the eye reflect fully from a clear [surface], / and, reversing, apprehend one's own face'—he is asked:

3.s:
dehādanyatra yattejastadadhiṣṭhāturātmanaḥ /
tenaiva tejasā jñatve ko'rthaḥ syāddarpaṇena tu // 13
3.d:
देहादन्यत्र यत्तेजस्तदधिष्ठातुरात्मनः ।
तेनैव तेजसा ज्ञत्वे कोऽर्थः स्याद्दर्पणेन तु ॥ 13
3.m: "The light which is elsewhere than the body belongs to the self that presides over it; / if knowing occurs through that light itself, what purpose would there be for a mirror?

3.s:
viparyastaistu tejobhirgrāhakātmatvamāgataiḥ /
rūpaṃ dṛśyeta vadane nije na makurāntare // 14
3.d:
विपर्यस्तैस्तु तेजोभिर्ग्राहकात्मत्वमागतैः ।
रूपं दृश्येत वदने निजे न मकुरान्तरे ॥ 14
3.m: And if the rays, reversed, become the apprehender, / the visual form would be seen on one's own face, not inside the mirror.

3.s:
svamukhe sparśavaccaitadrūpaṃ bhāyānmametyalam /
na tvasya spṛśyabhinnasya vedyaikāntasvarūpiṇaḥ // 15
3.d:
स्वमुखे स्पर्शवच्चैतद्रूपं भायान्ममेत्यलम् ।
न त्वस्य स्पृश्यभिन्नस्य वेद्यैकान्तस्वरूपिणः ॥ 15
3.m: Like touch, this visual form would appear on one's own face as 'mine' completely, / and not as belonging to this [reflection] which is distinct from what is touched and whose nature is exclusively an object of cognition.

3.s:
rūpasaṃsthānamātraṃ tatsparśagandharasādibhiḥ /
nyagbhūtaireva tadyuktaṃ vastu tatpratibimbitam // 16
3.d:
रूपसंस्थानमात्रं तत्स्पर्शगन्धरसादिभिः ।
न्यग्भूतैरेव तद्युक्तं वस्तु तत्प्रतिबिम्बितम् ॥ 16
3.m: That is only visual form and configuration; the thing that is reflected / is endowed with them, while touch, smell, taste, and the like are concealed.

3.s:
nyagbhāvo grāhyatābhāvāttadabhāvo'pramāṇataḥ /
sa cārthasaṃgamābhāvātso'pyādarśe'navasthiteḥ // 17
3.d:
न्यग्भावो ग्राह्यताभावात्तदभावोऽप्रमाणतः ।
स चार्थसंगमाभावात्सोऽप्यादर्शेऽनवस्थितेः ॥ 17
3.m: Their concealment is due to absence of graspability; that absence is due to absence of means of valid cognition; / and that is due to absence of contact with the object, and that in turn because it does not abide in the mirror.

3.s:
ata eva gurutvādirdharmo naitasya lakṣyate /
nahyādarśe saṃsthito'sau taddṛṣṭau sa upāyakaḥ // 18
3.d:
अत एव गुरुत्वादिर्धर्मो नैतस्य लक्ष्यते ।
नह्यादर्शे संस्थितोऽसौ तद्दृष्टौ स उपायकः ॥ 18
3.m: Precisely therefore, a property such as weight is not perceived in this [reflection]; / for it does not reside in the mirror: that [mirror] is merely an instrument in seeing it.

3.s:
tasmāttu naiṣa bhedena yadbhāti tata ucyate /
ādhārastatra tūpāyā dīpadṛksaṃvidaḥ kramāt // 19
3.d:
तस्मात्तु नैष भेदेन यद्भाति तत उच्यते ।
आधारस्तत्र तूपाया दीपदृक्संविदः क्रमात् ॥ 19
3.m: Therefore, it is stated: 'From that in which it shines without difference, / there is the substratum; but the means therein are, in succession, a lamp, the eye, and consciousness.'

3.s:
dīpacakṣurvibodhānāṃ kāṭhinyābhāvataḥ param /
sarvataścāpi nairmalyānna vibhādarśavatpṛthak // 20
3.d:
दीपचक्षुर्विबोधानां काठिन्याभावतः परम् ।
सर्वतश्चापि नैर्मल्यान्न विभादर्शवत्पृथक् ॥ 20
3.m: Because of the absence of solidity in the lamp, the eye, and consciousness, / and because of their universal purity, [the reflection] does not shine separately as in a mirror.

3.s:
etacca devadevena darśitaṃ bodhavṛddhaye /
mūḍhānāṃ vastu bhavati tato'pyanyatra nāpyalam // 21
3.d:
एतच्च देवदेवेन दर्शितं बोधवृद्धये ।
मूढानां वस्तु भवति ततोऽप्यन्यत्र नाप्यलम् ॥ 21
3.m: And this has been shown by the God of gods for the growth of understanding; / for the deluded, an entity exists, but elsewhere it does not exist at all.

3.s:
pratīghāti svatantraṃ no na sthāyyasthāyi cāpi na /
svacchasyaivaiṣa kasyāpi mahimeti kṛpālunā // 22
3.d:
प्रतीघाति स्वतन्त्रं नो न स्थाय्यस्थायि चापि न ।
स्वच्छस्यैवैष कस्यापि महिमेति कृपालुना ॥ 22
3.m: It is neither obstructive nor autonomous, neither permanent nor impermanent; / this is the greatness of some transparent [reality],' so [said] the compassionate one.

3.s:
na deśoṃ no rūpaṃ na ca samayayogo na parimā na cānyonyāsaṃgo na ca tadapahānirna ghanatā /
na cāvastutvaṃ syānna ca kimapi sāraṃ nijamiti dhruvaṃ mohaḥ śāmyediti niradiśaddarpaṇavidhiḥ // 23
3.d:
न देशों नो रूपं न च समययोगो न परिमा न चान्योन्यासंगो न च तदपहानिर्न घनता ।
न चावस्तुत्वं स्यान्न च किमपि सारं निजमिति ध्रुवं मोहः शाम्येदिति निरदिशद्दर्पणविधिः ॥ 23
3.m: "There is neither location nor form, neither conjunction with time nor measurement, neither intermingling nor its cessation, neither density, / nor unreality, nor any individual core of its own"—to ensure delusion would indeed cease, the compassionate one taught the rule of the mirror.

3.s:
itthaṃ pradarśite'mutra pratibimbanavartmani /
śabdasya pratibimbaṃ yat pratiśrutketi bhaṇyate // 24
3.d:
इत्थं प्रदर्शितेऽमुत्र प्रतिबिम्बनवर्त्मनि ।
शब्दस्य प्रतिबिम्बं यत् प्रतिश्रुत्केति भण्यते ॥ 24
3.m: The path of reflection having thus been demonstrated here, / that which is the reflection of sound is termed an echo.

3.s:
na cāsau śabdajaḥ śabda āgacchattvena saṃśravāt /
tenaiva vaktrā dūrasthaiḥ śabdasyāśravaṇādapi // 25
3.d:
न चासौ शब्दजः शब्द आगच्छत्त्वेन संश्रवात् ।
तेनैव वक्त्रा दूरस्थैः शब्दस्याश्रवणादपि ॥ 25
3.m: And this is not a sound produced from sound, because it is heard as coming [back], / and also because the sound is not heard by those standing far away from that very speaker.

3.s:
piṭhirādipidhānāṃśaviśiṣṭachidrasaṃgatau /
citratvāccāsya śabdasya pratibimbaṃ mukhādivat // 26
3.d:
पिठिरादिपिधानांशविशिष्टछिद्रसंगतौ ।
चित्रत्वाच्चास्य शब्दस्य प्रतिबिम्बं मुखादिवत् ॥ 26
3.m: When it encounters a cavity characterized by a part covered by a pot or the like, / and because of this variegated nature of sound, its reflection is like a face and the like.

3.s:
idamanyasya vedyasya rūpamityavabhāsate /
yathādarśe tathā kenāpyuktamākarṇaye tviti // 27
3.d:
इदमन्यस्य वेद्यस्य रूपमित्यवभासते ।
यथादर्शे तथा केनाप्युक्तमाकर्णये त्विति ॥ 27
3.m: "This appears as the form of another knowable object"— / just as in a mirror, so one says: "I hear [it] spoken by someone else."

3.s:
niyamādbimbasāṃmukhyaṃ pratibimbasya yattataḥ /
tanmadhyagāḥ pramātāraḥ śṛṇvanti pratiśabdakam // 28
3.d:
नियमाद्बिम्बसांमुख्यं प्रतिबिम्बस्य यत्ततः ।
तन्मध्यगाः प्रमातारः शृण्वन्ति प्रतिशब्दकम् ॥ 28
3.m: Because of the rule that a reflection is oriented face to face with the original archetype, / the knowers standing between them hear the echo.

3.s:
mukhyagrahaṃ tvapi vinā pratibimbagraho bhavet /
svapaścātsthaṃ priyaṃ paśyeṭṭaṅkitaṃ mukure vapuḥ // 29
3.d:
मुख्यग्रहं त्वपि विना प्रतिबिम्बग्रहो भवेत् ।
स्वपश्चात्स्थं प्रियं पश्येट्टङ्कितं मुकुरे वपुः ॥ 29
3.m: Even without grasping the primary archetype, however, there can be apprehension of the reflection: / one may see the form of one's beloved standing behind oneself engraved in a mirror.

3.s: sāṃmukhyaṃ cocyate tādṛgdarpaṇābhedasaṃsthiteḥ // 30
3.d: सांमुख्यं चोच्यते तादृग्दर्पणाभेदसंस्थितेः ॥ 30
3.m: And such mutual facing is spoken of because of non-differentiation from the mirror.

3.s:
ataḥ kūpādipiṭhirākāśe tatpratibimbitam /
vaktrākāśaṃ saśabdaṃ sadbhāti tatparavaktavat // 31
3.d:
अतः कूपादिपिठिराकाशे तत्प्रतिबिम्बितम् ।
वक्त्राकाशं सशब्दं सद्भाति तत्परवक्तवत् ॥ 31
3.m: Therefore, reflected in the space of a well, pot, or the like, / the space of the speaker's mouth, possessing sound, appears like the mouth of another.

3.s:
yathā cādarśapāścātyabhāgastho vetti no mukham /
tathā tathāvidhākāśapaścātstho vetti na dhvanim // 32
3.d:
यथा चादर्शपाश्चात्यभागस्थो वेत्ति नो मुखम् ।
तथा तथाविधाकाशपश्चात्स्थो वेत्ति न ध्वनिम् ॥ 32
3.m: And just as someone situated behind a mirror does not perceive the face, / so someone situated behind such space does not perceive the sound.

3.s:
śabdo na cānabhivyaktaḥ pratibimbati taddhruvam /
abhivyaktiśrutī tasya samakālaṃ dvitīyake // 33
3.d:
शब्दो न चानभिव्यक्तः प्रतिबिम्बति तद्ध्रुवम् ।
अभिव्यक्तिश्रुती तस्य समकालं द्वितीयके ॥ 33
3.m: And sound certainly does not reflect unmanifest; / its manifestation and audition are simultaneous. In the second

3.s:
kṣaṇe tu pratibimbatvaṃ śrutiśca samakālikā /
tulyakālaṃ hi no hastatacchāyārūpaniścayaḥ // 34
3.d:
क्षणे तु प्रतिबिम्बत्वं श्रुतिश्च समकालिका ।
तुल्यकालं हि नो हस्ततच्छायारूपनिश्चयः ॥ 34
3.m: moment, however, its status as a reflection and its hearing are simultaneous; / for the determination of the hand and the form of its shadow do not occur at the same time.

3.s:
itthaṃ pradarśite'mutra pratibimbasatattvake /
prakṛtaṃ brūmahe tatra pratibimbanamarhati // 35
3.d:
इत्थं प्रदर्शितेऽमुत्र प्रतिबिम्बसतत्त्वके ।
प्रकृतं ब्रूमहे तत्र प्रतिबिम्बनमर्हति ॥ 35
3.m: The true nature of reflection having thus been demonstrated here, / we state the subject at hand: there, reflection is possible.

3.s:
śabdo nabhasi sānande sparśadhāmani sundaraḥ /
sparśo'nyo'pi dṛḍhāghātaśūlaśītādikodbhavaḥ /
parasthaḥ pratibimbatvātsvadehoddhūlanākaraḥ // 36
3.d:
शब्दो नभसि सानन्दे स्पर्शधामनि सुन्दरः ।
स्पर्शोऽन्योऽपि दृढाघातशूलशीतादिकोद्भवः ।
परस्थः प्रतिबिम्बत्वात्स्वदेहोद्धूलनाकरः ॥ 36
3.m: Sound [reflects] in space, a beautiful touch in the delightful locus of touch, / and another touch, arising from a firm blow, colic, cold, and the like / situated in another, because it is a reflection, causes trembling in one's own body.

3.s: na caiṣa mukhyastatkāryapāramparyāprakāśanāt // 37
3.d: न चैष मुख्यस्तत्कार्यपारम्पर्याप्रकाशनात् ॥ 37
3.m: And this is not primary, because it does not display the sequence of its [full] effects.

3.s: evaṃ ghrāṇāntare gandho raso dantodake sphuṭaḥ // 38
3.d: एवं घ्राणान्तरे गन्धो रसो दन्तोदके स्फुटः ॥ 38
3.m: Likewise, smell is evident within the olfactory organ, and taste in the saliva of the teeth.

3.s:
yathā ca rūpaṃ pratibimbitaṃ dṛśorna cakṣuṣānyena vinā hi lakṣyate /
tathā rasasparśanasaurabhādikaṃ na lakṣyate'kṣeṇa vinā sthitaṃ tvapi // 39
3.d:
यथा च रूपं प्रतिबिम्बितं दृशोर्न चक्षुषान्येन विना हि लक्ष्यते ।
तथा रसस्पर्शनसौरभादिकं न लक्ष्यतेऽक्षेण विना स्थितं त्वपि ॥ 39
