3.m: And just as form reflected in the eyes is not noticed without another eye, / so taste, touch, fragrance, and the like, even when present, are not noticed without a sense organ.

3.s: na cāntare sparśanadhāmani sthitaṃ bahiḥspṛśonyākṣadhiyaḥ sa gocaraḥ // 40
3.d: न चान्तरे स्पर्शनधामनि स्थितं बहिःस्पृशोन्याक्षधियः स गोचरः ॥ 40
3.m: Nor is what is present within the locus of touch an object of the perceptual cognition of an external tactile sense organ.

3.s:
ato'ntikasthasvakatādṛgindriyaprayojanāntaḥkaraṇairyadā kṛtā /
tadā tadāttaṃ pratibimbamindriye svakāṃ kriyāṃ sūyata eva tādṛśīm // 41
3.d:
अतोऽन्तिकस्थस्वकतादृगिन्द्रियप्रयोजनान्तःकरणैर्यदा कृता ।
तदा तदात्तं प्रतिबिम्बमिन्द्रिये स्वकां क्रियां सूयत एव तादृशीम् ॥ 41
3.m: Therefore, when generated by internal organs that employ such nearby sense organs of their own, / then the reflection received in the sense organ produces its own corresponding activity.

3.s:
na tu smṛtānmānasagocarādṛtā bhavetkriyā sā kila vartamānataḥ /
ataḥ sthitaḥ sparśavarastadindriye samāgataḥ sanviditastathākriyaḥ // 42
3.d:
न तु स्मृतान्मानसगोचरादृता भवेत्क्रिया सा किल वर्तमानतः ।
अतः स्थितः स्पर्शवरस्तदिन्द्रिये समागतः सन्विदितस्तथाक्रियः ॥ 42
3.m: For that activity does not arise from a remembered object of the mind without presentness; / therefore, the excellent touch, present in that sense organ and having arrived, is experienced as having such an activity.

3.s:
asaṃbhave bāhyagatasya tādṛśaḥ sva eva tasminpratibimbitastathā /
karoti tāṃ sparśavaraḥ sukhātmikāṃ sa cāpi kasyāmapi nāḍisaṃtatau // 43
3.d:
असंभवे बाह्यगतस्य तादृशः स्व एव तस्मिन्प्रतिबिम्बितस्तथा ।
करोति तां स्पर्शवरः सुखात्मिकां स चापि कस्यामपि नाडिसंततौ ॥ 43
3.m: In the absence of an external one, such an excellent touch, reflected within itself in that way, / produces that pleasant feeling, and that too in some network of subtle channels.

3.s:
tena saṃvittimakure viśvamātmānamarpayat /
nāthasya vadate'muṣya vimalāṃ viśvarūpatām // 44
3.d:
तेन संवित्तिमकुरे विश्वमात्मानमर्पयत् ।
नाथस्य वदतेऽमुष्य विमलां विश्वरूपताम् ॥ 44
3.m: Thereby, the universe offering itself up in the mirror of consciousness / proclaims the immaculate omniformity of this Lord.

3.s:
yathā ca gandharūpaspṛgrasādyāḥ pratibimbitāḥ /
tadādhāroparāgeṇa bhānti khaṅge mukhādivat // 45
3.d:
यथा च गन्धरूपस्पृग्रसाद्याः प्रतिबिम्बिताः ।
तदाधारोपरागेण भान्ति खङ्गे मुखादिवत् ॥ 45
3.m: And just as smell, form, touch, taste, and the like, when reflected, / appear colored by their substratum, like a face or the like in a sword,

3.s:
tathā viśvamidaṃ bodhe pratibimbitamāśrayet /
prakāśatvasvatantratvaprabhṛtiṃ dharmavistaram // 46
3.d:
तथा विश्वमिदं बोधे प्रतिबिम्बितमाश्रयेत् ।
प्रकाशत्वस्वतन्त्रत्वप्रभृतिं धर्मविस्तरम् ॥ 46
3.m: so this universe, reflected in consciousness, takes on / the multitude of attributes such as luminosity and absolute autonomy.

3.s:
yathā ca sarvataḥ svacche sphaṭike sarvato bhavet /
pratibimbaṃ tathā bodhe sarvataḥ svacchatājuṣi // 47
3.d:
यथा च सर्वतः स्वच्छे स्फटिके सर्वतो भवेत् ।
प्रतिबिम्बं तथा बोधे सर्वतः स्वच्छताजुषि ॥ 47
3.m: And just as in a crystal that is completely transparent, a reflection / appears on all sides, so it does in consciousness which enjoys complete transparency on all sides.

3.s:
atyantasvacchatā sā yatsvākṛtyanavabhāsanam /
ataḥ svacchatamo bodho na ratnaṃ tvākṛtigrahāt // 48
3.d:
अत्यन्तस्वच्छता सा यत्स्वाकृत्यनवभासनम् ।
अतः स्वच्छतमो बोधो न रत्नं त्वाकृतिग्रहात् ॥ 48
3.m: Absolute transparency is that non-appearance of one's own shape; / therefore, consciousness is the most transparent, but not a gem, because of its apprehension of shape.

3.s:
pratibimbaṃ ca bimbena bāhyasthena samarpyate /
tasyaiva pratibimbatve kiṃ bimbamavaśiṣyatām // 49
3.d:
प्रतिबिम्बं च बिम्बेन बाह्यस्थेन समर्प्यते ।
तस्यैव प्रतिबिम्बत्वे किं बिम्बमवशिष्यताम् ॥ 49
3.m: And a reflection is presented by an original archetype situated externally; / if that [external reality] itself is a reflection, what original archetype could remain?

3.s:
yadvāpi kāraṇaṃ kiṃcidbimbatvenābhiṣicyate /
tadapi pratibimbatvameti bodhe'nyathā tvasat // 50
3.d:
यद्वापि कारणं किंचिद्बिम्बत्वेनाभिषिच्यते ।
तदपि प्रतिबिम्बत्वमेति बोधेऽन्यथा त्वसत् ॥ 50
3.m: Or whatever cause is consecrated as the original archetype, / that too attains the state of reflection in consciousness; otherwise, it would be non-existent.

3.s:
itthametatsvasaṃvittidṛḍhanyāyāstrarakṣitam /
sāmrājyameva viśvatra pratibimbasya jṛmbhate // 51
3.d:
इत्थमेतत्स्वसंवित्तिदृढन्यायास्त्ररक्षितम् ।
साम्राज्यमेव विश्वत्र प्रतिबिम्बस्य जृम्भते ॥ 51
3.m: Thus, protected by the firm weapon of reasoning based on self-awareness, / the sovereign dominion of reflection alone expands everywhere.

3.s:
nanu bimbasya virahe pratibimbaṃ kathaṃ bhavet /
kiṃ kurmo dṛśyate taddhi nanu tadbimbamucyatām // 52
3.d:
ननु बिम्बस्य विरहे प्रतिबिम्बं कथं भवेत् ।
किं कुर्मो दृश्यते तद्धि ननु तद्बिम्बमुच्यताम् ॥ 52
3.m: [Objection:] But in the absence of an original archetype, how can there be a reflection? / [Reply:] What can we do? For it is seen! [Objection:] Then let that be called the original archetype!

3.s:
naivaṃ tallakṣaṇābhāvādbimbaṃ kila kimucyate /
anyāmiśraṃ svatantraṃ sadbhāsamānaṃ mukhaṃ yathā // 53
3.d:
नैवं तल्लक्षणाभावाद्बिम्बं किल किमुच्यते ।
अन्यामिश्रं स्वतन्त्रं सद्भासमानं मुखं यथा ॥ 53
3.m: [Reply:] Not so, because its defining characteristic is absent. For what is called the original archetype? / That which appears unmixed with another and independent, like a face.

3.s:
svarūpānapahānena pararūpasadṛkṣatām /
pratibimbātmatāmāhuḥ khaḍgādarśatalādivat // 54
3.d:
स्वरूपानपहानेन पररूपसदृक्षताम् ।
प्रतिबिम्बात्मतामाहुः खड्गादर्शतलादिवत् ॥ 54
3.m: They declare the nature of a reflection to be resemblance to the form of another / without abandoning one's own essential nature, as on the surface of a sword, a mirror, and the like.

3.s:
uktaṃ ca sati bāhye'pi dhīrekānekavedanāt /
anekasadṛśākārā na tvaneketi saugataiḥ // 55
3.d:
उक्तं च सति बाह्येऽपि धीरेकानेकवेदनात् ।
अनेकसदृशाकारा न त्वनेकेति सौगतैः ॥ 55
3.m: And it has been stated by the Buddhists: "Even when the external exists, cognition is single, yet through the apprehension of manifold things / it has a form resembling the manifold, but is not itself manifold."

3.s:
nanvitthaṃ pratibimbasya lakṣaṇaṃ kiṃ taducyate /
anyavyāmiśraṇāyogāttadbhedāśakyabhāsanam /
pratibimbamiti prāhurdarpaṇe vadanaṃ yathā // 56
3.d:
नन्वित्थं प्रतिबिम्बस्य लक्षणं किं तदुच्यते ।
अन्यव्यामिश्रणायोगात्तद्भेदाशक्यभासनम् ।
प्रतिबिम्बमिति प्राहुर्दर्पणे वदनं यथा ॥ 56
3.m: [Objection:] If so, what is said to be the definition of a reflection? / [Reply:] Because mixing with another is impossible, that whose appearance as distinct from it is impossible / is called a reflection, like a face in a mirror.

3.s:
bodhamiśramidaṃ bodhādbhedenāśakyabhāsanam /
paratattvādi bodhe kiṃ pratibimbaṃ na bhaṇyate // 57
3.d:
बोधमिश्रमिदं बोधाद्भेदेनाशक्यभासनम् ।
परतत्त्वादि बोधे किं प्रतिबिम्बं न भण्यते ॥ 57
3.m: This [universe], mixed with consciousness, cannot appear as distinct from consciousness; / why is the highest reality and so on not spoken of as a reflection in consciousness?

3.s:
lakṣaṇasya vyavasthaiṣākasmāccedbimbamucyatām /
prājñā vastuni yujyante na tu sāmayike dhvanau // 58
3.d:
लक्षणस्य व्यवस्थैषाकस्माच्चेद्बिम्बमुच्यताम् ।
प्राज्ञा वस्तुनि युज्यन्ते न तु सामयिके ध्वनौ ॥ 58
3.m: This is the established definition. If you ask why it should not be called an archetype, / the wise concern themselves with the real entity, not with conventional words.

3.s:
nanu na pratibimbasya vinā bimbaṃ bhavetsthitiḥ /
kiṃ tataḥ pratibimbe hi bimbaṃ tādātmyavṛtti na // 59
3.d:
ननु न प्रतिबिम्बस्य विना बिम्बं भवेत्स्थितिः ।
किं ततः प्रतिबिम्बे हि बिम्बं तादात्म्यवृत्ति न ॥ 59
3.m: [Objection:] But a reflection cannot exist without an original archetype! / [Reply:] What of it? For the original archetype does not exist identically in the reflection.

3.s:
ataśca lakṣaṇasyāsya proktasya tadasaṃbhave /
na hānirhetumātre tu praśno'yaṃ paryavasyati // 60
3.d:
अतश्च लक्षणस्यास्य प्रोक्तस्य तदसंभवे ।
न हानिर्हेतुमात्रे तु प्रश्नोऽयं पर्यवस्यति ॥ 60
3.m: And so, if that [archetype] is absent, there is no damage / to this stated definition; this question only boils down to the cause alone.

3.s:
tatrāpi ca nimittākhye nopādāne kathaṃcana /
nimittakāraṇānāṃ ca kadācitkvāpi saṃbhavaḥ // 61
3.d:
तत्रापि च निमित्ताख्ये नोपादाने कथंचन ।
निमित्तकारणानां च कदाचित्क्वापि संभवः ॥ 61
3.m: And there, too, [it relates only] to what is called an efficient cause, not at all to a material cause; / and efficient causes are possible sometimes, somewhere.

3.s:
ata eva purovartinyāloke smaraṇādinā /
nimittena ghanenāstu saṃkrāntadayitākṛtiḥ // 62
3.d:
अत एव पुरोवर्तिन्यालोके स्मरणादिना ।
निमित्तेन घनेनास्तु संक्रान्तदयिताकृतिः ॥ 62
3.m: Therefore, in the light present before one, through an intense efficient cause / such as memory, let the form of the beloved be transferred.

3.s:
anyathā saṃvidārūḍhā kāntā vicchedayoginī /
kasmādbhāti na vai saṃvid vicchedaṃ purato gatā // 63
3.d:
अन्यथा संविदारूढा कान्ता विच्छेदयोगिनी ।
कस्माद्भाति न वै संविद् विच्छेदं पुरतो गता ॥ 63
3.m: Otherwise, why would the beloved, mounted on consciousness and possessing separation, / appear [there]? Consciousness certainly does not become separated having gone out in front.

3.s:
ata evāntaraṃ kiṃciddhīsaṃjñaṃ bhavatu sphuṭam /
yatrāsya vicchidā bhānaṃ saṃkalpasvapnadarśane // 64
3.d:
अत एवान्तरं किंचिद्धीसंज्ञं भवतु स्फुटम् ।
यत्रास्य विच्छिदा भानं संकल्पस्वप्नदर्शने ॥ 64
3.m: Therefore, let there be an internal something clearly designated as the intellect, / wherein its appearance takes place with separation, as in conceptualization and dream vision.

3.s:
ato nimittaṃ devasya śaktayaḥ santu tādṛśe /
itthaṃ viśvamidaṃ nāthe bhairavīyacidambare /
pratibimbamalaṃ svacche na khalvanyaprasādataḥ // 65
3.d:
अतो निमित्तं देवस्य शक्तयः सन्तु तादृशे ।
इत्थं विश्वमिदं नाथे भैरवीयचिदम्बरे ।
प्रतिबिम्बमलं स्वच्छे न खल्वन्यप्रसादतः ॥ 65
3.m: Therefore, let the powers of the God be the efficient cause in such a case. / Thus this universe is fully a reflection in the Lord, in the transparent sky of Bhairavian consciousness, / and certainly not through the favor of anything else.

3.s:
ananyāpekṣitā yāsya viśvātmatvaṃ prati prabhoḥ /
tāṃ parāṃ pratibhāṃ devīṃ saṃgirante hyanuttarām // 66
3.d:
अनन्यापेक्षिता यास्य विश्वात्मत्वं प्रति प्रभोः ।
तां परां प्रतिभां देवीं संगिरन्ते ह्यनुत्तराम् ॥ 66
3.m: That independence of anything else which belongs to this Lord with respect to being the self of the universe, / they proclaim as that supreme, unexcelled goddess, intuitive flash.

3.s:
akulasyāsya devasya kulaprathanaśālinī /
kaulikī sā parā śaktiraviyukto yayā prabhuḥ // 67
3.d:
अकुलस्यास्य देवस्य कुलप्रथनशालिनी ।
कौलिकी सा परा शक्तिरवियुक्तो यया प्रभुः ॥ 67
3.m: This supreme Kaula power, characterized by the expansion of the Kula of this god who is beyond Kula (akula), / is that by which the Lord is never abandoned. // 67

3.s:
tayoryadyāmalaṃ rūpaṃ sa saṃghaṭṭa iti smṛtaḥ /
ānandaśaktiḥ saivoktā yato viśvaṃ visṛjyate // 68
3.d:
तयोर्यद्यामलं रूपं स संघट्ट इति स्मृतः ।
आनन्दशक्तिः सैवोक्ता यतो विश्वं विसृज्यते ॥ 68
3.m: The dyadic form of the two is remembered as the conjunction (saṃghaṭṭa). / That itself is spoken of as the power of bliss (ānandaśakti), from which the universe is creatively emitted. // 68

3.s:
parāparātparaṃ tattvaṃ saiṣā devī nigadyate /
tatsāraṃ tacca hṛdayaṃ sa visargaḥ paraḥ prabhuḥ // 69
3.d:
परापरात्परं तत्त्वं सैषा देवी निगद्यते ।
तत्सारं तच्च हृदयं स विसर्गः परः प्रभुः ॥ 69
3.m: This very goddess is declared to be the reality transcending the higher and the lower (parāparātpara); / she is that essence and that heart; she is the supreme creative emission, the Lord. // 69

3.s:
devīyāmalaśāstre sā kathitā kālakarṣiṇī /
mahāḍāmarake yāge śrīparā mastake tathā // 70
3.d:
देवीयामलशास्त्रे सा कथिता कालकर्षिणी ।
महाडामरके यागे श्रीपरा मस्तके तथा ॥ 70
3.m: In the Devīyāmala scripture, she is spoken of as Kālakarṣiṇī; / and in the sacrifice of the Mahāḍāmara, on the head, as the venerable Parā. // 70

3.s:
śrīpūrvaśāstre sā mātṛsadbhāvatvena varṇitā /
saṃghaṭṭe'smiṃścidātmatvādyattatpratyavamarśanam // 71
3.d:
श्रीपूर्वशास्त्रे सा मातृसद्भावत्वेन वर्णिता ।
संघट्टेऽस्मिंश्चिदात्मत्वाद्यत्तत्प्रत्यवमर्शनम् ॥ 71
3.m: In the venerable Pūrva scripture (Mālinīvijayottara), she is described as the true nature of the Mother (mātṛsadbhāva). / In this conjunction, because it consists of consciousness, the reflective awareness that arises— // 71

3.s:
icchāśaktiraghorāṇāṃ śaktīnāṃ sā parā prabhuḥ /
saiva prakṣubdharūpā cedīśitrī saṃprajāyate // 72
3.d:
इच्छाशक्तिरघोराणां शक्तीनां सा परा प्रभुः ।
सैव प्रक्षुब्धरूपा चेदीशित्री संप्रजायते ॥ 72
3.m: is the power of will (icchāśakti), the supreme Lord of the benevolent (aghora) powers. / If that very [power] assumes an agitated form, she becomes the ruler (īśitrī). // 72

3.s:
tadā ghorāḥ parā devyo jātāḥ śaivādhvadaiśikāḥ /
svātmapratyavamarśo yaḥ prāgabhūdekavīrakaḥ // 73
3.d:
तदा घोराः परा देव्यो जाताः शैवाध्वदैशिकाः ।
स्वात्मप्रत्यवमर्शो यः प्रागभूदेकवीरकः ॥ 73
3.m: Then the fierce (ghora) supreme goddesses are born, the guides on the Śaiva path. / The reflective awareness of one's own self, which was previously a solitary hero, // 73

3.s:
jñātavyaviśvonmeṣātmā jñānaśaktitayā sthitaḥ /
iyaṃ parāparā devī ghorāṃ yā mātṛmaṇḍalīm // 74
3.d:
ज्ञातव्यविश्वोन्मेषात्मा ज्ञानशक्तितया स्थितः ।
इयं परापरा देवी घोरां या मातृमण्डलीम् ॥ 74
3.m: abides as the power of knowledge (jñānaśakti), consisting of the opening out of the entire universe to be known. / This is the Goddess Parāparā, who unceasingly emits // 74

3.s:
sṛjatyavirataṃ śuddhāśuddhamārgaikadīpikām /
jñeyāṃśaḥ pronmiṣankṣobhaṃ yadaiti balavattvataḥ // 75
3.d:
सृजत्यविरतं शुद्धाशुद्धमार्गैकदीपिकाम् ।
ज्ञेयांशः प्रोन्मिषन्क्षोभं यदैति बलवत्त्वतः ॥ 75
3.m: the fierce circle of mothers, the sole illuminator of the pure and impure paths. / When the objective aspect, unfolding forcefully, undergoes agitation, // 75

3.s:
ūnatābhāsanaṃ saṃvinmātratve jāyate tadā /
rūḍhaṃ tajjñeyavargasya sthitiprārambha ucyate // 76
3.d:
ऊनताभासनं संविन्मात्रत्वे जायते तदा ।
रूढं तज्ज्ञेयवर्गस्य स्थितिप्रारम्भ उच्यते ॥ 76
3.m: then the appearance of deficiency arises in what is sheer consciousness; / that established [deficiency] is called the commencement of the persistence of the class of objects of knowledge. // 76

3.s:
rūḍhireṣā vibodhābdheścitrākāraparigrahaḥ /
idaṃ tadbījasaṃdarbhabījaṃ cinvanti yoginaḥ // 77
3.d:
रूढिरेषा विबोधाब्धेश्चित्राकारपरिग्रहः ।
इदं तद्बीजसंदर्भबीजं चिन्वन्ति योगिनः ॥ 77
3.m: This establishment is the ocean of consciousness assuming diverse forms. / This is that seed of the collection of seeds which yogins gather. // 77

3.s:
icchāśaktirdvirūpoktā kṣubhitākṣubhitā ca yā /
iṣyamāṇaṃ hi sā vastudvairūpyeṇātmani śrayet // 78
3.d:
इच्छाशक्तिर्द्विरूपोक्ता क्षुभिताक्षुभिता च या ।
इष्यमाणं हि सा वस्तुद्वैरूप्येणात्मनि श्रयेत् ॥ 78
3.m: The power of will is said to be twofold: agitated and unagitated; / for it rests within itself through the twofold nature of the object willed: // 78

3.s:
aciradyutibhāsinyā śaktyā jvalanarūpayā /
iṣyamāṇasamāpattiḥ sthairyeṇātha dharātmanā // 79
3.d:
अचिरद्युतिभासिन्या शक्त्या ज्वलनरूपया ।
इष्यमाणसमापत्तिः स्थैर्येणाथ धरात्मना ॥ 79
3.m: through the power shining like lightning, having the nature of fire, / there is absorption into what is willed; then, through stability, [it rests] in the nature of earth. // 79

3.s:
unmeṣaśaktāvastyetajjñeyaṃ yadyapi bhūyasā /
tathāpi vibhavasthānaṃ sā na tu prācyajanmabhūḥ // 80
3.d:
उन्मेषशक्तावस्त्येतज्ज्ञेयं यद्यपि भूयसा ।
तथापि विभवस्थानं सा न तु प्राच्यजन्मभूः ॥ 80
3.m: Although this object of knowledge exists abundantly in the power of opening (unmeṣaśakti), / nevertheless, that [power of opening] is its place of expansion, but not its original birthplace. // 80

3.s:
icchāśakterataḥ prāhuścātūrūpyaṃ parāmṛtam /
kṣobhāntarasyāsadbhāvānnedaṃ bījaṃ ca kasyacit // 81
3.d:
इच्छाशक्तेरतः प्राहुश्चातूरूप्यं परामृतम् ।
क्षोभान्तरस्यासद्भावान्नेदं बीजं च कस्यचित् ॥ 81
3.m: Therefore, they proclaim the fourfold nature of the power of will to be the supreme nectar (parāmṛta); / and because no further agitation exists, this is not the seed of anything. // 81

3.s:
prakṣobhakatvaṃ bījatvaṃ kṣobhādhāraśca yonitā /
kṣobhakaṃ saṃvido rūpaṃ kṣubhyati kṣobhayatyapi // 82
3.d:
प्रक्षोभकत्वं बीजत्वं क्षोभाधारश्च योनिता ।
क्षोभकं संविदो रूपं क्षुभ्यति क्षोभयत्यपि ॥ 82
3.m: Being the agitator is seedhood (bījatva), and the receptacle of agitation is the source-womb (yonitā). / The agitator is the form of consciousness; it is agitated, and it also agitates. // 82

3.s:
kṣobhaḥ syājjñeyadharmatvaṃ kṣobhaṇā tadbahiṣkṛtiḥ /
antaḥsthaviśvābhinnaikabījāṃśavisisṛkṣutā // 83
3.d:
क्षोभः स्याज्ज्ञेयधर्मत्वं क्षोभणा तद्बहिष्कृतिः ।
अन्तःस्थविश्वाभिन्नैकबीजांशविसिसृक्षुता ॥ 83
3.m: Agitation is being an attribute of the knowable; the act of agitating is its externalization: / the desire to emit the single seed-fraction that is non-different from the universe residing within. // 83

3.s:
kṣobho'tadicche tattvecchābhāsanaṃ kṣobhaṇāṃ viduḥ /
yadaikyāpattimāsādya tadicchā kṛtinī bhavet // 84
3.d:
क्षोभोऽतदिच्छे तत्त्वेच्छाभासनं क्षोभणां विदुः ।
यदैक्यापत्तिमासाद्य तदिच्छा कृतिनी भवेत् ॥ 84
3.m: Agitation is the will toward that [object]; they know the manifestation of the will toward reality as the act of agitating. / Attaining unity with that, that will becomes effective. // 84

3.s:
kṣobhādhāramimaṃ prāhuḥ śrīsomānandaputrakāḥ /
saṃvidāmīṣaṇādīnāmanudbhinnaviśeṣakam // 85
3.d:
क्षोभाधारमिमं प्राहुः श्रीसोमानन्दपुत्रकाः ।
संविदामीषणादीनामनुद्भिन्नविशेषकम् ॥ 85
3.m: The spiritual sons of venerable Somānanda declare this to be the receptacle of agitation: / it has no differentiated particularities among the conscious states such as wishing. // 85

3.s:
yajjñeyamātraṃ tadbījaṃ yadyogādbījatā svare /
tasya bījasya saivoktā visisṛkṣā ya udbhavaḥ /
yato grāhyamidaṃ bhāsyadbhinnakalpaṃ cidātmanaḥ // 86
3.d:
यज्ज्ञेयमात्रं तद्बीजं यद्योगाद्बीजता स्वरे ।
तस्य बीजस्य सैवोक्ता विसिसृक्षा य उद्भवः ।
यतो ग्राह्यमिदं भास्यद्भिन्नकल्पं चिदात्मनः ॥ 86
3.m: That which is merely an object of knowledge is that seed; through connection with it, seedhood arises in the vowel. / That very desire to emit, which is the arising, is declared to belong to that seed, / whence this apprehensible object is to be manifested, as if differentiated from the conscious self. // 86

3.s:
eṣa kṣobhaḥ kṣobhaṇā tu tūṣṇīṃbhūtānyamātṛgam /
haṭhādyadaudāsīnyāṃśacyāvanaṃ saṃvido balāt // 87
3.d:
एष क्षोभः क्षोभणा तु तूष्णींभूतान्यमातृगम् ।
हठाद्यदौदासीन्यांशच्यावनं संविदो बलात् ॥ 87
3.m: This is agitation; but the act of agitating is the forcible displacement of the fraction of neutrality of consciousness / toward another knowing subject that has become silent. // 87

3.s:
jātāpi visisṛkṣāsau yadvimarśāntaraikyataḥ /
kṛtārthā jāyate kṣobhādhāro'traitatprakīrtitam // 88
3.d:
जातापि विसिसृक्षासौ यद्विमर्शान्तरैक्यतः ।
कृतार्था जायते क्षोभाधारोऽत्रैतत्प्रकीर्तितम् ॥ 88
3.m: Though arisen, this desire to emit becomes fulfilled through unity with another reflective awareness; / herein this is proclaimed to be the receptacle of agitation. // 88

3.s:
tatastadāntaraṃ jñeyaṃ bhinnakalpatvamicchati /
viśvabījādataḥ sarva bāhyaṃ bimbaṃ vivartsyati // 89
3.d:
ततस्तदान्तरं ज्ञेयं भिन्नकल्पत्वमिच्छति ।
विश्वबीजादतः सर्व बाह्यं बिम्बं विवर्त्स्यति ॥ 89
3.m: Then, that internal knowable seeks to become as if differentiated; / therefore, from the universal seed, the entire external reflection will unfold. // 89

3.s:
kṣobhyakṣobhakabhāvasya satattvaṃ darśitaṃ mayā /
śrīmanmaheśvareṇoktaṃ guruṇā yatprasādataḥ // 90
3.d:
क्षोभ्यक्षोभकभावस्य सतत्त्वं दर्शितं मया ।
श्रीमन्महेश्वरेणोक्तं गुरुणा यत्प्रसादतः ॥ 90
3.m: The true essence of the relation between the agitated and the agitator has been demonstrated by me, / as it was spoken by the venerable Maheśvara, through the grace of the guru. // 90

3.s:
prakṛtaṃ brūmahe nedaṃ bījaṃ varṇacatuṣṭayam /
nāpi yoniryato naitatkṣobhādhāratvamṛcchati // 91
3.d:
प्रकृतं ब्रूमहे नेदं बीजं वर्णचतुष्टयम् ।
नापि योनिर्यतो नैतत्क्षोभाधारत्वमृच्छति ॥ 91
3.m: We return to the topic at hand: this tetrad of phonemes is neither a seed / nor a source-womb, because it does not attain the status of being a receptacle of agitation. // 91

3.s:
ātmanyeva ca viśrāntyā tatproktamamṛtātmakam /
itthaṃ prāguditaṃ yattatpañcakaṃ tatparasparam // 92
3.d:
आत्मन्येव च विश्रान्त्या तत्प्रोक्तममृतात्मकम् ।
इत्थं प्रागुदितं यत्तत्पञ्चकं तत्परस्परम् ॥ 92
3.m: And because it rests in the self alone, it is spoken of as consisting of nectar. / Thus, the pentad described earlier, mutually— // 92

3.s:
ucchaladvividhākāramanyonyavyatimiśraṇāt /
yo'nuttaraḥ paraḥ spando yaścānandaḥ samucchalan // 93
3.d:
उच्छलद्विविधाकारमन्योन्यव्यतिमिश्रणात् ।
योऽनुत्तरः परः स्पन्दो यश्चानन्दः समुच्छलन् ॥ 93
3.m: spurting forth into diverse forms through mutual blending: / that which is the unexcelled supreme vibration (spanda), and that which is blissful spurting forth, // 93

3.s:
tāvicchonmeṣasaṃghaṭṭādgacchato'tivicitratām /
anuttarānandacitī icchāśaktau niyojite // 94
3.d:
ताविच्छोन्मेषसंघट्टाद्गच्छतोऽतिविचित्रताम् ।
अनुत्तरानन्दचिती इच्छाशक्तौ नियोजिते ॥ 94
3.m: those two, through the conjunction of will and opening, attain extreme manifoldness. / When the consciousnesses of the unexcelled and bliss are united in the power of will, // 94

3.s:
trikoṇamiti tatprāhurvisargāmodasundaram /
anuttarānandaśaktī tatra rūḍhimupāgate // 95
3.d:
त्रिकोणमिति तत्प्राहुर्विसर्गामोदसुन्दरम् ।
अनुत्तरानन्दशक्ती तत्र रूढिमुपागते ॥ 95
3.m: they call that the triangle, beautiful with the fragrance of creative emission. / When the powers of the unexcelled and bliss reach maturity therein, // 95

3.s:
trikoṇadvitvayogena vrajataḥ ṣaḍarasthitim /
ta evonmeṣayoge'pi punastanmayatāṃ gate // 96
3.d:
त्रिकोणद्वित्वयोगेन व्रजतः षडरस्थितिम् ।
त एवोन्मेषयोगेऽपि पुनस्तन्मयतां गते ॥ 96
3.m: through the doubling of the triangle they arrive at the state of a six-spoked [figure]. / Those very two, when united with opening, having again become identical with it, // 96

3.s:
kriyāśakteḥ sphuṭaṃ rūpamabhivyaṅktaḥ parasparam /
icchonmeṣagataḥ kṣobho yaḥ proktastadgaterapi // 97
3.d:
क्रियाशक्तेः स्फुटं रूपमभिव्यङ्क्तः परस्परम् ।
इच्छोन्मेषगतः क्षोभो यः प्रोक्तस्तद्गतेरपि ॥ 97
3.m: clearly manifest the form of the power of action (kriyāśakti) mutually. / As for the agitation situated in will and opening that has been spoken of, because of their entering [into that state], // 97

3.s:
te eva śaktī tādrūpyabhāginyau nānyathāsthite /
nanvanuttaratānandau svātmanā bhedavarjitau // 98
3.d:
ते एव शक्ती ताद्रूप्यभागिन्यौ नान्यथास्थिते ।
नन्वनुत्तरतानन्दौ स्वात्मना भेदवर्जितौ ॥ 98
3.m: those very two powers share in that nature, and do not remain otherwise. / [Objection:] Are not the unexcelled and bliss devoid of difference in their essential nature? // 98

3.s:
kathametāvatīmenāṃ vaicitrīṃ svātmani śritau /
śṛṇu tāvadayaṃ saṃvinnātho'parimitātmakaḥ // 99
3.d:
कथमेतावतीमेनां वैचित्रीं स्वात्मनि श्रितौ ।
शृणु तावदयं संविन्नाथोऽपरिमितात्मकः ॥ 99
3.m: How have they resorted to such manifoldness within themselves? / Listen: this Lord of consciousness is unlimited in nature; // 99

3.s:
anantaśaktivaicitryalayodayakaleśvaraḥ /
asthāsyadekarūpeṇa vapuṣā cenmaheśvaraḥ // 100
3.d:
अनन्तशक्तिवैचित्र्यलयोदयकलेश्वरः ।
अस्थास्यदेकरूपेण वपुषा चेन्महेश्वरः ॥ 100
3.m: he is the Lord of the arts of dissolution and arising of endless varieties of power. / If the Great Lord were to remain with a uniform body, // 100

3.s:
maheśvaratvaṃ saṃvittvaṃ tadatyakṣyaddhaṭādivat /
paricchinnaprakāśatvaṃ jaḍasya kila lakṣaṇam // 101
3.d:
महेश्वरत्वं संवित्त्वं तदत्यक्ष्यद्धटादिवत् ।
परिच्छिन्नप्रकाशत्वं जडस्य किल लक्षणम् ॥ 101
3.m: he would forfeit his great sovereignty and his nature as consciousness, like a pot or the like. / For limited luminosity is indeed the defining characteristic of the insentient. // 101

3.s:
jaḍādvilakṣaṇo bodho yato na parimīyate /
tena bodhamahasindhorullāsinyaḥ svaśaktayaḥ // 102
3.d:
जडाद्विलक्षणो बोधो यतो न परिमीयते ।
तेन बोधमहसिन्धोरुल्लासिन्यः स्वशक्तयः ॥ 102
3.m: Consciousness is distinct from the insentient because it cannot be measured; / therefore, his own powers, leaping forth from the great ocean of consciousness, // 102

3.s:
āśrayantyūrmaya iva svātmasaṃghaṭṭacitratām /
svātmasaṃghaṭṭavaicitryaṃ śaktīnāṃ yatparasparam // 103
3.d:
आश्रयन्त्यूर्मय इव स्वात्मसंघट्टचित्रताम् ।
स्वात्मसंघट्टवैचित्र्यं शक्तीनां यत्परस्परम् ॥ 103
3.m: resort, like waves, to the manifoldness of mutual conjunction. / That mutual variety of conjunction of the powers // 103

3.s:
etadeva paraṃ prāhuḥ kriyāśakteḥ sphuṭaṃ vapuḥ /
asmiṃścaturdaśe dhāmni sphuṭībhūtatriśaktike // 104
3.d:
एतदेव परं प्राहुः क्रियाशक्तेः स्फुटं वपुः ।
अस्मिंश्चतुर्दशे धाम्नि स्फुटीभूतत्रिशक्तिके ॥ 104
3.m: is proclaimed to be this very supreme, manifest body of the power of action. / And in this fourteenth abode, wherein the three powers have become manifest, // 104

3.s:
triśūlatvamataḥ prāha śāstā śrīpūrvaśāsane /
nirañjanamidaṃ coktaṃ gurubhistattvadarśibhiḥ // 105
3.d:
त्रिशूलत्वमतः प्राह शास्ता श्रीपूर्वशासने ।
निरञ्जनमिदं चोक्तं गुरुभिस्तत्त्वदर्शिभिः ॥ 105
3.m: the Teacher in the venerable Pūrva teaching therefore spoke of the trident. / And this is declared to be unstained (nirañjana) by the gurus who perceive reality, // 105

3.s:
śaktimānañjyate yasmānna śaktirjātu kenacit /
icchā jñānaṃ kriyā ceti yatpṛthakpṛthagañjyate // 106
3.d:
शक्तिमानञ्ज्यते यस्मान्न शक्तिर्जातु केनचित् ।
इच्छा ज्ञानं क्रिया चेति यत्पृथक्पृथगञ्ज्यते ॥ 106
3.m: because the possessor of power is stained, while the power is never [stained] by anything. / That will, knowledge, and action are manifested separately— // 106

3.s:
tadeva śaktimatsvaiḥ svairiṣyamāṇādikaiḥ sphuṭam /
etattritayamaikyena yadā tu prasphurettadā // 107
3.d:
तदेव शक्तिमत्स्वैः स्वैरिष्यमाणादिकैः स्फुटम् ।
एतत्त्रितयमैक्येन यदा तु प्रस्फुरेत्तदा ॥ 107
3.m: that is clearly the possessor of power through its respective willed [objects] and so on. / But when this triad flashes forth in unity, then // 107

3.s:
na kenacidupādheyaṃ svasvavipratiṣedhataḥ /
lolībhūtamataḥ śaktitritayaṃ tattriśūlakam /
yasminnāśu samāveśādbhavedyogī nirañjanaḥ // 108
3.d:
न केनचिदुपाधेयं स्वस्वविप्रतिषेधतः ।
लोलीभूतमतः शक्तित्रितयं तत्त्रिशूलकम् ।
यस्मिन्नाशु समावेशाद्भवेद्योगी निरञ्जनः ॥ 108
3.m: it cannot be appropriated by anything, because each [power] negates the other. / Therefore, the triad of powers blended together is that trident, / by entering into which swiftly the yogin becomes unstained. // 108

3.s:
itthaṃ parāmṛtapadādārabhyāṣṭakamīdṛśam /
brāhmyādirūpasaṃbhedādyātyaṣṭāṣṭakatāṃ sphuṭam // 109
3.d:
इत्थं परामृतपदादारभ्याष्टकमीदृशम् ।
ब्राह्म्यादिरूपसंभेदाद्यात्यष्टाष्टकतां स्फुटम् ॥ 109
3.m: In this way, starting from the plane of supreme nectar, such an octad / clearly becomes a group of sixty-four through blending with forms such as Brāhmī. // 109

3.s:
atrānuttaraśaktiḥ sā svaṃ vapuḥ prakaṭasthitam /
kurvantyapi jñeyakalākāluṣyādvindurūpiṇī // 110
3.d:
अत्रानुत्तरशक्तिः सा स्वं वपुः प्रकटस्थितम् ।
कुर्वन्त्यपि ज्ञेयकलाकालुष्याद्विन्दुरूपिणी ॥ 110
3.m: Here, that unexcelled power, even while making her own body manifestly present, / takes the form of the point (bindu) due to the turbidness of the fraction of the knowable. // 110

3.s:
uditāyāṃ kriyāśaktau somasūryāgnidhāmani /
avibhāgaḥ prakāśo yaḥ sa binduḥ paramo hi naḥ // 111
3.d:
उदितायां क्रियाशक्तौ सोमसूर्याग्निधामनि ।
अविभागः प्रकाशो यः स बिन्दुः परमो हि नः ॥ 111
3.m: When the power of action has arisen in the abode of moon, sun, and fire, / the undivided luminosity that exists is indeed, for us, the supreme point (bindu). // 111

3.s:
tattvarakṣāvidhāne ca taduktaṃ parameśinā /
hṛtpadmamaṇḍalāntaḥstho naraśaktiśivātmakaḥ // 112
3.d:
तत्त्वरक्षाविधाने च तदुक्तं परमेशिना ।
हृत्पद्ममण्डलान्तःस्थो नरशक्तिशिवात्मकः ॥ 112
3.m:
And in the Tattvarakṣāvidhāna, this is stated by the Supreme Lord:
"Residing within the circle of the heart-lotus, consisting of the person, power, and Śiva,

3.s:
boddhavyo layabhedena vindurvimalatārakaḥ /
yo'sau nādātmakaḥ śabdaḥ sarvaprāṇiṣvavasthitaḥ // 113
3.d:
बोद्धव्यो लयभेदेन विन्दुर्विमलतारकः ।
योऽसौ नादात्मकः शब्दः सर्वप्राणिष्ववस्थितः ॥ 113
3.m:
the bindu, the pure star, is to be known through dissolution and distinction.
That sound, consisting of resonance (nāda), situated in all living beings,

3.s:
adha+ūrdhvavibhāgena niṣkriyeṇāvatiṣṭhate /
hlādataikṣṇyādi vaicitryaṃ sitaraktādikaṃ ca yat // 114
3.d:
अध+ऊर्ध्वविभागेन निष्क्रियेणावतिष्ठते ।
ह्लादतैक्ष्ण्यादि वैचित्र्यं सितरक्तादिकं च यत् ॥ 114
3.m:
abides by way of the division into lower and upper, without activity."
Whatever variety there is—such as delight or sharpness, white or red—,

3.s:
svayaṃ tannirapekṣo'sau prakāśo gururāha ca /
yanna sūryo na vā somo nāgnirbhāsayate'pi ca // 115
3.d:
स्वयं तन्निरपेक्षोऽसौ प्रकाशो गुरुराह च ।
यन्न सूर्यो न वा सोमो नाग्निर्भासयतेऽपि च ॥ 115
3.m:
that luminosity is inherently independent of it. And the Guru said:
"Which neither the sun nor the moon nor even fire illuminates;

3.s:
na cārkasomavahnīnāṃ tatprakāśādvinā mahaḥ /
kimapyasti nijaṃ kiṃ tu saṃviditthaṃ prakāśate // 116
3.d:
न चार्कसोमवह्नीनां तत्प्रकाशाद्विना महः ।
किमप्यस्ति निजं किं तु संविदित्थं प्रकाशते ॥ 116
3.m:
nor do sun, moon, and fire possess any light of their own apart from its light;
rather, consciousness shines forth in this way."

3.s:
svasvātantryaprabhāvodyadvicitropādhisaṃgataḥ /
prakāśo yāti taikṣṇyādimavāntaravicitratām // 117
3.d:
स्वस्वातन्त्र्यप्रभावोद्यद्विचित्रोपाधिसंगतः ।
प्रकाशो याति तैक्ष्ण्यादिमवान्तरविचित्रताम् ॥ 117
3.m:
Conjoined with various limiting adjuncts arising through the power of its own absolute autonomy,
luminosity attains intermediate variety, such as sharpness and the like.

3.s:
durdarśano'pi gharmāṃśuḥ patitaḥ pāthasāṃ pathi /
netrānandatvamabhyeti paśyopādheḥ prabhāvitām // 118
3.d:
दुर्दर्शनोऽपि घर्मांशुः पतितः पाथसां पथि ।
नेत्रानन्दत्वमभ्येति पश्योपाधेः प्रभाविताम् ॥ 118
3.m:
Even the scorching-rayed [sun], hard to look upon, when fallen upon the watery path,
becomes a delight to the eyes: behold the power of the limiting adjunct!

3.s:
sūryādiṣu prakāśo'sāvupādhikaluṣīkṛtaḥ /
saṃvitprakāśaṃ māheśamata eva hyapekṣate // 119
3.d:
सूर्यादिषु प्रकाशोऽसावुपाधिकलुषीकृतः ।
संवित्प्रकाशं माहेशमत एव ह्यपेक्षते ॥ 119
3.m:
This luminosity in the sun and others, contaminated by limiting adjuncts,
therefore depends upon the great Lord's luminosity of consciousness.

3.s:
prakāśamātraṃ suvyaktaṃ sūrya ityucyate sphuṭam /
prakāśyavastusārāṃśavarṣi tatsoma ucyate // 120
3.d:
प्रकाशमात्रं सुव्यक्तं सूर्य इत्युच्यते स्फुटम् ।
प्रकाश्यवस्तुसारांशवर्षि तत्सोम उच्यते ॥ 120
3.m:
Mere luminosity, clearly manifest, is explicitly called the sun;
that which showers the essential portion of the object to be illuminated is called the moon.

3.s:
sūrya pramāṇamityāhuḥ somaṃ meyaṃ pracakṣate /
anyonyamaviyuktau tau svatantrāvapyubhau sthitau // 121
3.d:
सूर्य प्रमाणमित्याहुः सोमं मेयं प्रचक्षते ।
अन्योन्यमवियुक्तौ तौ स्वतन्त्रावप्युभौ स्थितौ ॥ 121
3.m:
They say the sun is the means of knowledge (pramāṇa); they call the moon the object of knowledge (meya).
Though each is independent, both remain inseparable from one another.

3.s:
bhoktṛbhogyobhayātmaitadanyonyonmukhatāṃ gatam /
tato jvalanacidrūpaṃ citrabhānuḥ prakīrtitaḥ // 122
3.d:
भोक्तृभोग्योभयात्मैतदन्योन्योन्मुखतां गतम् ।
ततो ज्वलनचिद्रूपं चित्रभानुः प्रकीर्तितः ॥ 122
3.m:
Consisting of both the enjoyer and the enjoyed, this [pair] enters into mutual orientation;
hence fire, the nature of which is consciousness, is celebrated as Citrabhānu (variegated radiance).

3.s:
yo'yaṃ vahneḥ paraṃ tattvaṃ pramāturidameva tat /
saṃvideva tu vijñeyatādātmyādanapekṣiṇī // 123
3.d:
योऽयं वह्नेः परं तत्त्वं प्रमातुरिदमेव तत् ।
संविदेव तु विज्ञेयतादात्म्यादनपेक्षिणी ॥ 123
3.m:
This supreme reality of fire is precisely that of the knower (pramātṛ);
yet consciousness itself, being independent of identity with the knowable,

3.s:
svatantratvātpramātoktā vicitro jñeyabhedataḥ /
somāṃśadāhyavastūtthavaicitryābhāsabṛṃhitaḥ // 124
3.d:
स्वतन्त्रत्वात्प्रमातोक्ता विचित्रो ज्ञेयभेदतः ।
सोमांशदाह्यवस्तूत्थवैचित्र्याभासबृंहितः ॥ 124
3.m:
is declared to be the knower because of its autonomy, diversified through the diversity of the knowable,
augmented by the appearance of diversity arising from objects to be burned, which are portions of the moon.

3.s:
tata evāgniruditaścitrabhānurmaheśinā /
jñeyādyupāyasaṃghātanirapekṣaiva saṃvidaḥ // 125
3.d:
तत एवाग्निरुदितश्चित्रभानुर्महेशिना ।
ज्ञेयाद्युपायसंघातनिरपेक्षैव संविदः ॥ 125
3.m:
For that very reason, fire was declared to be Citrabhānu by the Great Lord.
Consciousness's abiding as 'I am the knower' is entirely independent

3.s:
sthitirmātāhamasmīti jñātā śāstrajñavadyataḥ /
ajña eva yato jñātānubhavātmā na rūpataḥ // 126
3.d:
स्थितिर्माताहमस्मीति ज्ञाता शास्त्रज्ञवद्यतः ।
अज्ञ एव यतो ज्ञातानुभवात्मा न रूपतः ॥ 126
3.m:
of the aggregate of means [of knowledge] and knowable objects, just as one knowledgeable in scripture knows [without dependence].
For the knower is such by nature of [pure] experience, not through [external] form, unlike an ignorant person.

3.s:
na tu sā jñātṛtā yasyāṃ śuddhajñeyādyapekṣate /
tasyāṃ daśāyāṃ jñātṛtvamucyate yogyatāvaśāt // 127
3.d:
न तु सा ज्ञातृता यस्यां शुद्धज्ञेयाद्यपेक्षते ।
तस्यां दशायां ज्ञातृत्वमुच्यते योग्यतावशात् ॥ 127
3.m:
Yet that is not the [true] state of being a knower in which it depends upon pure objects of knowledge and the like;
in that state, the status of knower is spoken of figuratively, through capacity.

3.s:
mānataiva tu sā prācyapramātṛparikalpitā /
ucchalantyapi saṃvittiḥ kālakramavivarjanāt // 128
3.d:
मानतैव तु सा प्राच्यप्रमातृपरिकल्पिता ।
उच्छलन्त्यपि संवित्तिः कालक्रमविवर्जनात् ॥ 128
3.m:
Indeed, that [state] is merely the state of a means of knowledge, imagined by the primary knower.
Consciousness, even as it surges forth, is devoid of temporal succession;

3.s:
uditaiva satī pūrṇā mātṛmeyādirūpiṇī /
pākādistu kriyā kālaparicchedātkramocitā // 129
3.d:
उदितैव सती पूर्णा मातृमेयादिरूपिणी ।
पाकादिस्तु क्रिया कालपरिच्छेदात्क्रमोचिता ॥ 129
3.m:
arisen indeed, it is full, consisting of knower, knowable, and the rest.
An action like cooking, however, is bound to succession because of determination by time;

3.s:
matāntyakṣaṇavandhyāpi na pākatvaṃ prapadyate /
itthaṃ prakāśatattvasya somasūryāgnitā sthitā // 130
3.d:
मतान्त्यक्षणवन्ध्यापि न पाकत्वं प्रपद्यते ।
इत्थं प्रकाशतत्त्वस्य सोमसूर्याग्निता स्थिता ॥ 130
3.m:
even if devoid of the final moment in thought, it does not attain the condition of cooking.
Thus is established the status of moon, sun, and fire belonging to the principle of luminosity;

3.s:
api mukhyaṃ tatprakāśamātratvaṃ na vyapohyate /
eṣāṃ yatprathamaṃ rūpaṃ hrasvaṃ tatsūrya ucyate // 131
3.d:
अपि मुख्यं तत्प्रकाशमात्रत्वं न व्यपोह्यते ।
एषां यत्प्रथमं रूपं ह्रस्वं तत्सूर्य उच्यते ॥ 131
3.m:
nevertheless, its primary nature as mere luminosity is not abolished.
Their first form, which is short, is called the sun;

3.s:
kṣobhānandavaśāddīrghaviśrāntyā soma ucyate /
yattatparaṃ plutaṃ nāma somānandātparaṃ sthitam // 132
3.d:
क्षोभानन्दवशाद्दीर्घविश्रान्त्या सोम उच्यते ।
यत्तत्परं प्लुतं नाम सोमानन्दात्परं स्थितम् ॥ 132
3.m:
through the force of agitated bliss, by restful repose in the long, it is called the moon;
that supreme [form] called prolated (pluta), situated beyond the bliss of the moon,

3.s:
prakāśarūpaṃ tatprāhurāgneyaṃ śāstrakovidāḥ /
atra prakāśamātraṃ yatsthite dhāmatraye sati // 133
3.d:
प्रकाशरूपं तत्प्राहुराग्नेयं शास्त्रकोविदाः ।
अत्र प्रकाशमात्रं यत्स्थिते धामत्रये सति ॥ 133
3.m:
consisting of luminosity—that, the experts in scripture call fiery.
Here, when the triad of abodes is established, that which is mere luminosity

3.s:
uktaṃ vindutayā śāstre śivavindurasau mataḥ /
makārādanya evāyaṃ tacchāyāmātradhṛdyathā // 134
3.d:
उक्तं विन्दुतया शास्त्रे शिवविन्दुरसौ मतः ।
मकारादन्य एवायं तच्छायामात्रधृद्यथा ॥ 134
3.m:
is stated in scripture as the bindu; it is regarded as the Śiva-bindu.
This is completely distinct from the letter 'm', merely holding its shadow; just as

3.s:
ralahāḥ ṣaṇṭhavaisargavarṇarūpatvasaṃsthitāḥ /
ikāra eva rephāṃśacchāyayānyo yathā svaraḥ // 135
3.d:
रलहाः षण्ठवैसर्गवर्णरूपत्वसंस्थिताः ।
इकार एव रेफांशच्छाययान्यो यथा स्वरः ॥ 135
3.m:
r, l, and h abide as the forms of the neuter and visarga phonemes,
or just as the letter 'i' becomes another vowel through the shadow of a portion of 'r',

3.s:
tathaiva mahaleśādaḥ so'nyo dvedhāsvaro'pi san /
asyāntarvisisṛkṣāsau yā proktā kaulikī parā // 136
3.d:
तथैव महलेशादः सोऽन्यो द्वेधास्वरोऽपि सन् ।
अस्यान्तर्विसिसृक्षासौ या प्रोक्ता कौलिकी परा ॥ 136
3.m:
just so this [bindu] is another, though a non-vowel in two ways, taking a trace of the letter 'm'.
Inside this, that desire to emit which is taught as the supreme Kaula [power],

3.s:
saiva kṣobhavaśādeti visargātmakatāṃ dhruvam /
uktaṃ ca triśiraḥśāstre kalāvyāptyantacarcane // 137
3.d:
सैव क्षोभवशादेति विसर्गात्मकतां ध्रुवम् ।
उक्तं च त्रिशिरःशास्त्रे कलाव्याप्त्यन्तचर्चने ॥ 137
3.m:
that very [power] definitely attains the nature of visarga through the force of agitation.
And it is said in the Triśirobhairavatantra, in the investigation of the limit of pervasion by the kalās:

3.s:
kalā saptadaśī tasmādamṛtākārarūpiṇī /
parāparasvasvarūpabindugatyā visarpitā // 138
3.d:
कला सप्तदशी तस्मादमृताकाररूपिणी ।
परापरस्वस्वरूपबिन्दुगत्या विसर्पिता ॥ 138
3.m:
"Therefore the seventeenth kalā, whose nature is of the form of nectar,
having spread forth through the movement of the bindu, which is its own supreme and intermediate nature,

3.s:
prakāśyaṃ sarvavastūnāṃ visargarahitā tu sā /
śaktikuṇḍalikā caiva prāṇakuṇḍalikā tathā // 139
3.d:
प्रकाश्यं सर्ववस्तूनां विसर्गरहिता तु सा ।
शक्तिकुण्डलिका चैव प्राणकुण्डलिका तथा ॥ 139
3.m:
is the illumination of all entities; but devoid of creative emission (visarga),
she is indeed the power Kuṇḍalikā, and likewise the vital Kuṇḍalikā;

3.s:
visargaprāntadeśe tu parā kuṇḍalinīti ca /
śivavyometi paramaṃ brahmātmasthānamucyate // 140
3.d:
विसर्गप्रान्तदेशे तु परा कुण्डलिनीति च ।
शिवव्योमेति परमं ब्रह्मात्मस्थानमुच्यते ॥ 140
3.m:
at the boundary of creative emission, however, [she is] the supreme Kuṇḍalinī."
The void of Śiva is called the supreme place, whose self is Brahman.

3.s:
visargamātraṃ nāthasya sṛṣṭisaṃhāravibhramāḥ /
svātmanaḥ svātmani svātmakṣepo vaisargikī sthitiḥ // 141
3.d:
विसर्गमात्रं नाथस्य सृष्टिसंहारविभ्रमाः ।
स्वात्मनः स्वात्मनि स्वात्मक्षेपो वैसर्गिकी स्थितिः ॥ 141
3.m:
The Lord's play of creation and dissolution is merely creative emission;
the casting of oneself into oneself by oneself is the state of creative emission.

3.s:
visarga evamutsṛṣṭa āśyānatvamupāgataḥ /
haṃsaḥ prāṇo vyañjanaṃ ca sparśaśca paribhāṣyate // 142
3.d:
विसर्ग एवमुत्सृष्ट आश्यानत्वमुपागतः ।
हंसः प्राणो व्यञ्जनं च स्पर्शश्च परिभाष्यते ॥ 142
3.m:
Creative emission thus emitted, having reached a congealed state,
is designated as the haṃsa, vital breath, consonant, and stop consonant (sparśa).

3.s:
anuttaraṃ paraṃ dhāma tadevākulamucyate /
visargastasya nāthasya kaulikī śaktirucyate // 143
3.d:
अनुत्तरं परं धाम तदेवाकुलमुच्यते ।
विसर्गस्तस्य नाथस्य कौलिकी शक्तिरुच्यते ॥ 143
3.m:
The unexcelled, supreme abode is alone called Akula;
creative emission is called the Kaula power of that Lord.

3.s:
visargatā ca saivāsyā yadānandodayakramāt /
spaṣṭībhūtakriyāśaktiparyantā procchalatsthitiḥ // 144
3.d:
विसर्गता च सैवास्या यदानन्दोदयक्रमात् ।
स्पष्टीभूतक्रियाशक्तिपर्यन्ता प्रोच्छलत्स्थितिः ॥ 144
3.m:
And her state of creative emission is precisely this: an upsurging condition,
which, through the succession of the rise of bliss, terminates in the clearly manifest power of action.

3.s:
visarga eva tāvānyadākṣiptaitāvadātmakaḥ /
iyadrūpaṃ sāgarasya yadanantormisaṃtatiḥ // 145
3.d:
विसर्ग एव तावान्यदाक्षिप्तैतावदात्मकः ।
इयद्रूपं सागरस्य यदनन्तोर्मिसंततिः ॥ 145
3.m:
Creative emission is only so extensive as to contain all this within itself;
such is the nature of the ocean, which consists of an endless succession of waves.

3.s:
ata eva visargo'yamavyaktahakalātmakaḥ /
kāmatattvamiti śrīmatkulaguhvara ucyate // 146
3.d:
अत एव विसर्गोऽयमव्यक्तहकलात्मकः ।
कामतत्त्वमिति श्रीमत्कुलगुह्वर उच्यते ॥ 146
3.m:
Therefore, this creative emission, consisting of the unmanifest kalā 'h',
is called the reality of desire (kāmatattva) in the venerable Kulaguhvara:

3.s:
yattadakṣaramavyakta kāntākaṇṭhe vyavasthitam /
dhvanirūpamanicchaṃ tu dhyānadhāraṇavarjitam // 147
3.d:
यत्तदक्षरमव्यक्त कान्ताकण्ठे व्यवस्थितम् ।
ध्वनिरूपमनिच्छं तु ध्यानधारणवर्जितम् ॥ 147
3.m:
"That unmanifest syllable situated in the throat of the beloved,
consisting of sound, beyond desire, free of meditation and concentration—

3.s:
tatra cittaṃ samādhāya vaśayedyugapajjagat /
ata eva visargasya haṃse yadvatsphuṭā sthitiḥ // 148
3.d:
तत्र चित्तं समाधाय वशयेद्युगपज्जगत् ।
अत एव विसर्गस्य हंसे यद्वत्स्फुटा स्थितिः ॥ 148
3.m:
fixing the mind on that, one would simultaneously subjugate the universe."
Therefore, just as the presence of creative emission in haṃsa is evident,

3.s:
tadvatsānuttarādīnāṃ kādisāntatayā sthitiḥ /
anuttarātkavargasya sūtiḥ pañcātmanaḥ sphuṭam // 149
3.d:
तद्वत्सानुत्तरादीनां कादिसान्ततया स्थितिः ।
अनुत्तरात्कवर्गस्य सूतिः पञ्चात्मनः स्फुटम् ॥ 149
3.m:
so too the presence of the unexcelled and subsequent [vowels] in the consonants from 'k' to 's' is evident.
From the unexcelled clearly arises the fivefold k-series (kavarga),

3.s:
pañcaśaktyātmatovaśa ekaikatra yathā sphuṭaḥ /
icchāśakteḥ svasvarūpasaṃsthāyā ekarūpataḥ // 150
3.d:
पञ्चशक्त्यात्मतोवश एकैकत्र यथा स्फुटः ।
इच्छाशक्तेः स्वस्वरूपसंस्थाया एकरूपतः ॥ 150
3.m:
just as the power of consisting of the five powers is clearly distinct in each single one.
From the power of will, abiding in its own nature as unitary,

3.s:
cavargaḥ pañcaśaktyātmā kramaprasphuṭatātmakaḥ /
yā tūktā jñeyakāluṣyabhākkṣipracarayogataḥ // 151
3.d:
चवर्गः पञ्चशक्त्यात्मा क्रमप्रस्फुटतात्मकः ।
या तूक्ता ज्ञेयकालुष्यभाक्क्षिप्रचरयोगतः ॥ 151
3.m:
the c-series (cavarga) arises, consisting of five powers and having the nature of gradual manifestation.
That [power of will], however, which is spoken of as having the contamination of the knowable through its connection with rapid movement,

3.s:
dvirūpāyāstato jātaṃ ṭa-tādyaṃ vargayugmakam /
unmeṣātpādivargastu yato viśvaṃ samāpyate // 152
3.d:
द्विरूपायास्ततो जातं ट-ताद्यं वर्गयुग्मकम् ।
उन्मेषात्पादिवर्गस्तु यतो विश्वं समाप्यते ॥ 152
3.m:
having a twofold form—from it arose the pair of series beginning with 'ṭ' and 't'.
From the unfolding [of consciousness] (unmeṣa) arises the p-series, where the universe terminates;

3.s:
jñeyarūpamidaṃ pañcaviṃśatyantaṃ yataḥ sphuṭam /
jñeyatvātsphuṭataḥ proktametāvatsparśarūpakam // 153
3.d:
ज्ञेयरूपमिदं पञ्चविंशत्यन्तं यतः स्फुटम् ।
ज्ञेयत्वात्स्फुटतः प्रोक्तमेतावत्स्पर्शरूपकम् ॥ 153
3.m:
for this knowable universe clearly terminates with the twenty-fifth [tattva].
Because of its knowability, so much is clearly declared to be of the nature of contacts (sparśa, stops).

3.s:
icchāśaktiśca yā dvedhā kṣubhitākṣubhitatvataḥ /
sā vijātīyaśaktyaṃśapronmukhī yāti yātmatām // 154
3.d:
इच्छाशक्तिश्च या द्वेधा क्षुभिताक्षुभितत्वतः ।
सा विजातीयशक्त्यंशप्रोन्मुखी याति यात्मताम् ॥ 154
3.m:
And the power of will, which is twofold through being agitated and unagitated,
becoming oriented toward an aspect of heterogeneous power, becomes the letter 'y'.

3.s:
saiva śīghrataropāttajñeyakāluṣyarūṣitā /
vijātīyonmukhatvena ratvaṃ latvaṃ ca gacchati // 155
3.d:
सैव शीघ्रतरोपात्तज्ञेयकालुष्यरूषिता ।
विजातीयोन्मुखत्वेन रत्वं लत्वं च गच्छति ॥ 155
3.m:
That very [power], smeared with the contamination of the knowable seized very rapidly,
through orientation toward the heterogeneous, goes to the state of 'r' and 'l'.

3.s:
tadvadunmeṣaśaktirdvirūpā vaijātyaśaktigā /
vakāratvaṃ prapadyeta sṛṣṭisārapravarṣakam // 156
3.d:
तद्वदुन्मेषशक्तिर्द्विरूपा वैजात्यशक्तिगा ।
वकारत्वं प्रपद्येत सृष्टिसारप्रवर्षकम् ॥ 156
3.m:
Likewise, the power of unfolding (unmeṣa), twofold, entering heterogeneous power,
would attain the condition of the letter 'v', showering down the essence of creation.

3.s:
icchaivānuttarānandayātā śīghratvayogataḥ /
vāyurityucyate vahnirbhāsanātsthairyato dharā // 157
3.d:
इच्छैवानुत्तरानन्दयाता शीघ्रत्वयोगतः ।
वायुरित्युच्यते वह्निर्भासनात्स्थैर्यतो धरा ॥ 157
3.m:
The will itself, having attained unexcelled bliss, through conjunction with rapidity
is called wind; fire through shining; earth through stability.

3.s:
idaṃ catuṣkamantaḥsthamata eva nigadyate /
icchādyantargatatvena svasamāptau ca saṃsthiteḥ // 158
3.d:
इदं चतुष्कमन्तःस्थमत एव निगद्यते ।
इच्छाद्यन्तर्गतत्वेन स्वसमाप्तौ च संस्थितेः ॥ 158
3.m: This tetrad is spoken of as internal for this very reason: / because it rests within desire and the others, and because it abides in its own culmination.

3.s:
sajātīyakaśaktīnāmicchādyānāṃ ca yojanam /
kṣobhātmakamidaṃ prāhuḥ kṣobhākṣobhātmanāmapi // 159
3.d:
सजातीयकशक्तीनामिच्छाद्यानां च योजनम् ।
क्षोभात्मकमिदं प्राहुः क्षोभाक्षोभात्मनामपि ॥ 159
3.m: And the union of powers of the same kind, beginning with desire, / they declare to be agitation; it is so even for those whose nature is agitation and non-agitation.

3.s:
anuttarasya sājātye bhavettu dvitayī gatiḥ /
anuttaraṃ yattatraikaṃ taccedānandasūtaye // 160
3.d:
अनुत्तरस्य साजात्ये भवेत्तु द्वितयी गतिः ।
अनुत्तरं यत्तत्रैकं तच्चेदानन्दसूतये ॥ 160
3.m: In the case of homogeneity with the unexcelled, however, there are two courses: / the unexcelled that is singular there, if it is for the generation of bliss,

3.s:
prabhaviṣyati tadyoge yogaḥ kṣobhātmakaḥ sphuṭaḥ /
atrāpyanuttaraṃ dhāma dvitīyamapi sūtaye // 161
3.d:
प्रभविष्यति तद्योगे योगः क्षोभात्मकः स्फुटः ।
अत्राप्यनुत्तरं धाम द्वितीयमपि सूतये ॥ 161
3.m: will be capable, then in that union the union clearly consists of agitation. / Here too, when the second unexcelled abode is also for generation,

3.s:
na paryāptaṃ tadā kṣobhaṃ vinaivānuttarātmatā /
icchā yā karmaṇā hīnā yā caiṣṭavyena rūṣitā // 162
3.d:
न पर्याप्तं तदा क्षोभं विनैवानुत्तरात्मता ।
इच्छा या कर्मणा हीना या चैष्टव्येन रूषिता ॥ 162
3.m: and not sufficient [for it], then the nature of the unexcelled is without any agitation at all. / The desire that is devoid of an object of action, and that which is tinged by what is to be desired,

3.s:
śīghrasthairyaprabhinnena tridhā bhāvamupāgatā /
anunmiṣitamunmīlatpronmīlitamiti sthitam // 163
3.d:
शीघ्रस्थैर्यप्रभिन्नेन त्रिधा भावमुपागता ।
अनुन्मिषितमुन्मीलत्प्रोन्मीलितमिति स्थितम् ॥ 163
3.m: has attained a threefold state differentiated by swiftness and stability, / existing as: unbloomed, blooming, and fully blossomed.

3.s:
iṣyamāṇaṃ tridhaitasyāṃ tādrūpyasyāparicyuteḥ /
tadeva svoṣmaṇā svātmasvātantryapreraṇātmanā // 164
3.d:
इष्यमाणं त्रिधैतस्यां ताद्रूप्यस्यापरिच्युतेः ।
तदेव स्वोष्मणा स्वात्मस्वातन्त्र्यप्रेरणात्मना ॥ 164
3.m: What is desired in this [desire] is threefold, without losing its identical nature; / this very [triad], through its own warmth consisting of the impulsion of its own absolute autonomy,

3.s:
bahirbhāvya sphuṭaṃ kṣiptaṃ śa-ṣa-satritayaṃ sthitam /
tata eva sakāre'sminsphuṭaṃ viśvaṃ prakāśate // 165
3.d:
बहिर्भाव्य स्फुटं क्षिप्तं श-ष-सत्रितयं स्थितम् ।
तत एव सकारेऽस्मिन्स्फुटं विश्वं प्रकाशते ॥ 165
3.m: having been externalised, is clearly cast forth and stands as the triad śa, ṣa, and sa. / Therefore, in this letter sa the universe clearly shines forth.

3.s:
amṛtaṃ ca paraṃ dhāma yoginastatpracakṣate /
kṣobhādyantavirāmeṣu tadeva ca parāmṛtam // 166
3.d:
अमृतं च परं धाम योगिनस्तत्प्रचक्षते ।
क्षोभाद्यन्तविरामेषु तदेव च परामृतम् ॥ 166
3.m: And yogins declare it to be nectar, the supreme abode; / and at the cessation of the beginning and end of agitation, it is this very supreme nectar.

3.s:
sītkārasukhasadbhāvasamāveśasamādhiṣu /
tadeva brahma paramamavibhaktaṃ pracakṣate // 167
3.d:
सीत्कारसुखसद्भावसमावेशसमाधिषु ।
तदेव ब्रह्म परममविभक्तं प्रचक्षते ॥ 167
3.m: In the hiss of pleasure, reality, immersion, and absorption, / they declare it to be this very supreme, undivided Brahman.

3.s:
uvāca bhagavāneva tacchrīmatkulaguhkare /
śaktiśaktimadaikātmyalabdhānvarthābhidhānake // 168
3.d:
उवाच भगवानेव तच्छ्रीमत्कुलगुह्करे ।
शक्तिशक्तिमदैकात्म्यलब्धान्वर्थाभिधानके ॥ 168
3.m: The Lord himself said this in the venerable Kulaguhvara, / which received a meaningful name from the identity of power and the possessor of power:

3.s:
kākacañcupuṭākāraṃ dhyānadhāraṇavarjitam /
viṣatattvamanackākhyaṃ tava snehātprakāśitam // 169
3.d:
काकचञ्चुपुटाकारं ध्यानधारणवर्जितम् ।
विषतत्त्वमनच्काख्यं तव स्नेहात्प्रकाशितम् ॥ 169
3.m: "Having the form of a crow's beak, devoid of meditation and concentration, / the principle of poison, called 'vowelless', has been revealed out of love for you.

3.s:
kāmasya pūrṇatā tattvaṃ saṃghaṭṭe pravibhāvyate /
viṣasya cāmṛtaṃ tattvaṃ chādyatve'ṇoścyute sati // 170
3.d:
कामस्य पूर्णता तत्त्वं संघट्टे प्रविभाव्यते ।
विषस्य चामृतं तत्त्वं छाद्यत्वेऽणोश्च्युते सति ॥ 170
3.m: The reality of desire is fullness, conceived in mutual friction; / and the reality of poison is nectar when the soul's state of being veiled has ceased.

3.s:
vyāptrī śaktirviṣaṃ yasmādavyāptuśchādayenmahaḥ /
nirañjanaṃ paraṃ dhāma tattvaṃ tasya tu sāñjanam // 171
3.d:
व्याप्त्री शक्तिर्विषं यस्मादव्याप्तुश्छादयेन्महः ।
निरञ्जनं परं धाम तत्त्वं तस्य तु साञ्जनम् ॥ 171
3.m: Because the all-pervading power is poison, it conceals the splendour of the non-pervader. / The supreme abode is unblemished, but its reality is tinged with blemish.

3.s:
kriyāśaktyātmakaṃ viśvamayaṃ tasmātsphuredyataḥ /
icchā kāmo viṣaṃ jñānaṃ kriyā devī nirañjanam // 172
3.d:
क्रियाशक्त्यात्मकं विश्वमयं तस्मात्स्फुरेद्यतः ।
इच्छा कामो विषं ज्ञानं क्रिया देवी निरञ्जनम् ॥ 172
3.m: Because the universe, consisting of the power of action, pulses from it: / desire is Kāma, poison is knowledge, the Goddess is action, [and] the unblemished."

3.s:
etattrayasamāveśaḥ śivo bhairava ucyate /
atra rūḍhiṃ sadā kuryāditi no guravo jaguḥ // 173
3.d:
एतत्त्रयसमावेशः शिवो भैरव उच्यते ।
अत्र रूढिं सदा कुर्यादिति नो गुरवो जगुः ॥ 173
3.m: The absorption in these three is called Śiva, Bhairava; / "One should always take root here," thus our gurus have sung.

3.s:
viṣatattve saṃpraviśya na bhūtaṃ na viṣaṃ na ca /
grahaḥ kevala evāhamiti bhāvanayā sphuret // 174
3.d:
विषतत्त्वे संप्रविश्य न भूतं न विषं न च ।
ग्रहः केवल एवाहमिति भावनया स्फुरेत् ॥ 174
3.m: Having entered into the principle of poison, neither element nor poison, / nor grasping [exists]: he should pulse with the contemplation, "I am purely alone."

3.s:
nanvatra ṣaṇṭhavarṇebhyo janmoktaṃ tena ṣaṇṭhatā /
kathaṃ syāditi cedbrūmo nātra ṣaṇṭhasya sotṛtā // 175
3.d:
नन्वत्र षण्ठवर्णेभ्यो जन्मोक्तं तेन षण्ठता ।
कथं स्यादिति चेद्ब्रूमो नात्र षण्ठस्य सोतृता ॥ 175
3.m: Now, if it is objected: "Here their birth is stated to be from the neuter letters; / how then can they be neuter?" We reply: the neuter is not a generator here.

3.s:
tathāhi tatragā yāsāvicchāśaktirudīritā /
saiva sūte svakartavyamantaḥsthaṃ sveṣṭarūpakam // 176
3.d:
तथाहि तत्रगा यासाविच्छाशक्तिरुदीरिता ।
सैव सूते स्वकर्तव्यमन्तःस्थं स्वेष्टरूपकम् ॥ 176
3.m: For that power of desire mentioned as residing there / is the very one that generates what is to be done by itself, internal, having the form of its own desired [object].

3.s:
yattvatra rūṣaṇāhetureṣitavyaṃ sthitaṃ tataḥ /
bhāgānna prasavastajjaṃ kāluṣyaṃ tadvapuśca tat // 177
3.d:
यत्त्वत्र रूषणाहेतुरेषितव्यं स्थितं ततः ।
भागान्न प्रसवस्तज्जं कालुष्यं तद्वपुश्च तत् ॥ 177
3.m: As for that which is the cause of tingeing here, the desired object, it is situated / from a part from which there is no generation; the turbidity born of it is its form.

3.s:
jñeyārūṣaṇayā yuktaṃ samudāyātmakaṃ viduḥ /
ṣaṇṭhaṃ kṣobhakatākṣobhadhāmatvābhāvayogataḥ // 178
3.d:
ज्ञेयारूषणया युक्तं समुदायात्मकं विदुः ।
षण्ठं क्षोभकताक्षोभधामत्वाभावयोगतः ॥ 178
3.m: They know [the neuter] as endowed with the tingeing by the knowable, consisting of an aggregate, / because the neuter is devoid of the state of being an agitator or an unagitated abode.

3.s:
etadvarṇacatuṣkasya svoṣmaṇābhāsanāvaśāt /
ūṣmeti kathitaṃ nāma bhairaveṇāmalātmanā // 179
3.d:
एतद्वर्णचतुष्कस्य स्वोष्मणाभासनावशात् ।
ऊष्मेति कथितं नाम भैरवेणामलात्मना ॥ 179
3.m: Because this tetrad of letters shines forth through its own warmth, / the pure-natured Bhairava declared its name to be 'sibilants' (warmths).

3.s:
kādi-hāntamidaṃ prahuḥ kṣobhādhāratayā budhāḥ /
yonirūpeṇa tasyāpi yoge kṣobhāntaraṃ vrajet // 180
3.d:
कादि-हान्तमिदं प्रहुः क्षोभाधारतया बुधाः ।
योनिरूपेण तस्यापि योगे क्षोभान्तरं व्रजेत् ॥ 180
3.m: The wise speak of this [group] from ka to ha as the receptacle of agitation; / through its union with the yoni, it would enter into another agitation.

3.s:
tannidarśanayogena pañcāśattamavarṇatā /
pañcaviṃśakasaṃjñeyaprāgvadbhūmisusaṃsthitam // 181
3.d:
तन्निदर्शनयोगेन पञ्चाशत्तमवर्णता ।
पञ्चविंशकसंज्ञेयप्राग्वद्भूमिसुसंस्थितम् ॥ 181
3.m: Through connection with that example, it attains the state of the fiftieth letter; / the well-situated earth [is here] as before, known as the twenty-fifth.

3.s:
catuṣkaṃ ca catuṣkaṃ ca bhedābhedagataṃ kramāt /
ādyaṃ catuṣkaṃ saṃvitterbhedasaṃdhānakovidam // 182
3.d:
चतुष्कं च चतुष्कं च भेदाभेदगतं क्रमात् ।
आद्यं चतुष्कं संवित्तेर्भेदसंधानकोविदम् ॥ 182
3.m: And tetrad and tetrad relate successively to difference and non-difference: / the first tetrad of consciousness is skilled in bringing about difference,

3.s:
bhedasyābhedarūḍhyekaheturanyaccatuṣṭayam /
itthaṃ yadvarṇajātaṃ tatsarva svaramayaṃ purā // 183
3.d:
भेदस्याभेदरूढ्येकहेतुरन्यच्चतुष्टयम् ।
इत्थं यद्वर्णजातं तत्सर्व स्वरमयं पुरा ॥ 183
3.m: while the other tetrad is the sole cause of taking root in non-difference from difference. / Thus, whatever collection of letters [exists], it was all previously of the nature of vowels.

3.s:
vyaktiyogādvyañjanaṃ tatsvaraprāṇaṃ yataḥ kila /
svarāṇāṃ ṣaṭkameveha mūlaṃ syādvarṇasaṃtatau // 184
3.d:
व्यक्तियोगाद्व्यञ्जनं तत्स्वरप्राणं यतः किल ।
स्वराणां षट्कमेवेह मूलं स्याद्वर्णसंततौ ॥ 184
3.m: Through connection with manifestation it is a consonant, since its life-breath is indeed the vowel; / only the sextet of vowels would be the root here in the continuous series of letters.

3.s:
ṣaḍdevatāstu tā eva ye mukhyāḥ sūryaraśmayaḥ /
saurāṇāmeva raśmīnāmantaścāndrakalā yataḥ // 185
3.d:
षड्देवतास्तु ता एव ये मुख्याः सूर्यरश्मयः ।
सौराणामेव रश्मीनामन्तश्चान्द्रकला यतः ॥ 185
3.m: Those six deities are indeed the primary rays of the sun, / because the digits of the moon are within the solar rays themselves.

3.s:
ato'tra dīrghatritayaṃ sphuṭaṃ cāndramasaṃ vapuḥ /
candraśca nāma naivānyo bhogyaṃ bhoktuśca nāparam // 186
3.d:
अतोऽत्र दीर्घत्रितयं स्फुटं चान्द्रमसं वपुः ।
चन्द्रश्च नाम नैवान्यो भोग्यं भोक्तुश्च नापरम् ॥ 186
3.m: Therefore, the triad of long vowels here clearly has a lunar form; / and the moon is indeed none other than the enjoyed, and the enjoyer is none other.

3.s:
bhoktaiva bhogyabhāvena dvaividhyātsaṃvyavasthitaḥ /
ghaṭasya na hi bhogyatvaṃ svaṃ vapurmātṛgaṃ hi tat // 187
3.d:
भोक्तैव भोग्यभावेन द्वैविध्यात्संव्यवस्थितः ।
घटस्य न हि भोग्यत्वं स्वं वपुर्मातृगं हि तत् ॥ 187
3.m: The enjoyer himself is established in two ways in the form of the enjoyed; / for the pot's being an object of enjoyment is not its own form, for that resides in the subject.

3.s:
ato mātari yā rūḍhiḥ sāsya bhogyatvamucyate /
anuttaraṃ parāmṛśyaparāmarśakabhāvataḥ // 188
3.d:
अतो मातरि या रूढिः सास्य भोग्यत्वमुच्यते ।
अनुत्तरं परामृश्यपरामर्शकभावतः ॥ 188
3.m: Therefore, the rooting that takes place in the subject is called its status as enjoyed. / The unexcelled, through the relation of reflective awareness and that which is reflectively aware,

3.s:
saṃghaṭṭarūpatāṃ prāptaṃ bhogyamicchādikaṃ tathā /
anuttarānandabhuvāmicchādye bhogyatāṃ gate // 189
3.d:
संघट्टरूपतां प्राप्तं भोग्यमिच्छादिकं तथा ।
अनुत्तरानन्दभुवामिच्छाद्ये भोग्यतां गते ॥ 189
3.m: attained the form of mutual friction, and likewise desire and the rest [became] the enjoyed; / when desire and the rest, born of the unexcelled and bliss, have become the enjoyed,

3.s:
saṃdhyakṣarāṇāmudayo bhoktṛrūpaṃ ca kathyate /
anuttarānandamayo devo bhoktaiva kathyate // 190
3.d:
संध्यक्षराणामुदयो भोक्तृरूपं च कथ्यते ।
अनुत्तरानन्दमयो देवो भोक्तैव कथ्यते ॥ 190
3.m: the arising of diphthongs and the form of the enjoyer is proclaimed. / The Lord consisting of the unexcelled and bliss is spoken of as the enjoyer alone.

3.s:
icchādikaṃ bhogyameva tata evāsya śaktitā /
bhogyaṃ bhoktari līnaṃ ced bhoktā tadvastutaḥ sphuṭaḥ // 191
3.d:
इच्छादिकं भोग्यमेव तत एवास्य शक्तिता ।
भोग्यं भोक्तरि लीनं चेद् भोक्ता तद्वस्तुतः स्फुटः ॥ 191
3.m: Desire and the rest are simply the enjoyed; precisely therefore do they have the status of power. / If the enjoyed is dissolved in the enjoyer, the enjoyer is clearly so in reality.

3.s:
ataḥ ṣaṇṇāṃ trikaṃ sāraṃ cidiṣyunmeṣaṇātmakam /
tadeva tritayaṃ prāhurbhairavasya paraṃ mahaḥ // 192
3.d:
अतः षण्णां त्रिकं सारं चिदिष्युन्मेषणात्मकम् ।
तदेव त्रितयं प्राहुर्भैरवस्य परं महः ॥ 192
3.m: Therefore the triad of the six is the essence, consisting of consciousness, desire, and blooming; / that very triad they call the supreme splendour of Bhairava.

3.s:
tattrikaṃ parameśasya pūrṇā śaktiḥ pragīyate /
tenākṣiptaṃ yato viśvamato'sminsamupāsite // 193
3.d:
तत्त्रिकं परमेशस्य पूर्णा शक्तिः प्रगीयते ।
तेनाक्षिप्तं यतो विश्वमतोऽस्मिन्समुपासिते ॥ 193
3.m: That triad is sung as the complete power of the supreme Lord; / because the universe is implied by it, therefore when this is worshipped,

3.s:
viśvaśaktāvavacchedavandhye jātamupāsanam /
ityeṣa mahimaitāvāniti tāvanna śakyate // 194
3.d:
विश्वशक्ताववच्छेदवन्ध्ये जातमुपासनम् ।
इत्येष महिमैतावानिति तावन्न शक्यते ॥ 194
3.m: worship is performed in the universal power free of limitation. / Thus, "Such is this greatness!" cannot be [limited] so far.

3.s:
aparicchinnaśakteḥ kaḥ kuryācchaktiparicchidām /
tasmādanuttaro devaḥ svācchandyānuttaratvataḥ // 195
3.d:
अपरिच्छिन्नशक्तेः कः कुर्याच्छक्तिपरिच्छिदाम् ।
तस्मादनुत्तरो देवः स्वाच्छन्द्यानुत्तरत्वतः ॥ 195
3.m: Who could make a delimitation of the power of one whose power is uncircumscribed? / Therefore the unexcelled Lord, because of the unexcelled nature of his freedom,

3.s:
visargaśaktiyuktatvātsaṃpanno viśvarūpakaḥ /
evaṃ pañcāśadāmarśapūrṇaśaktirmaheśvaraḥ // 196
3.d:
विसर्गशक्तियुक्तत्वात्संपन्नो विश्वरूपकः ।
एवं पञ्चाशदामर्शपूर्णशक्तिर्महेश्वरः ॥ 196
3.m: and because of being endowed with the power of creative emission, has become omniform. / Thus the Great Lord, whose power is complete with the fifty reflective awarenesses,

3.s:
vimarśātmaika evānyāḥ śaktayo'traiva niṣṭhitāḥ /
ekāśītipadā devī hyatrāntarbhāvayiṣyate // 197
3.d:
विमर्शात्मैक एवान्याः शक्तयोऽत्रैव निष्ठिताः ।
एकाशीतिपदा देवी ह्यत्रान्तर्भावयिष्यते ॥ 197
3.m: is singular, consisting of reflective awareness; the other powers are established right here. / The Goddess of eighty-one words will indeed be included here.

3.s:
ekāmarśasvabhāvatve śabdarāśiḥ sa bhairavaḥ /
āmṛśyacchāyayā yogātsaiva śaktiśca mātṛkā // 198
3.d:
एकामर्शस्वभावत्वे शब्दराशिः स भैरवः ।
आमृश्यच्छायया योगात्सैव शक्तिश्च मातृका ॥ 198
3.m: When having the nature of a single reflective awareness, that aggregate of words is Bhairava; / and through union with the reflection of that which is cognised, that very [aggregate] is the power Mātṛkā.

3.s:
sā śabdarāśisaṃghaṭṭādbhinnayonistu mālinī /
prāgvannavatayāmarśātpṛthagvargasvarūpiṇī // 199
3.d:
सा शब्दराशिसंघट्टाद्भिन्नयोनिस्तु मालिनी ।
प्राग्वन्नवतयामर्शात्पृथग्वर्गस्वरूपिणी ॥ 199
3.m: From the friction of that aggregate of words, however, she whose origin is distinct is Mālinī, / consisting of distinct classes through reflective awareness as a novenad as before.

3.s:
ekaikāmarśarūḍhau tu saiva pañcāśadātmikā /
itthaṃ nādānuvedhena parāmarśasvabhāvakaḥ // 200
3.d:
एकैकामर्शरूढौ तु सैव पञ्चाशदात्मिका ।
इत्थं नादानुवेधेन परामर्शस्वभावकः ॥ 200
3.m: When rooted in each single reflective awareness, however, she consists of the fifty. / Thus, through interpenetration with sound, possessing the nature of reflective awareness,

3.s:
śivo mātāpitṛtvena kartā viśvatra saṃsthitaḥ /
visarga eva śākto'yaṃ śivabindutayā punaḥ // 201
3.d:
शिवो मातापितृत्वेन कर्ता विश्वत्र संस्थितः ।
विसर्ग एव शाक्तोऽयं शिवबिन्दुतया पुनः ॥ 201
3.m: Śiva resides everywhere as the agent, through the status of mother and father. / This creative emission belongs to Śakti; again, through the state of the Śiva-bindu,

3.s:
garbhīkṛtānantaviśvaḥ śrayate'nuttarātmatām /
aparicchinnaviśvāntaḥsāre svātmani yaḥ prabhoḥ // 202
3.d:
गर्भीकृतानन्तविश्वः श्रयतेऽनुत्तरात्मताम् ।
अपरिच्छिन्नविश्वान्तःसारे स्वात्मनि यः प्रभोः ॥ 202
3.m: having internalised the infinite universe, it resorts to the state of the unexcelled. / That which is the reflective awareness of the Lord in his own self, the inner essence of the uncircumscribed universe,

3.s:
parāmarśaḥ sa evokto dvayasaṃpattilakṣaṇaḥ /
anuttaravisargātmaśivaśaktyadvayātmani // 203
3.d:
परामर्शः स एवोक्तो द्वयसंपत्तिलक्षणः ।
अनुत्तरविसर्गात्मशिवशक्त्यद्वयात्मनि ॥ 203
3.m: is declared to be characterised by the attainment of the pair, / in the non-dual self of Śiva and Śakti whose nature is the unexcelled and creative emission.

3.s:
parāmarśo nirbharatvādahamityucyate vibhoḥ /
anuttarādyā prasṛtirhāntā śaktisvarūpiṇī // 204
3.d:
परामर्शो निर्भरत्वादहमित्युच्यते विभोः ।
अनुत्तराद्या प्रसृतिर्हान्ता शक्तिस्वरूपिणी ॥ 204
3.m: Because of its fullness, the reflective awareness of the all-pervading Lord is called 'I' ('aham'). / The emission beginning with the unexcelled ('a') and ending in 'ha' is the very nature of [His] power.

3.s:
pratyāhṛtāśeṣaviśvānuttare sā nilīyate /
tadidaṃ viśvamantaḥsthaṃ śaktau sānuttare pare // 205
3.d:
प्रत्याहृताशेषविश्वानुत्तरे सा निलीयते ।
तदिदं विश्वमन्तःस्थं शक्तौ सानुत्तरे परे ॥ 205
3.m: Having withdrawn the entire universe, she dissolves into the unexcelled; / thus, this universe resides within power, and she within the supreme unexcelled.

3.s:
tattasyāmiti yatsatyaṃ vibhunā saṃpuṭīkṛtiḥ /
tena śrītrīśikāśāstre śakteḥ saṃpuṭitākṛtiḥ // 206
3.d:
तत्तस्यामिति यत्सत्यं विभुना संपुटीकृतिः ।
तेन श्रीत्रीशिकाशास्त्रे शक्तेः संपुटिताकृतिः ॥ 206
3.m: That this universe is enclosed within her is true, [effected] by the all-pervading Lord; / therefore, in the venerable Triśikāśāstra, power has an enclosed form.

3.s:
saṃvittau bhāti yadviśvaṃ tatrāpi khalu saṃvidā /
tadetattritayaṃ dvandvayogātsaṃghātatāṃ gatam // 207
3.d:
संवित्तौ भाति यद्विश्वं तत्रापि खलु संविदा ।
तदेतत्त्रितयं द्वन्द्वयोगात्संघाततां गतम् ॥ 207
3.m: Even the universe that shines in consciousness does so indeed through consciousness. / Thus, this triad, through the union of the pair, has attained unity.

3.s:
ekameva paraṃ rūpaṃ bhairavasyāhamātmakam /
visargaśaktiryā śaṃbhoḥ setthaṃ sarvatra vartate // 208
3.d:
एकमेव परं रूपं भैरवस्याहमात्मकम् ।
विसर्गशक्तिर्या शंभोः सेत्थं सर्वत्र वर्तते ॥ 208
3.m: The single supreme form of Bhairava consists of 'I' ('aham'); / that power of creative emission belonging to Śambhu operates thus everywhere.

3.s:
tata evasamasto'yamānandarasavibhramaḥ /
tathāhi madhure gīte sparśe vā candanādike // 209
3.d:
तत एवसमस्तोऽयमानन्दरसविभ्रमः ।
तथाहि मधुरे गीते स्पर्शे वा चन्दनादिके ॥ 209
3.m: From that alone proceeds all this play of the savor of bliss; / for instance, in sweet music, or in the touch of sandalwood and the like,

3.s:
mādhyasthyavigame yāsau hṛdaye spandamānatā /
ānandaśaktiḥ saivoktā yataḥ sahṛdayo janaḥ // 210
3.d:
माध्यस्थ्यविगमे यासौ हृदये स्पन्दमानता ।
आनन्दशक्तिः सैवोक्ता यतः सहृदयो जनः ॥ 210
3.m: when indifference falls away, that vibrating movement in the heart / is said to be the power of bliss, whence a person is called sensitive (sahṛdaya).

3.s:
pūrva visṛjyasakalaṃ kartavyaṃ śūnyatānale /
cittaviśrāntisaṃjño'yamāṇavastadanantaram // 211
3.d:
पूर्व विसृज्यसकलं कर्तव्यं शून्यतानले ।
चित्तविश्रान्तिसंज्ञोऽयमाणवस्तदनन्तरम् ॥ 211
3.m: Having first cast out all that is to be done into the fire of the void, / this [state], named rest of the mind, follows thereupon and pertains to the limited individual (āṇava).

3.s:
dṛṣṭaśrutāditadvastupronmukhatvaṃ svasaṃvidi /
cittasaṃbodhanāmoktaḥ śāktollāsabharātmakaḥ // 212
3.d:
दृष्टश्रुतादितद्वस्तुप्रोन्मुखत्वं स्वसंविदि ।
चित्तसंबोधनामोक्तः शाक्तोल्लासभरात्मकः ॥ 212
3.m: The turning towards the object seen, heard, or otherwise perceived within one's own consciousness / is named awakening of the mind, consisting of the full surge of power (śākta).

3.s:
tatronmukhatvatadvastusaṃghaṭṭādvastuno hṛdi /
rūḍheḥ pūrṇatayāveśānmitacittalayācchive // 213
3.d:
तत्रोन्मुखत्वतद्वस्तुसंघट्टाद्वस्तुनो हृदि ।
रूढेः पूर्णतयावेशान्मितचित्तलयाच्छिवे ॥ 213
3.m: There, from the impact between that intentness and the object, from the object / taking root in the heart, from entering fullness, and from the dissolution of the limited mind into Śiva,

3.s:
prāgvadbhaviṣyadaunmukhyasaṃbhāvyamitatālayāt /
cittapralayanāmāsau visargaḥ śāmbhavaḥ paraḥ // 214
3.d:
प्राग्वद्भविष्यदौन्मुख्यसंभाव्यमिततालयात् ।
चित्तप्रलयनामासौ विसर्गः शाम्भवः परः ॥ 214
3.m: because of the dissolution of the limitation to be anticipated as before in future intentness, / this is named dissolution of the mind: the supreme creative emission of Śambhu (śāmbhava).

3.s:
tattvarakṣāvidhāne'to visargatraidhamucyate /
hṛtpadmakośamadhyasthastayoḥ saṃghaṭṭa iṣyate // 215
3.d:
तत्त्वरक्षाविधानेऽतो विसर्गत्रैधमुच्यते ।
हृत्पद्मकोशमध्यस्थस्तयोः संघट्ट इष्यते ॥ 215
3.m: Therefore, in the context of preserving the reality of things, the threefold nature of creative emission is spoken of: / the union of the two situated within the lotus-calyx of the heart is desired.

3.s:
visargo'ntaḥ sa ca proktaścittaviśrāntilakṣaṇaḥ /
dvitīyaḥ sa visargastu cittasaṃbodhalakṣaṇaḥ // 216
3.d:
विसर्गोऽन्तः स च प्रोक्तश्चित्तविश्रान्तिलक्षणः ।
द्वितीयः स विसर्गस्तु चित्तसंबोधलक्षणः ॥ 216
3.m: And that creative emission within is taught to have the characteristic of rest of the mind; / the second creative emission, however, has the characteristic of awakening of the mind.

3.s:
ekībhūtaṃ vibhātyatra jagadetaccarācaram /
grāhyagrāhakabhedo vai kiṃcidatreṣyate yadā // 217
3.d:
एकीभूतं विभात्यत्र जगदेतच्चराचरम् ।
ग्राह्यग्राहकभेदो वै किंचिदत्रेष्यते यदा ॥ 217
3.m: Here, this world of moving and unmoving things shines unified. / Indeed, when some differentiation of object and subject is admitted here,

3.s:
tadāsau sakalaḥ prokto niṣkalaḥ śivayogataḥ /
grāhyagrāhakavicchittisaṃpūrṇagrahaṇātmakaḥ // 218
3.d:
तदासौ सकलः प्रोक्तो निष्कलः शिवयोगतः ।
ग्राह्यग्राहकविच्छित्तिसंपूर्णग्रहणात्मकः ॥ 218
3.m: then it is proclaimed composite (sakala); it is non-composite (niṣkala) through union with Śiva, / consisting in complete apprehension through the severance of object and subject.

3.s:
tṛtīyaḥ sa visargastu cittapralayalakṣaṇaḥ /
ekībhāvātmakaḥ sūkṣmo vijñānātmātmanirvṛtaḥ // 219
3.d:
तृतीयः स विसर्गस्तु चित्तप्रलयलक्षणः ।
एकीभावात्मकः सूक्ष्मो विज्ञानात्मात्मनिर्वृतः ॥ 219
3.m: The third creative emission, however, has the characteristic of dissolution of the mind: / consisting in oneness, subtle, composed of pure consciousness, resting in the Self.

3.s:
nirūpito'yamarthaḥ śrīsiddhayogīśvarīmate /
sātra kuṇḍalinī bījaṃ jīvabhūtā cidātmikā // 220
3.d:
निरूपितोऽयमर्थः श्रीसिद्धयोगीश्वरीमते ।
सात्र कुण्डलिनी बीजं जीवभूता चिदात्मिका ॥ 220
3.m: This matter is set forth in the venerable Siddhayogīśvarīmata: / here, the Kuṇḍalinī is the seed, the life-principle consisting of consciousness.

3.s:
tajjaṃ dhruvecchonmeṣākhyaṃ trikaṃ varṇāstataḥ punaḥ /
ā ityavarṇādityādiyāvadvaisargikī kalā // 221
3.d:
तज्जं ध्रुवेच्छोन्मेषाख्यं त्रिकं वर्णास्ततः पुनः ।
आ इत्यवर्णादित्यादियावद्वैसर्गिकी कला ॥ 221
3.m: Born from her is the triad named Dhruva ('a'), Icchā ('i'), and Unmeṣa ('u'); from that, again, the phonemes: / beginning from 'ā' without phonemes, and so on, up to the emissive energy (visarga).

3.s:
kakārādisakārāntā visargātpañcadhā sa ca /
bahiścāntaśca hṛdaye nāde'tha parame pade // 222
3.d:
ककारादिसकारान्ता विसर्गात्पञ्चधा स च ।
बहिश्चान्तश्च हृदये नादेऽथ परमे पदे ॥ 222
3.m: Beginning with 'ka' and ending with 'sa', and arising from the creative emission, it is fivefold: / outside, inside, in the heart, in sound (nāda), and then in the supreme state.

3.s:
bindurātmani mūrdhāntaṃ hṛdayādvyāpako hi saḥ /
ādimāntyavihīnāstu mantrāḥ syuḥ śaradabhravat // 223
3.d:
बिन्दुरात्मनि मूर्धान्तं हृदयाद्व्यापको हि सः ।
आदिमान्त्यविहीनास्तु मन्त्राः स्युः शरदभ्रवत् ॥ 223
3.m: The point (bindu) is in the Self, pervading indeed from the heart up to the head; / but mantras devoid of the first ('a') and the last ('ha') are like autumn clouds [yielding no rain].

3.s:
gurorlakṣaṇametāvadādimāntyaṃ ca vedayet /
pūjyaḥ so'hamiva jñānī bhairavo devatātmakaḥ // 224
3.d:
गुरोर्लक्षणमेतावदादिमान्त्यं च वेदयेत् ।
पूज्यः सोऽहमिव ज्ञानी भैरवो देवतात्मकः ॥ 224
3.m: The definition of a guru is just this: he should make known the first and the last. / Such a knower is to be revered like myself, being Bhairava, having the nature of the deity.

3.s:
ślokagāthādi yatkiṃcidādimāntyayutaṃ tataḥ /
tasmādvidaṃstathā sarvaṃ mantratvenaiva paśyati // 225
3.d:
श्लोकगाथादि यत्किंचिदादिमान्त्ययुतं ततः ।
तस्माद्विदंस्तथा सर्वं मन्त्रत्वेनैव पश्यति ॥ 225
3.m: Whatever verse, meter, and the like exists is therefore endowed with the first and the last; / therefore, knowing thus, one sees everything only as mantra.

3.s:
visargaśaktirviśvasya kāraṇaṃ ca nirūpitā /
aitareyākhyavedānte parameśena vistarāt // 226
3.d:
विसर्गशक्तिर्विश्वस्य कारणं च निरूपिता ।
ऐतरेयाख्यवेदान्ते परमेशेन विस्तरात् ॥ 226
3.m: And the power of creative emission is explained as the cause of the universe / at length by the Supreme Lord in the Vedānta known as Aitareya.

3.s:
yallohitaṃ tadagniryadvīryaṃ sūryenduvigraham /
a iti brahma paramaṃ tatsaṃghaṭṭodayātmakam // 227
3.d:
यल्लोहितं तदग्निर्यद्वीर्यं सूर्येन्दुविग्रहम् ।
अ इति ब्रह्म परमं तत्संघट्टोदयात्मकम् ॥ 227
3.m: That which is red is fire; that which is virility has the form of sun and moon; / 'a' is the supreme Brahman, whose nature is the arising of their collision.

3.s:
tasyāpi ca paraṃ vīrya pañcabhūtakalātmakam /
bhogyatvenānnarūpaṃ ca śabdasparśarasātmakam // 228
3.d:
तस्यापि च परं वीर्य पञ्चभूतकलात्मकम् ।
भोग्यत्वेनान्नरूपं च शब्दस्पर्शरसात्मकम् ॥ 228
3.m: And the supreme virility of that consists of the energies of the five elements; / as the object of enjoyment it has the form of food, consisting of sound, touch, and taste.

3.s:
śabdo'pi madhuro yasmādvīryopacayakārakaḥ /
taddhi vīryaṃ paraṃ śuddhaṃ visisṛkṣātmakaṃ matam // 229
3.d:
शब्दोऽपि मधुरो यस्माद्वीर्योपचयकारकः ।
तद्धि वीर्यं परं शुद्धं विसिसृक्षात्मकं मतम् ॥ 229
3.m: For even sweet sound causes the accumulation of virility; / that supreme, pure virility is indeed considered to consist of the desire to emit.

3.s:
tadbalaṃ ca tadojaśca te prāṇāḥ sā ca kāntatā /
tasmādvīryātprajāstāśca vīrya karmasu kathyate // 230
3.d:
तद्बलं च तदोजश्च ते प्राणाः सा च कान्तता ।
तस्माद्वीर्यात्प्रजास्ताश्च वीर्य कर्मसु कथ्यते ॥ 230
3.m: That is strength, that is vigor, those are the vital breaths, and that is loveliness; / from that virility offspring are born, and that virility is declared in sacrificial acts.

3.s:
yajñādikeṣu tadvṛṣṭau sauṣadhīṣvatha tāḥ punaḥ /
vīrye tacca prajāsvevaṃ visarge viśvarūpatā // 231
3.d:
यज्ञादिकेषु तद्वृष्टौ सौषधीष्वथ ताः पुनः ।
वीर्ये तच्च प्रजास्वेवं विसर्गे विश्वरूपता ॥ 231
3.m: In sacrifices and the like, that [becomes] rain; that in turn [becomes] plants; / they become virility, and that [becomes] offspring; thus, the form of the universe exists in creative emission.

3.s:
śabdarāśiḥ sa evokto mātṛkā sāca kīrtitā /
kṣobhyakṣobhakatāveśānmālinīṃ tāṃ pracakṣate // 232
3.d:
शब्दराशिः स एवोक्तो मातृका साच कीर्तिता ।
क्षोभ्यक्षोभकतावेशान्मालिनीं तां प्रचक्षते ॥ 232
3.m: That very [power] is called the totality of sounds (śabdarāśi), and she is celebrated as Mātṛkā; / because of the penetration of the agitated and the agitator, they call her Mālinī.

3.s:
bījayonisamāpattivisargodayasundarā /
mālinī hi parā śaktirnirṇītā viśvarūpiṇī // 233
3.d:
बीजयोनिसमापत्तिविसर्गोदयसुन्दरा ।
मालिनी हि परा शक्तिर्निर्णीता विश्वरूपिणी ॥ 233
3.m: Lovely with the emergence of the creative emission from the union of seed and womb, / Mālinī is indeed determined to be the supreme power whose form is the universe.

3.s:
eṣā vastuta ekaiva parā kālasya karṣiṇī /
śaktimadbhedayogena yāmalatvaṃ prapadyate // 234
3.d:
एषा वस्तुत एकैव परा कालस्य कर्षिणी ।
शक्तिमद्भेदयोगेन यामलत्वं प्रपद्यते ॥ 234
3.m: She is in reality singular, the supreme drawer of time; / through connection with the division of the possessor of power, she assumes dyadic nature.

3.s:
tasya pratyavamarśo yaḥ paripūrṇo'hamātmakaḥ /
sa svātmani svatantratvādvibhāgamavabhāsayet // 235
3.d:
तस्य प्रत्यवमर्शो यः परिपूर्णोऽहमात्मकः ।
स स्वात्मनि स्वतन्त्रत्वाद्विभागमवभासयेत् ॥ 235
3.m: His reflective awareness, which is full and consists of 'I', / displays division within Himself through His absolute autonomy.

3.s:
vibhāgābhāsane cāsya tridhā vapurudāhṛtam /
paśyantī madhyamā sthūlā vaikharītyabhiśabditam // 236
3.d:
विभागाभासने चास्य त्रिधा वपुरुदाहृतम् ।
पश्यन्ती मध्यमा स्थूला वैखरीत्यभिशब्दितम् ॥ 236
3.m: And in the manifestation of division, His body is declared to be threefold: / designated as the visionary (paśyantī), the intermediate (madhyamā), and the gross (vaikharī).

3.s:
tāsāmapi tridhā rūpaṃ sthūlasūkṣmaparatvataḥ /
tatra yā svarasandarbhasubhagā nādarūpiṇī // 237
3.d:
तासामपि त्रिधा रूपं स्थूलसूक्ष्मपरत्वतः ।
तत्र या स्वरसन्दर्भसुभगा नादरूपिणी ॥ 237
3.m: Their form too is threefold, through gross, subtle, and supreme states; / among them, that which is charming with the arrangement of musical notes, having the form of sound (nāda),

3.s:
sā sthūlā khalu paśyantī varṇādyapravibhāgataḥ /
avibhāgaikarūpatvaṃ mādhuryaṃ śaktirucyate // 238
3.d:
सा स्थूला खलु पश्यन्ती वर्णाद्यप्रविभागतः ।
अविभागैकरूपत्वं माधुर्यं शक्तिरुच्यते ॥ 238
3.m: is indeed gross paśyantī, because of the absence of differentiation of phonemes and the like; / sweet charm (mādhurya) is the sole condition of non-differentiation, and is called power.

3.s:
sthānavāyvādigharṣotthā sphuṭataiva ca pāruṣī /
tadasyāṃ nādarūpāyāṃ saṃvitsavidhavṛttitaḥ // 239
3.d:
स्थानवाय्वादिघर्षोत्था स्फुटतैव च पारुषी ।
तदस्यां नादरूपायां संवित्सविधवृत्तितः ॥ 239
3.m: Distinctness arising from the friction of places of articulation, breath, and the like is harshness (pāruṣī). / Therefore, in this [paśyantī] which has the form of sound, because consciousness functions in close proximity,

3.s:
sājātyāntarma[ttama] yībhūtirjhagityevopalabhyate /
yeṣāṃ na tanmayībhūtiste dehādinimajjanam // 240
3.d:
साजात्यान्तर्म[त्तम] यीभूतिर्झगित्येवोपलभ्यते ।
येषां न तन्मयीभूतिस्ते देहादिनिमज्जनम् ॥ 240
3.m: the absorption consisting of identity of genus within is perceived immediately. / Those who do not experience that absorption, who are ignorant of the immersion of body and the like,

3.s:
avidanto magnasaṃvinmānāstvahṛdayā iti /
yattucarmāvanaddhādi kiṃcittatraiṣa yo dhvaniḥ // 241
3.d:
अविदन्तो मग्नसंविन्मानास्त्वहृदया इति ।
यत्तुचर्मावनद्धादि किंचित्तत्रैष यो ध्वनिः ॥ 241
3.m: whose measure of consciousness is submerged, are without heart. / But whatever sound exists there on a drum or the like covered with hide,

3.s:
sa sphuṭāsphuṭarūpatvānmadhyamā sthūlarūpiṇī /
madhyāyāścāvibhāgāṃśasadbhāva iti raktatā // 242
3.d:
स स्फुटास्फुटरूपत्वान्मध्यमा स्थूलरूपिणी ।
मध्यायाश्चाविभागांशसद्भाव इति रक्तता ॥ 242
3.m: that is intermediate (madhyamā) having a gross form, because of its indistinct-distinct nature; / and because an aspect of non-differentiation exists in madhyamā, there is delight.

3.s:
avibhāgasvaramayī yatra syāttatsurañjakam /
avibhāgo hi nirvṛtyai dṛśyatāṃ tālapāṭhataḥ // 243
3.d:
अविभागस्वरमयी यत्र स्यात्तत्सुरञ्जकम् ।
अविभागो हि निर्वृत्यै दृश्यतां तालपाठतः ॥ 243
3.m: Where it consists of non-differentiated musical sound, that brings delight; / for non-differentiation leads to bliss: let it be seen from the recitation of rhythm.

3.s:
kilāvyaktadhvanau tasminvādane parituṣyati /
yā tu sphuṭānāṃ varṇānāmutpattau kāraṇaṃ bhavet // 244
3.d:
किलाव्यक्तध्वनौ तस्मिन्वादने परितुष्यति ।
या तु स्फुटानां वर्णानामुत्पत्तौ कारणं भवेत् ॥ 244
3.m: Indeed, one is completely satisfied in that playing of instruments with indistinct sound. / That, however, which is the cause in the arising of distinct phonemes,

3.s:
sā sthūlā vaikharī yasyāḥ kāryaṃ vākyādi bhūyasā /
asminsthūlatraye yattadanusandhānamādivat // 245
3.d:
सा स्थूला वैखरी यस्याः कार्यं वाक्यादि भूयसा ।
अस्मिन्स्थूलत्रये यत्तदनुसन्धानमादिवत् ॥ 245
3.m: is gross vaikharī, whose effect is predominantly sentences and the like. / In this triad of gross forms, that synthesis which is, as before,

3.s:
pṛthakpṛthaktattritayaṃ sūkṣmamityabhiśabdyate /
ṣaḍjaṃ karomi madhuraṃ vādayāmi bruve vacaḥ // 246
3.d:
पृथक्पृथक्तत्त्रितयं सूक्ष्ममित्यभिशब्द्यते ।
षड्जं करोमि मधुरं वादयामि ब्रुवे वचः ॥ 246
3.m: distinctly threefold, is called subtle: / 'I produce the note ṣaḍja,' 'I play sweetly,' 'I speak words'—

3.s:
pṛthagevānusandhānatrayaṃ saṃvedyate kila /
etasyāpi trayasyādyaṃ yadrupamanupādhimat // 247
3.d:
पृथगेवानुसन्धानत्रयं संवेद्यते किल ।
एतस्यापि त्रयस्याद्यं यद्रुपमनुपाधिमत् ॥ 247
3.m: the triad of syntheses is indeed experienced distinctly. / That primary form of this triad which is free of limiting conditions

3.s:
tatparaṃ tritayaṃ tatra śivaḥ paracidātmakaḥ /
vibhāgābhāsanāyāṃ ca mukhyāstisro'tra śaktayaḥ // 248
3.d:
तत्परं त्रितयं तत्र शिवः परचिदात्मकः ।
विभागाभासनायां च मुख्यास्तिस्रोऽत्र शक्तयः ॥ 248
3.m: is the supreme triad; therein, Śiva consists of supreme consciousness. / And in the manifestation of division, three powers are primary here:

3.s:
anuttarā parecchā ca parāparatayā sthitā /
unmeṣaśaktirjñānākhyā tvapareti nigadyate // 249
3.d:
अनुत्तरा परेच्छा च परापरतया स्थिता ।
उन्मेषशक्तिर्ज्ञानाख्या त्वपरेति निगद्यते ॥ 249
3.m: the unexcelled (anuttarā) is supreme; will (icchā) stands as both supreme and non-supreme; / the power of unfoldment (unmeṣaśakti), named knowledge, is declared to be non-supreme.

3.s:
kṣobharūpātpunastāsāmuktāḥ ṣaṭ saṃvido'malāḥ /
āsāmeva samāveśātkriyāśaktitayoditāt // 250
3.d:
क्षोभरूपात्पुनस्तासामुक्ताः षट् संविदोऽमलाः ।
आसामेव समावेशात्क्रियाशक्तितयोदितात् ॥ 250
3.m:
From the state of agitation among them, again, six immaculate states of consciousness are declared.
Through the very immersion in these, arisen in the form of the power of action,

3.s:
saṃvido dvādaśa proktā yāsu sarvaṃ samāpyate /
etāvaddevadevasya mukhyaṃ tacchakticakrakam // 251
3.d:
संविदो द्वादश प्रोक्ता यासु सर्वं समाप्यते ।
एतावद्देवदेवस्य मुख्यं तच्छक्तिचक्रकम् ॥ 251
3.m:
twelve states of consciousness are proclaimed, in which everything is culminated.
Such is the primary circle of powers of the God of gods.

3.s:
etāvatā devadevaḥ pūrṇaśaktiḥ sa bhairavaḥ /
parāmarśātmakatvena visargākṣepayogataḥ // 252
3.d:
एतावता देवदेवः पूर्णशक्तिः स भैरवः ।
परामर्शात्मकत्वेन विसर्गाक्षेपयोगतः ॥ 252
3.m:
By virtue of this much, the God of gods, that Bhairava, possesses full power,
possessing the nature of reflective awareness, through connection with the projection of creative emission.

3.s:
iyattākalanājjñānāttāḥ proktāḥ kālikāḥ kvacit /
śrīsāraśāstre cāpyuktaṃ madhya ekākṣarāṃ parām // 253
3.d:
इयत्ताकलनाज्ज्ञानात्ताः प्रोक्ताः कालिकाः क्वचित् ।
श्रीसारशास्त्रे चाप्युक्तं मध्य एकाक्षरां पराम् ॥ 253
3.m:
Because of reckoning finite measures, [and] through knowledge, they are elsewhere called the Kālikās.
And in the venerable Sāraśāstra it is also said: in the center, the supreme [goddess] of one syllable,

3.s:
pūjayedbhairavātmākhyāṃ yoginīdvādaśāvṛtām /
